- `createAttackClock` (function): function createAttackClock(config: AttackClockConfig, initial?: AttackClockState): AttackClock — Attack-wave timing for an RTS opponent: nothing before `firstAt`, then a wave launches when the army reaches `minArmy + growPerWave × waves launched`, or after `maxWait` seconds with whatever army exists. Waves are spaced by `minGap`.
- `createBuildPlanner` (function): function createBuildPlanner(config: BuildPlanConfig, options: BuildPlannerOptions = {}): BuildPlanner — An RTS economy planner: follows `config.steps` in order, inserting the tech path for any unmet requirement, then sustains workers and an army `composition`, building supply ahead of a block. The {@link DifficultyProfile} sets how often it decides (`reactionSeconds` × `intervalPerReaction`), how often a composition pick is worse than the best (`decisionNoise`), and whether it saves for unaffordable wants. Returns a decision per call; the game executes it.

A prerequisite in progress is skipped in favour of another missing one, so "make 4 knights" builds the stables and the smithy side by side. Cycle-safe.

## @jgengine/core/ai/decisionGraph

- `Blackboard` (type): type Blackboard = Record<string, BlackboardValue> — Named facts available to conditions, utilities, and actions.
- `BlackboardValue` (type): type BlackboardValue = number | boolean | string — Scalar values stored in a decision graph blackboard.
- `DecisionAbort` (type): type DecisionAbort<Context = unknown> = ( action: string, ctx: Context, params: Record<string, BlackboardValue> | undefined, blackboard: Blackboard, ) => void — Called when an action that was running last tick is not reached this tick, so it can release what it holds.
- `DecisionAction` (type): type DecisionAction<Context = unknown> = ( ctx: Context, params: Record<string, BlackboardValue> | undefined, blackboard: Blackboard, ) => DecisionStatus — Callback implementation for an action node.
- `DecisionGraph` (type): type DecisionGraph = DecisionNode — Root node for a serializable AI decision graph.
- `DecisionGraphOptions` (interface): interface DecisionGraphOptions<Context = unknown> — Optional hooks and injected randomness for {@link createDecisionGraphRuntime}.
- `DecisionGraphRuntime` (interface): interface DecisionGraphRuntime<Context = unknown> — Stateful evaluator for a serializable decision graph.
- `DecisionGraphSnapshot` (interface): interface DecisionGraphSnapshot — Serializable state retained by an active decision graph. Fields besides `runningPath` are absent in older saves.
- `DecisionNode` (type): type DecisionNode = | { kind: "selector"; children: DecisionNode[]; memory?: boolean } | { kind: "sequence"; children: DecisionNode[]; memory?: boolean } | { kind: "condition"; key: string; op: DecisionOperator; value: BlackboardValue } | { kind: "action"; action: string; params?: Record<string, Bla… — Serializable decision node. - `selector` runs children in order until one does not fail; `sequence` until one does not finish. With `memory`, a composite whose child was running last tick resumes at that child instead of re-checking earlier ones. - `condition` compares a blackboard key; `action` calls a registered action. - `utility` runs the option with the highest weighted blackboard score. - `invert` swaps `done` and `failed`; `cooldown` fails for `seconds` after its child finishes; `wait` stays running for `seconds`; `random` picks a child by `weights` from the runtime's `rng` and keeps it while it runs.
- `DecisionNodeMemory` (interface): interface DecisionNodeMemory — Progress of a memory composite, `random` choice, or `wait` timer, keyed by node id (depth-first order).
- `DecisionOperator` (type): type DecisionOperator = "=" | "==" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" | "eq" | "ne" | "lt" | "lte" | "gt" | "gte" — Comparison operators supported by decision conditions.
- `DecisionStatus` (type): type DecisionStatus = "running" | "done" | "failed" — Outcome reported when a decision graph evaluates.
- `createDecisionGraphRuntime` (function): function createDecisionGraphRuntime<Context = unknown>(graph: DecisionGraph, actions: Record<string, DecisionAction<Context>>, options: DecisionGraphOptions<Context> = {}): DecisionGraphRuntime<Context> — Creates a deterministic runtime for a serializable decision graph.

## @jgengine/core/ai/difficulty

- `DIFFICULTY_TIERS` (const): const DIFFICULTY_TIERS: Readonly<Record<DifficultyTier, DifficultyProfile>> — The canonical easy/standard/expert profiles. Frozen — use {@link difficultyProfile} to derive a tweaked copy instead of mutating.
- `DifficultyProfile` (interface): interface DifficultyProfile — Serializable decision-quality data. All fields are plain numbers so a profile can live in a save, an encounter definition, or a per-entity spawn record.
- `DifficultyTier` (type): type DifficultyTier = "easy" | "standard" | "expert" — Difficulty is decision *quality*, owned in one place: a serializable {@link DifficultyProfile} describing how fast, how accurately, and how far ahead an agent decides, plus appliers at the universal decision seams every opponent shares — reacting to new information, choosing among scored options, executing with error, spending abilities, and planning ahead. The same profile tunes an RTS grunt, a street enemy, a boss's special-ability discipline, or a turn-based lookahead player; the game supplies the domain (candidates, scores, moves) and this module degrades or sharpens the choice. Three canonical tiers ({@link DIFFICULTY_TIERS}) cover "kinda dumb / smart / super smart"; per-game overrides stay data.
- `LookaheadDomain` (interface): interface LookaheadDomain<S, M> — The game-owned decision domain {@link planLookahead} searches. States and moves are caller types; the planner never inspects them.
- `ReactionGateState` (interface): interface ReactionGateState<T> — Serializable reaction-gate state: the value the agent is currently acting on plus the newer value it has noticed but not yet committed to. `T` should be serializable (ids, positions as tuples) if the gate lives in saved state.
- `ScoredOption` (interface): interface ScoredOption<T> — One candidate with a caller-computed score; higher is better.
- `advanceReactionGate` (function): function advanceReactionGate<T>(state: ReactionGateState<T>, dt: number, desired: T, profile: DifficultyProfile): T — Advance one reaction step and return the value to act on. `desired` is what a perfect agent would act on this frame (current best target, latest known player position); the gate holds the previously committed value until `desired` has been stable for `profile.reactionSeconds`, restarting the delay whenever `desired` changes again (compared with `Object.is`). Feed the returned value — not `desired` — into pursuit/aim/ability logic. Mutates `state` in place; allocation-free.
- `createReactionGate` (function): function createReactionGate<T>(initial: T): ReactionGateState<T> — A fresh gate already committed to `initial`.
- `difficultyProfile` (function): function difficultyProfile(tier: DifficultyTier, overrides?: Partial<DifficultyProfile>): DifficultyProfile — A fresh profile from a canonical tier with optional per-game overrides — e.g. an "easy" boss that still reacts fast: `difficultyProfile("easy", { reactionSeconds: 0.2 })`.
- `executionError` (function): function executionError(profile: DifficultyProfile, rng: () => number, scale = 1): number — Symmetric execution error in `[-scale * executionJitter, +scale * executionJitter]` — add it to a yaw, a lead time, a throw power, or a release timestamp. `scale` maps the unitless jitter onto the caller's units (e.g. pass max miss radians).
- `pickScored` (function): function pickScored<T>(options: readonly ScoredOption<T>[], profile: DifficultyProfile, rng: () => number): T | null — Choose from a scored option list at the profile's quality: with probability `profile.decisionNoise` the pick is uniform over all options (the "wrong target / bad move" mistake), otherwise it is the best score (first wins ties). Works over any decision the game can score — acquisition candidates, ability choices, retreat routes, chess moves. Returns `null` for an empty list. Allocation-free scan; one rng draw plus one more on a noisy pick.
- `planLookahead` (function): function planLookahead<S, M>(root: S, domain: LookaheadDomain<S, M>, profile: DifficultyProfile, rng: () => number): M | null — Pick the agent's next move by bounded lookahead: a depth-limited negamax (or single-perspective sequence search when `adversarial: false`) over the caller's {@link LookaheadDomain}, exploring at most `profile.planWidth` moves per ply to `profile.planDepth` plies, with the final root choice run through {@link pickScored} so `decisionNoise` still injects tier-appropriate blunders. Depth `1` is greedy — an easy profile literally cannot see the fork coming; an expert profile finds multi-ply tactics. Work is bounded by `planWidth ** planDepth` domain calls; run it at decision cadence (turns, ability windows, order re-evaluation), not per frame.
- `shouldUseAbility` (function): function shouldUseAbility(opportunity: number, profile: DifficultyProfile, rng: () => number): boolean — Should the agent spend an ability now? `opportunity` is the caller-scored quality of this moment in `0..1` (targets clumped for the AoE, player mid-animation, burn phase). The perceived opportunity is fuzzed by `decisionNoise` and compared against `abilityDiscipline`: an easy profile (low discipline, high noise) wastes cooldowns on weak moments and sometimes sits on a perfect window; an expert profile fires exactly on strong windows. One rng draw when noisy.

## @jgengine/core/ai/director/storyteller

- `StoryBeat` (interface): interface StoryBeat<R = unknown> — One incident the storyteller chose, with the points it spent.
- `StoryIncident` (interface): interface StoryIncident<R = unknown> — The storyteller: what happens to a colony, a household or a crew between the player's own decisions. Threat points build with play time (and with whatever the game says makes it a richer target), and every gap an incident is drawn from the ones the points can afford, so early days get small trouble and boons while later days can afford the big ones. A threat that spends a lot buys extra quiet afterwards. The game owns what an incident does; this owns when and which.

- `StorytellerConfig` (interface): interface StorytellerConfig<R = unknown> — Pacing: how fast points build, how far apart incidents are and how picks lean.

- `StorytellerView` (interface): interface StorytellerView — The storyteller as a HUD or probe reads it.
- `createStoryteller` (function): function createStoryteller<R = unknown>(config: StorytellerConfig<R>): Storyteller<R> — Build a storyteller that paces incidents by threat points.

## @jgengine/core/ai/driver

- `DrivePathPoint` (type): type DrivePathPoint = readonly [number, number] — A 2D polyline point (`[x, z]`), structurally compatible with authored road path centerlines.
- `DriverGoal` (interface): interface DriverGoal — Where the driver is trying to go this step.
- `DriverPose` (interface): interface DriverPose — A difficulty-aware driver brain: pose + goal in, the shared {@link AxisInput} (`throttle`/`brake`/`steer`/`handbrake`) out, ready for `tickDrivableVehicle` — the chase/traffic steering loop every game with AI cars hand-rolls as `steer = error * k, throttle = 1`. A {@link DifficultyProfile} decides how *well* it drives: reaction time trails the target, corners shed speed instead of orbiting at full throttle, obstacles are noticed late on low tiers, the wheel wobbles by `executionJitter`, and a stuck car backs out with counter-steer after grinding for a tier-scaled while. State is one small serializable object; randomness is injected; every step is allocation-light scalar math. The caller owns the sim, collision, and all spatial queries — this module never scans the world.
- `DriverState` (interface): interface DriverState — Serializable per-driver state advanced in place by {@link driveStep}.
- `DriverStep` (interface): interface DriverStep extends AxisInput — {@link driveStep}'s result: the axis sample to feed the vehicle sim, plus arrival.
- `DriverTuning` (interface): interface DriverTuning — Vehicle-feel numbers the game supplies; everything has a sensible default except `maxSpeed`.
- `PaceBand` (interface): interface PaceBand — Catch-up pacing for one car in a field: the gap it tries to hold to a reference car (a rival, the player, a convoy lead) and how its pace bends when it drifts off that gap. Past `margin` by `tolerance` it sheds up to `ease` of its pace; short of it by `tolerance` it gains up to `push`; inside that tolerance it leaves the car alone. The push never outdrives `DriverTuning.maxSpeed`, so a band changes how hard a car tries, never what it is built to do.
- `createDriverState` (function): function createDriverState(targetX = 0, targetZ = 0): DriverState — Fresh driver state committed to an initial target (usually the spawn-time goal or the spawn position itself).
- `driveStep` (function): function driveStep(state: DriverState, dt: number, pose: DriverPose, goal: DriverGoal, profile: DifficultyProfile, tuning: DriverTuning, rng: () => number, obstacleAhead: number | null = null): DriverStep — Advance one driving step, mutating `state`, and return the {@link AxisInput} to feed the vehicle sim. `obstacleAhead` is the caller-measured distance to the nearest blocker in the driving corridor this step (`null`/omitted when clear) — the driver perceives it late by `speed * reactionSeconds`, so easy tiers brake at the last moment and expert tiers with proper margin. The steering target is a delay-line over the goal — resampled every `reactionSeconds`, so it trails a moving goal by up to that long, which is what makes an easy chaser visibly cut toward where the target *was*. A {@link PaceBand} on the goal eases a car ahead of its margin and pushes one behind it, bounded by the car's own top speed. When throttle produces no motion for a tier-scaled while the driver reverses out with counter-steer (brake past standstill — the shared sim's reverse).
- `paceBandFactor` (function): function paceBandFactor(band: PaceBand, gap: number): number — The pace multiplier a {@link PaceBand} asks for at `gap`: `1` inside the tolerance, `1 - ease * scale` fully ahead of it, `1 + push * scale` fully behind it, ramped linearly across `easeAt` / `pushAt` in between. Pure scalar math, so a band is deterministic and costs no allocation per step; the result never goes negative.
- `pathTargetAhead` (function): function pathTargetAhead(path: readonly DrivePathPoint[], x: number, z: number, lookahead: number, loop = false): DrivePathPoint | null — The pure-pursuit target for street/route following: the point `lookahead` meters further along the polyline from wherever the vehicle currently projects onto it. Feed the result to {@link driveStep} as the goal each tick and the driver follows the road; `loop` wraps a circuit (traffic block, race lap) instead of pinning at the final point. Returns `null` for a degenerate path. Give sharper tiers a longer `lookahead` to cut corners cleanly and duller tiers a short one so they steer segment-to-segment.

## @jgengine/core/ai/interestScheduler

- `InterestCensus` (interface): interface InterestCensus — Aggregate counts of active vs dormant gates — the metric the issue asks a scheduler to expose.
- `InterestCensusAccumulator` (interface): interface InterestCensusAccumulator — A running census accumulator; call `record` inside the caller's existing tick loop (no extra pass).
- `InterestGateInput` (interface): interface InterestGateInput — Per-tick input the caller supplies to a gate.
- `InterestGateState` (interface): interface InterestGateState — Per-agent serializable gate state. Round-trip the whole object; never read fields to drive logic.
- `InterestGateStep` (interface): interface InterestGateStep — Per-tick output that tells the caller whether to run expensive work.
- `InterestSchedulerConfig` (interface): interface InterestSchedulerConfig — Static configuration shared by every gate of one behavior class.
- `InterestState` (type): type InterestState = "active" | "dormant" — Interest scheduling: the scale primitive that lets far-away agents sleep instead of running acquisition and pathing every frame. A per-agent gate decides — from proximity to the nearest interest source plus explicit wake signals — whether this tick does expensive work, at what cadence, with hysteresis so it never thrashes at the boundary and deterministic staggering so a thousand siblings do not all wake on the same frame. State is a plain serializable object; the caller drives it from a bounded spatial query, never a full-world scan.
- `InterestTier` (interface): interface InterestTier — A distance-keyed cadence tier: nearer agents tick faster, farther-but-awake agents tick slower.

Sleeping skips the expensive work (`active: false`) while the gate's timers keep advancing, so state is preserved; a `wake` signal or crossing `wakeRadius` flips it back to active and fires an immediate tick.

## @jgengine/core/ai/policeResponse

- `DEFAULT_POLICE_TIERS` (const): const DEFAULT_POLICE_TIERS: readonly PoliceTier[] — The starting tier table: patrol until heat arrives, then investigate, pursue and finally cordon.
- `DEFAULT_POLICE_TUNING` (const): const DEFAULT_POLICE_TUNING: PoliceTuning — The starting policy: linear decay, a six-second escape and a search area that grows at 2 m/s.
- `PoliceLaneHit` (interface): interface PoliceLaneHit — A lane near a world point: its id, the arc of the nearest point on it, and how far away that is.
- `PoliceResponse` (interface): interface PoliceResponse — Stateful wanted/pursuit API with retuning and save/restore support.
- `PoliceResponseConfig` (interface): interface PoliceResponseConfig extends Partial<PoliceTuning> — Everything {@link createPoliceResponse} needs: the witness seam, the roster and the caller's policy.
- `PoliceResponseKind` (type): type PoliceResponseKind = "patrol" | "investigate" | "pursue" | "roadblock" — How police answer the current heat tier — watching the streets up to cordoning them.
- `PoliceResponseState` (interface): interface PoliceResponseState — Serializable response state — the heat curve, the sight timer, the anchor and the counters.
- `PoliceRoadblockSite` (interface): interface PoliceRoadblockSite — A roadblock site on a lane, resolved from authored road data.
- `PoliceRoads` (interface): interface PoliceRoads — Road data the response reads: nearby lanes for the search area, authored sites for roadblocks.
- `PoliceRoadsOptions` (interface): interface PoliceRoadsOptions — How the document reader recognizes authored road content.
- `PoliceSearchArea` (interface): interface PoliceSearchArea — Where the search is, as the last sighting places it.
- `PoliceSighting` (interface): interface PoliceSighting — One remembered sighting of the suspect, as the perception service reports it — `PerceptionMemory` from `sensor/perception` satisfies this shape.
- `PoliceStats` (interface): interface PoliceStats — Counters a devtools probe, a HUD or a test reads.
- `PoliceStep` (interface): interface PoliceStep — One tick's answer: the heat, the tier, the search area, the cordon and the escape.
- `PoliceTickContext` (interface): interface PoliceTickContext — Per-tick world facts {@link PoliceResponse.tick} needs but cannot derive itself.
- `PoliceTier` (interface): interface PoliceTier — One response tier: the heat it begins at, what it puts on the street, and how wide it searches.
- `PoliceTuning` (interface): interface PoliceTuning — The serializable policy of a response: the tier table, the heat curve and the search shape.
- `PoliceWitness` (interface): interface PoliceWitness — The witness seam: perception memory, queried by observer id. Pass `createPerception` (`sensor/perception`) straight in — a crime is witnessed when an observer still holds the suspect in view, so there is no second sight path to keep in step.
- `createPoliceResponse` (function): function createPoliceResponse(config: PoliceResponseConfig): PoliceResponse — The wanted level a crime sandbox needs, over the shared heat curve: a crime raises heat only while a witness holds the suspect in view, the heat bleeds on a stated linear curve once the suspect has been out of every witness's sight for `escapeSeconds`, the tier table decides what police do (patrol → investigate → pursue → roadblock), the search area sits where the suspect was last seen and grows while the trail is cold, and a roadblock tier cordons it with authored sites off the lane graph. Heat, tiers and curves are caller policy; witness facts come from `sensor/perception` memory (`sourceId`/`sourceTick` kept), so there is no second sight path.
- `policeRoadsFromLaneGraph` (function): function policeRoadsFromLaneGraph(graph: LaneGraph, markers: readonly EditorMarker[] = [], options: PoliceRoadsOptions = {}): PoliceRoads — Read the police road data out of an authored lane graph: `traffic_roadblock` markers become cordon sites projected onto the lane they block, and lanes are indexed so `lanesNear` answers from the local cells rather than a scan of every lane. With no roadblock markers authored, the graph's intersections are the sites, so a cordon still sits where streets meet. Built once; the index is rebuildable from the document, so it is never serialized.

## @jgengine/core/ai/populationDirector

- `PopulationCensus` (type): type PopulationCensus = Record<string, Record<string, number>> — Live census of alive counts keyed `region -> species -> count`, used to reconcile the director to reality.
- `PopulationDirector` (interface): interface PopulationDirector — Stateful ambient population manager for one world; drive it with `tick` and lifecycle notifications.
- `PopulationDirectorConfig` (interface): interface PopulationDirectorConfig — Full ambient-population configuration: per-region species budgets plus global refill limits and PRNG seed.
- `PopulationDirectorState` (interface): interface PopulationDirectorState — Opaque, JSON-serializable persistence for a {@link PopulationDirector}. Round-trip it through `snapshot`/`hydrate`; never read or mutate the fields directly.
- `PopulationRegionConfig` (interface): interface PopulationRegionConfig — Ambient population budget for a single region: its species ceilings, refill timing, and spawn geometry.
- `PopulationSpawnRequest` (interface): interface PopulationSpawnRequest — A single ambient spawn the game should realise, refilling a region toward its species caps.
- `PopulationSpeciesEntry` (interface): interface PopulationSpeciesEntry — One species that ambiently populates a region: how heavily it is favoured and its alive ceiling.
- `PopulationTickContext` (interface): interface PopulationTickContext — Per-call spawn-point selection hook, letting a game apply bias (distance from players, etc.) at tick time.
- `createPopulationDirector` (function): function createPopulationDirector(config: PopulationDirectorConfig): PopulationDirector — Ambient open-world population director. Holds a target creature population per region and refills it over time, distinct from wave/horde spawning: instead of a budget draining down a wave, each region has per-species caps and a timed respawn queue. Removing a creature frees a slot; after a respawn delay `tick` emits weighted spawn requests (bounded per tick) that refill toward the caps without ever exceeding them. Species are chosen through a persisted, serializable {@link RandomSeed} cursor, so the same seed and the same lifecycle events always yield the same requests. Regions are independent, spawn points are optional, and the whole state round-trips through `snapshot`/`hydrate`.

## @jgengine/core/ai/pursuit

- `CooldownMode` (type): type CooldownMode = "always" | "inRange" — When the attack cooldown ticks down. - `"always"` (default): every step, like a wall-clock weapon timer that keeps counting during the chase, so the entity can swing the instant it reaches its target. - `"inRange"`: only while within `stopDistance`, so the timer freezes during the chase and the full interval is paid out after each contact.
- `PursuitAction` (type): type PursuitAction = | "leash" /** Out of range — advance toward the target. */ | "pursue" /** In range and the cooldown is ready — perform the attack, then {@link armPursuit}. */ | "attack" /** In range but the cooldown has not elapsed — hold (face the target, idle, etc.). */ | "wait" /** No engage… — Composable pursuit/aggro step: the "I have a target — now chase it, stop at reach, hit it on a cooldown, and break off if led too far from home" loop that melee mobs, RTS units, and stationary turrets all re-implement by hand. This owns exactly that state machine and the per-entity attack cooldown; target *selection* stays separate (see {@link ./targetAcquisition}), and every side effect — move, attack, break off — is performed by the caller in response to the returned action.
- `PursuitState` (interface): interface PursuitState — Per-entity cooldown state owned by the primitive. One serializable number; no methods.
- `advancePursuit` (function): function advancePursuit(state: PursuitState, dt: number, targetDistance: number | null, stopDistance: number, cooldownMode: CooldownMode = "always", homeDistance = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY, leashRange = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY): PursuitAction — Advance one pursuit step for a single entity, mutating `state.attackCooldown`, and return the action the caller should perform. All spatial input is scalar and measured this frame:
- `armPursuit` (function): function armPursuit(state: PursuitState, intervalSeconds: number): void — Set the cooldown after an attack fires (clamped at `0`). Call on the step that returned `"attack"`.
- `createPursuitState` (function): function createPursuitState(attackCooldown = 0): PursuitState — A fresh pursuit state, ready to attack immediately (`attackCooldown` at `0`).

## @jgengine/core/ai/rvo

- `RvoAgentSpec` (interface): interface RvoAgentSpec — One agent's circular footprint and top speed; positions and velocities live in the crowd.
- `RvoAgentView` (interface): interface RvoAgentView — One agent's live kinematics, as the crowd exposes them.
- `RvoCrowd` (interface): interface RvoCrowd — Many circular agents steering around each other. `setPreferredVelocity` states where each agent wants to go; `step` turns that into reciprocal collision-free velocities and integrates them. Deterministic: agents are visited in slot order, neighbours in grid and slot order, and head-on ties break on slot index rather than chance.
- `RvoCrowdOptions` (interface): interface RvoCrowdOptions extends Partial<RvoTunables> — Options for {@link createRvoCrowd}.
- `RvoSnapshot` (interface): interface RvoSnapshot — Serializable crowd state: tuning plus every agent's position, velocity and footprint.
- `RvoTunables` (interface): interface RvoTunables — Serializable avoidance tuning, retunable in play through {@link RvoCrowd.retune}.
- `createRvoCrowd` (function): function createRvoCrowd(options: RvoCrowdOptions = {}): RvoCrowd — Reciprocal velocity obstacle avoidance over circular agents. Each nearby pair contributes one or two half-plane constraints on the agent's velocity, and a small linear program picks the velocity closest to the preferred one that satisfies them all. The neighbour search is a uniform grid capped at `maxNeighbors`, so a tick costs the same for 50 agents and 5,000.

## @jgengine/core/ai/targetAcquisition

- `AcquisitionEnvelope` (type): type AcquisitionEnvelope = number | ((selfId: string, candidateId: string) => number) — Composable target acquisition: the "which enemy do I lock onto?" decision split into the independent concerns every aggro system tangles together — a bounded candidate provider, an eligibility filter, a per-pair acquisition envelope (dynamic range), a perception/LOS gate, scoring, deterministic tie-break, and retention hysteresis. This owns *policy*; threat, brains, and movement stay separate. Feed `candidates` a spatial-index query, never a full-world scan.
- `AcquisitionPolicy` (interface): interface AcquisitionPolicy — A fully composed acquisition policy. Every concern is an independent, injectable seam; the only required pieces are the bounded `candidates` provider and the `distance` metric. Omit the rest to fall back to the thin default — a static/unbounded range, everything eligible and perceptible, nearest-wins scoring, id tie-break, no hysteresis — which matches a plain proximity aggro radius.
- `AcquisitionResult` (interface): interface AcquisitionResult — Outcome of one acquisition pass.
- `AcquisitionRetention` (interface): interface AcquisitionRetention — Retention hysteresis that keeps an already-held target from flickering under churn.
- `TargetAcquirer` (interface): interface TargetAcquirer — A stateful acquirer that holds the current target across passes — sugar over {@link acquireTarget}.
- `acquireTarget` (function): function acquireTarget(policy: AcquisitionPolicy, selfId: string, held: string | null = null): AcquisitionResult — Run one acquisition pass and pick the best target under `policy`. Pass the currently `held` target so retention hysteresis (`switchMargin`, `dropRangeScale`) can keep the lock stable; pass `null` for a cold acquire. Pure and allocation-light — the caller owns the held-target state.
- `createTargetAcquirer` (function): function createTargetAcquirer(policy: AcquisitionPolicy): TargetAcquirer — Wrap an {@link AcquisitionPolicy} in a small object that remembers the held target between passes, so callers get retention hysteresis for free without threading the previous target by hand. The only state is the held id (a string) — trivially serializable; round-trip it with {@link TargetAcquirer.hold}.

## @jgengine/core/ai/temperament

- `TemperamentConfig` (interface): interface TemperamentConfig — One species' temperament: its kind plus the ranges and thresholds that tune it.
- `TemperamentInput` (interface): interface TemperamentInput — One decision's inputs: where the creature is, its den, its health, and its perception memory.
- `TemperamentIntent` (interface): interface TemperamentIntent — The decision: a mode, who it is about, and the point to move toward (null to hold position).
- `TemperamentKind` (type): type TemperamentKind = "passive" | "territorial" | "predator" — How a creature treats what it senses. `passive` keeps its distance, `territorial` defends an area and ignores what stays outside it, `predator` hunts what it senses and closes to strike.
- `TemperamentLight` (type): type TemperamentLight = "attracted" | "averse" | "none" — What light does to a creature: draws it toward a lit target, drives it away, or nothing.
- `TemperamentMode` (type): type TemperamentMode = "idle" | "flee" | "investigate" | "stalk" | "attack" | "guard" | "return" — What a creature is doing about what it senses.
- `decideTemperament` (function): function decideTemperament(config: TemperamentConfig, input: TemperamentInput): TemperamentIntent — Decide what one creature does about what its perception remembers, from its temperament alone: a passive grazer flees what comes near, a territorial guard attacks only intruders inside its area and returns home when they leave, a predator charges what it saw and follows a smell or a noise to where it came from. Light bends all three: an attracted creature walks toward a lit target it senses, an averse one backs away from it. Pure and deterministic, so a game calls it per creature per tick and moves the creature toward `goal` with its own navigation.

- `createAnimGraphRuntime` (function): function createAnimGraphRuntime(initial: AnimGraph, options: AnimGraphRuntimeOptions = {}): AnimGraphRuntime — Headless animation state machine and blend evaluator. It owns every clip's playback time and weight, so the renderer only seeks and weights actions on a mixer, and headless hosts, replays, and tests advance the same graph without three.js. Transitions are data (parameter comparisons and consumed triggers), layers can be masked or additive, and events fire by clip time, including across loop wraps.
- `parseAnimGraph` (function): function parseAnimGraph(value: unknown): AnimGraph | undefined — Validates untrusted JSON (a saved scene document, a network payload) as an {@link AnimGraph}. Malformed states, transitions to unknown states, and bad conditions are dropped; a layer whose entry state is missing is dropped; the result is `undefined` when no layer survives.
- `stateClipWeights` (function): function stateClipWeights(state: AnimState, params: AnimParams): Record<string, number> — Static clip weights of a state at `params`, before any crossfade.
- `validateAnimGraph` (function): function validateAnimGraph(value: unknown): AnimGraphValidation — Validate an authored graph without dropping broken combat states or weakening transition conditions. Known malformed fields and dangling references reject the whole graph with relative repair locations; valid data, including authored object/array order, is returned unchanged. Unknown extension fields are retained. Clip availability belongs to the imported-rig diagnostics. Use {@link parseAnimGraph} when permissive repair is intentional.

- `BoneTextureInput` (interface): interface BoneTextureInput — Inputs for {@link planBoneTexture}.
- `BoneTextureLayout` (interface): interface BoneTextureLayout — Where every bone matrix of every baked frame lives in a vertex-animation texture: one row per frame, four RGBA texels (matrix columns) per bone. Plain data, so a baked crowd can be cached, shipped or checked in a test without a renderer.

This is the CPU mirror of the crowd shader's lookup.

The local player's own model never glances. `maxCameraDistance` skips the work for characters too far away to read.

## @jgengine/core/anim/crowdRegistry.draw

- `CharacterCrowdRegistry` (class): class CharacterCrowdRegistry — The characters the crowd layer is currently drawing, written by their entity markers each frame. It holds poses rather than React state: 71 pedestrians writing matrices must not re-render the world, and the crowd batch reads the same entries back to fill its instance buffers.
- `crowdEligible` (function): function crowdEligible(model: ModelConfig | undefined): model is ModelConfig — Whether a model can leave its own rig for the GPU crowd path: one whose drawn result a batch can reproduce. A rigged, clip-played, plain model qualifies, and so does a model with no animation at all (a static crowd character) — it has no playback to lose. A model that needs per-entity materials, wind, hidden nodes, IK, attachments or a part composition keeps its own rig.
- `crowdKindOf` (function): function crowdKindOf(model: ModelConfig): string — The identity a character model shares with every other model the GPU crowd can draw: rig url, height normalization and material tint. Two entity kinds with the same key can share one instanced draw; a different tint or height needs its own.

## @jgengine/core/anim/footPlacement

- `FootGroundSample` (interface): interface FootGroundSample — One foot's animated ankle height and the ground found under it, both in world units.
- `FootPlacement` (interface): interface FootPlacement — Result of {@link placeFeet}: where each ankle should go and how far the pelvis drops.
- `FootPlacementInput` (interface): interface FootPlacementInput — Inputs for {@link placeFeet}. All heights are world units.
- `LegChain` (interface): interface LegChain — Thigh → shin → foot bone names for one leg.
- `RigBone` (interface): interface RigBone — A bone as {@link inferLegChains} sees it: its name and its parent's name.
- `inferLegChains` (function): function inferLegChains(bones: readonly RigBone[]): LegChain[] — Finds leg chains on a humanoid rig by bone name: a thigh-like bone (`UpLeg`, `UpperLeg`, `Thigh`) with its first child and grandchild as shin and foot. Control, IK-target and twist bones are skipped. Returns chains in rig order; an empty array means the rig has no recognizable legs.
- `placeFeet` (function): function placeFeet(input: FootPlacementInput, out?: FootPlacement): FootPlacement — Resolves foot placement for a rig whose clips were authored on flat ground at its origin. Each foot keeps its animated lift and moves by its ground's height above or below the origin, the sole is never left under the ground, and the pelvis drops by the deepest reach so both legs stay within length. Pure and allocation-light; the renderer applies the targets with {@link solveTwoBone}.

## @jgengine/core/anim/humanoidActionClips.draw

- `HUMANOID_SOCKETS` (const): const HUMANOID_SOCKETS: readonly SkeletonSlot[] — Standard slots that get a socket; each socket node takes its slot's name.
- `addHumanoidSockets` (function): function addHumanoidSockets(instance: THREE.Object3D, source: THREE.Object3D, clips: readonly THREE.AnimationClip[]): void — Adds a socket node under each hand of a humanoid rig instance, named `hand.r` and `hand.l` (no loaded bone takes those names: the loader strips the dot). A socket sits at its joint in the character's own frame as it stands in its idle pose (metres, +Y up, +Z forward), whatever the rig's bone axes and units, so an attachment's offset and rotation mean the same on every humanoid rig. A rig the standard cannot map gets none. `source` is the loaded scene `instance` was cloned from.
- `buildHumanoidActionClips` (function): function buildHumanoidActionClips(scene: THREE.Object3D, clips: readonly THREE.AnimationClip[], names: readonly HumanoidActionName[] = HUMANOID_ACTION_NAMES): THREE.AnimationClip[] — The authored humanoid actions as this rig's own clips, posed from its idle clip, or `[]` when the skeleton standard cannot map the rig as a full humanoid body. A clip the rig already ships under the same name is left out, so its own take wins.
- `firstPersonArms` (function): function firstPersonArms(instance: THREE.Object3D, source: THREE.Object3D, clips: readonly THREE.AnimationClip[]): (() => void) | null — Raises a first-person body's arms into view, on top of whatever the animation posed this frame: the returned function turns each arm by {@link HUMANOID_FIRST_PERSON_CARRY}, fading out while an action swings the arms far from their idle pose, so a punch or a tool swing plays as authored. Call it after the animation writes the pose; a frame the animation skipped is left alone. `null` when the rig is not a mapped humanoid.
- `withHumanoidActionClips` (function): function withHumanoidActionClips(scene: THREE.Object3D, clips: readonly THREE.AnimationClip[]): THREE.AnimationClip[] — A rig's clips plus the authored humanoid actions it lacks, built once per loaded model and shared by every instance of it. The source scene only supplies bone names and base transforms.

## @jgengine/core/anim/humanoidActions

- `HUMANOID_ACTIONS` (const): const HUMANOID_ACTIONS: Readonly<Record<HumanoidActionName, HumanoidActionClip>> — The authored action set. Jump is held while airborne, Swim and Tread loop while swimming, and the rest are one-shots that return to locomotion (Death holds its last key).
- `HUMANOID_ACTION_NAMES` (const): const HUMANOID_ACTION_NAMES: readonly ["Jump", "Swim", "Tread", "Punch", "Swing", "Gather", "Hurt", "Death"] — Engine-authored action clips for any humanoid rig mapped onto the skeleton standard: the motions a mocap library rarely ships beside its walk cycles (jump, swim, punch, tool swing, gather, hurt, death). Each clip is plain pose data on standard slots, so one authoring serves every rig the standard maps; `buildHumanoidActionClips` (`humanoidActionClips.draw`) turns it into the rig's own clips at load time.
- `HUMANOID_ACTION_SLOTS` (const): const HUMANOID_ACTION_SLOTS: readonly SkeletonSlot[] — Every slot an authored clip may turn.
- `HUMANOID_FIRST_PERSON_CARRY` (const): const HUMANOID_FIRST_PERSON_CARRY: Readonly<Pose> — The arms a first-person body carries in front of it, hands low in view at chest height, so the fists and whatever they hold stay on screen while standing or walking. Turns from the idle pose.
- `HumanoidActionClip` (interface): interface HumanoidActionClip — One authored action: its keys and whether it loops.
- `HumanoidActionName` (type): type HumanoidActionName = (typeof HUMANOID_ACTION_NAMES)[number] — One authored action's clip name.
- `HumanoidAnimationInput` (interface): interface HumanoidAnimationInput — Locomotion clip names and speeds a humanoid body's own library supplies.
- `HumanoidPoseKey` (interface): interface HumanoidPoseKey — One key of an authored clip: the slots it turns and how far the hips move, in model metres.
- `HumanoidRotation` (type): type HumanoidRotation = readonly [x: number, y: number, z: number] — Degrees about the model's X, Y and Z axes, composed in that order.
- `humanoidAnimation` (function): function humanoidAnimation(input: HumanoidAnimationInput): ModelAnimationConfig — The animation config for a humanoid body: its own idle, walk and run, plus the authored actions as the airborne, swimming and one-shot states. One-shot keys: `attack` (Punch), `swing`, `gather`, and the reserved `hit` (Hurt) and `death`, which fire from combat on their own; play the others with `ctx.game.playEntityAnimation(id, "swing")`.

## @jgengine/core/anim/ikSolver

- `Quat` (type): type Quat = readonly [number, number, number, number] — A quaternion in `(x, y, z, w)` order.
- `TwoBoneInput` (interface): interface TwoBoneInput — Inputs for {@link solveTwoBone}.
- `TwoBoneOutput` (interface): interface TwoBoneOutput — Reused output buffers filled by {@link solveTwoBone}.

- `multiplyQuaternions` (function): function multiplyQuaternions(a: Quat, b: Quat): Quat — The product of two quaternions (`a` applied after `b`), both as `[x, y, z, w]`.

The root remains fixed, and unreachable targets are clamped to the chain's maximum reach.

- `LOCOMOTION_FACING_PARAM` (const): const LOCOMOTION_FACING_PARAM: "facing" — Dot of the character's facing with its motion direction: `1` running forward, `-1` running backwards. A custom mover feeds it under `ANIM_PARAMS_KEY`.

- `LOCOMOTION_SPEED_PARAM` (const): const LOCOMOTION_SPEED_PARAM: "speed" — The parameter name the shell feeds with the entity's smoothed ground speed.
- `LOCOMOTION_STATE` (const): const LOCOMOTION_STATE: "locomotion" — State id of the forward idle/walk/run blend.
- `LOCOMOTION_STRAFE_STATE` (const): const LOCOMOTION_STRAFE_STATE: "strafe" — State id of the lateral strafe blend.
- `LOCOMOTION_SWIMMING_PARAM` (const): const LOCOMOTION_SWIMMING_PARAM: "swimming" — Swimming, as the shared player motor reports it; a custom mover feeds it under `ANIM_PARAMS_KEY`.
- `LOCOMOTION_SWIM_STATE` (const): const LOCOMOTION_SWIM_STATE: "swim" — State id of the swim blend.
- `LOCOMOTION_TURN_RATE_PARAM` (const): const LOCOMOTION_TURN_RATE_PARAM: "turnRate" — Signed yaw rate in radians/sec; a custom mover feeds it under `ANIM_PARAMS_KEY`.
- `LOCOMOTION_TURN_STATE` (const): const LOCOMOTION_TURN_STATE: "turn" — State id of the on-the-spot turn blend.
- `LOCOMOTION_VERTICAL_SPEED_PARAM` (const): const LOCOMOTION_VERTICAL_SPEED_PARAM: "verticalSpeed" — Resolved vertical velocity from the shared player motor, in world units/sec.
- `LocomotionGraphInput` (interface): interface LocomotionGraphInput — Inputs for {@link locomotionGraph}: the locomotion clip names and the one-shot table a rig config already carries.
- `animGraphFromConfig` (function): function animGraphFromConfig(config: ModelAnimationConfig): AnimGraph | undefined — The graph a model animation config plays: its `graph`, or the {@link locomotionGraph} its `states` and `oneShots` describe, retaining every one-shot variant. `undefined` for a single-clip config or incomplete locomotion roles. Idle must name a clip; an absent or blank walk role holds that idle clip at walking speeds until configured. The shell plays this and the editor inspects it, so both see the same graph.
- `locomotionGraph` (function): function locomotionGraph(input: LocomotionGraphInput): AnimGraph — The engine's default locomotion as an authored graph: a speed-driven blend between idle, walk and run, plus a state per one-shot that plays once and returns (or clamps for `death`). What `useModelAnimation` used to hardcode.

## @jgengine/core/anim/ragdollRig

- `HUMANOID_RAGDOLL_BODIES` (const): const HUMANOID_RAGDOLL_BODIES: Readonly<Partial<Record<SkeletonSlot, RagdollBodyShape>>> — Humanoid body shapes for the standard slots, sized for a roughly 1.8 m character standing on the ground. A rig of another scale multiplies them (see {@link RagdollRigOptions.scale}).
- `RagdollBodyShape` (interface): interface RagdollBodyShape — Half-extents and mass of one standard slot's physics body, in the rig's own world units.
- `RagdollPose` (interface): interface RagdollPose — One standard slot's world pose, sampled at the moment a character is killed. The orientation is the reference the ragdoll's aim rotates from, so every bone keeps the roll it died with.
- `RagdollRigOptions` (interface): interface RagdollRigOptions — Tuning for {@link ragdollConfigFromPoses}.
- `ragdollBoneOrientations` (function): function ragdollBoneOrientations(rest: readonly RagdollPose[], positions: Readonly<Partial<Record<SkeletonSlot, readonly [number, number, number]>>>): Partial<Record<SkeletonSlot, [number, number, number, number]>> — World orientations for a ragdoll's bones from its bodies' current positions: each bone rotates from its rest direction-to-child onto the current one, so the aim follows the joints while every bone keeps the roll it had in the death pose. A bone with no posed child keeps its rest orientation. The physics bodies carry translation only, so this is what gives the ragdoll a skeleton instead of a pile of boxes.
- `ragdollConfigFromPoses` (function): function ragdollConfigFromPoses(map: SkeletonMap, poses: readonly RagdollPose[], options: RagdollRigOptions = {}): RagdollConfig — A jointed ragdoll for a mapped rig from its bones' world poses at the moment of death: one box body per standard slot that has a shape, sized to the character, and one distance link per slot that has its parent present, holding the bones' own separation. The bodies start where the character actually was, so the collapse continues the death pose instead of snapping to a preset.

## @jgengine/core/anim/skeletonStandard

- `BIPED_SCHEME` (const): const BIPED_SCHEME: RigScheme — 3ds Max Biped rigs (`Bip01 Pelvis`, `Bip01 L UpperArm`), which every Microsoft Rocketbox human shares: the engine's realistic default body. Biped has a clavicle and a neck the standard folds into `chest`, and no hand-slot bone, so props attach to `hand.l`/`hand.r`.
- `HUMANOID_BODY_SLOTS` (const): const HUMANOID_BODY_SLOTS: readonly SkeletonSlot[] — Slots a rig needs before the engine poses it as a full humanoid body: limbs, spine and head.
- `KAYKIT_SCHEME` (const): const KAYKIT_SCHEME: RigScheme — The standard itself, as a scheme: a KayKit rig already is the standard, so its own names are the candidates. Both authored (`upperleg.l`) and runtime (`upperlegl`) spellings are accepted.
- `LOWER_BODY_MASK` (const): const LOWER_BODY_MASK: readonly string[] — Layer mask for a lower-body layer on a standard rig.
- `LOWER_BODY_SLOTS` (const): const LOWER_BODY_SLOTS: readonly SkeletonSlot[] — Standard slots a lower-body layer drives: hips, both legs and both feet.
- `MIXAMO_SCHEME` (const): const MIXAMO_SCHEME: RigScheme — Mixamo exports (`mixamorig*` names, or the same names without the prefix). Mixamo has a neck and a shoulder per side, which the standard folds into `chest` and `upperArm`; its toe is `ToeBase`, which is the standard's `toes`. Mixamo's topmost bone is `Hips`, so `root` and `hips` both resolve to it — a rig on this scheme has no bone above the pelvis.
- `QUATERNIUS_ALIEN_SCHEME` (const): const QUATERNIUS_ALIEN_SCHEME: RigScheme — Quaternius sci-fi aliens: a `Root` plus a `Spine_1..Spine_6` chain, a `Neck` and a `Head`. The pack ships no arms and no legs, so those slots stay empty and the alien can only be driven on its spine and head. That is the honest mapping: the pack's own clip set is `Alien_Idle` alone.
- `RIG_SCHEMES` (const): const RIG_SCHEMES: Readonly<Record<string, RigScheme>> — Every scheme the engine ships a mapping for, keyed by {@link RigScheme.id}.
- `RigScheme` (interface): interface RigScheme — A source naming scheme and the bone names on it that fill each standard slot. A slot lists every accepted spelling; matching is case- and punctuation-insensitive, so `mixamorigLeftUpLeg` and `LeftUpLeg` are the same candidate.
- `SKELETON_PARENT` (const): const SKELETON_PARENT: Readonly<Partial<Record<SkeletonSlot, SkeletonSlot>>> — The parent slot of each slot that has one; `root` has none.
- `SKELETON_SLOTS` (const): const SKELETON_SLOTS: readonly SkeletonSlot[] — Every standard slot, in parent-before-child order.
- `SKELETON_STANDARD` (const): const SKELETON_STANDARD: SkeletonStandard — The one humanoid skeleton standard. Bone names are the authored KayKit names; the loaded hierarchy spells them without `.` and `resolveRigNode` accepts either.
- `SkeletonMap` (interface): interface SkeletonMap — The result of mapping a rig's bones onto {@link SKELETON_STANDARD}.
- `SkeletonSlot` (type): type SkeletonSlot = | "root" | "hips" | "spine" | "chest" | "head" | "upperArm.l" | "upperArm.r" | "lowerArm.l" | "lowerArm.r" | "hand.l" | "hand.r" | "handSlot.l" | "handSlot.r" | "upperLeg.l" | "upperLeg.r" | "lowerLeg.l" | "lowerLeg.r" | "foot.l" | "foot.r" | "toes.l" | "toes.r" — The engine's one humanoid skeleton standard, and the path any other CC0 rig takes onto it.
- `SkeletonStandard` (interface): interface SkeletonStandard — A named skeleton standard: its id and the authored bone name for each slot it defines.
- `SlotLength` (interface): interface SlotLength — A standard slot and the rest-pose length of the bone chain that reaches it.
- `UPPER_BODY_MASK` (const): const UPPER_BODY_MASK: readonly string[] — Layer mask for an upper-body action layer (aim, reload, hit reaction) on a standard rig.
- `UPPER_BODY_SLOTS` (const): const UPPER_BODY_SLOTS: readonly SkeletonSlot[] — Standard slots an upper-body action layer drives: spine, chest, head and both arms.
- `detectHumanoidRig` (function): function detectHumanoidRig(bones: readonly string[]): SkeletonMap | null — The scheme that fills the most standard slots on this rig, mapped; `null` when no scheme fills every {@link HUMANOID_BODY_SLOTS} slot, so a quadruped or a partial rig is never posed as a person.
- `mapRigToStandard` (function): function mapRigToStandard(bones: readonly string[], scheme: RigScheme | string = KAYKIT_SCHEME): SkeletonMap — Maps a rig's bone names onto {@link SKELETON_STANDARD} through one {@link RigScheme}. Each slot takes the first candidate that resolves; a candidate list is tried in order, so a scheme can name a preferred bone and fall back. Bones that fill no slot come back in `unmapped`, and slots the rig cannot fill in `missing` — the caller decides whether a partial map is usable.
- `retargetBoneScales` (function): function retargetBoneScales(source: readonly SlotLength[], target: readonly SlotLength[]): Partial<Record<SkeletonSlot, number>> — Per-slot length ratios that stretch a source rig's bone chain onto the standard's proportions, so a retargeted clip moves both rigs the same distance rather than the same angle. Slots with no counterpart on either side are omitted; a source length of zero is skipped instead of dividing.
- `retargetTracks` (function): function retargetTracks(tracks: readonly string[], map: SkeletonMap): (string | null)[] — Renames a clip's tracks from a rig's own bone names onto the standard's, so one authored clip plays on a mapped rig. The emitted node is the **runtime** bone name (see {@link runtimeBoneName}), which is what both the loaded scene graph and the loaded clips spell. A track whose node fills no slot is dropped (`null` in the result) rather than left pointing at a bone the rig does not have; a track whose property is not one of the four three writes is dropped too, since renaming it would not make it resolvable.
- `runtimeBoneName` (function): function runtimeBoneName(authored: string): string — The runtime name GLTFLoader gives an authored bone name: three's `PropertyBinding.sanitizeNodeName` strips `[ ] . : /`, so the authored `upperleg.l` loads as `upperlegl`.
- `standardBoneMask` (function): function standardBoneMask(slots: readonly SkeletonSlot[]): string[] — Bone-name prefixes for a set of standard slots, for an {@link AnimLayer.mask}. A slot on one side contributes its side-less prefix (`upperLeg.l` → `upperleg`), which matches both sides' tracks; an unsided slot contributes its own runtime name. Masking by slot means a rig mapped onto the standard is masked without hand-typing its bone names.

Snaps immediately under reduced motion or a non-finite target.

## @jgengine/core/anim/useEntityRenderCues.draw

- `useEntityRenderCues` (function): function useEntityRenderCues(instanceId: string | undefined, tuning?: RenderCueTuning): MutableRefObject<EntityRenderCues> — Live motion + animation cues for one entity, read from a mutable ref inside your own `useFrame` — no re-render per frame, no diffing the parent group's position, no game-side module map for attack/hit timing. Backs both custom `renderEntity` rigs and a custom first-person viewmodel (#542): call it with `entity.id` / the local player's userId and drive bob/recoil/reload poses from `cuesRef.current` inside the calling component's own `useFrame`.

- `FootIkRig` (interface): interface FootIkRig — Bones resolved once per loaded scene for {@link applyFootIk}.

Ground probes hit terrain and blocking physical objects, never the model's own entity. `groundOffset` is the model-space height its soles rest on (`ModelConfig.y`). `options.quiet` drops the rig diagnostics (the engine's own default IK on a model that never asked for it); `options.maxCameraDistance` skips characters further than that from the camera, fading their correction out.

## @jgengine/core/anim/useModelAnimation.draw

- `GraphPose` (interface): interface GraphPose — A mixer set up to show {@link AnimGraph} output on a rig; see {@link createGraphPose}.
- `ModelAnimationDiagnostic` (interface): interface ModelAnimationDiagnostic — A repairable mismatch between a model animation config and its imported rig.
- `ModelMotionStep` (interface): interface ModelMotionStep — One visual sample's measured motion, used to derive the directional locomotion parameters. `dx`/`dz` are world horizontal displacement since the previous sample, `dyaw` the yaw change in radians and `seconds` the time the sample covers.
- `createGraphPose` (function): function createGraphPose(scene: THREE.Object3D, graph: AnimGraph, clips: THREE.AnimationClip[]): GraphPose — Binds a graph's clips to a rig exactly as `useModelAnimation` does (masked layers get filtered clips, additive layers additive ones) so a host that runs its own `createAnimGraphRuntime`, such as the editor's graph preview, poses the rig from the runtime's output.
- `diagnoseModelAnimation` (function): function diagnoseModelAnimation(scene: THREE.Object3D, animation: ModelAnimationConfig, clips: readonly THREE.AnimationClip[]): readonly ModelAnimationDiagnostic[] — Checks clip mappings, masked layers and root-motion assumptions without starting a mixer.
- `readModelAnimationParams` (function): function readModelAnimationParams(ctx: GameContext, instanceId: string, speed: number, out: Record<string, AnimParamValue>, step?: ModelMotionStep): Record<string, AnimParamValue> — Refreshes a caller-owned graph parameter dictionary from authored extras and known physical movement. Grounded, verticalSpeed and crouched use the shared motor's resolved state when available; custom movers retain their authored values. Speed always uses the supplied measured ground speed. Passing `step` derives the directional parameters from the character's own motion: `direction` is the motion's share along the character's right axis, `facing` its share along the facing axis, and `turnRate` its yaw change per second. Derived values override conflicting authored extras. Does not write game state.
- `useModelAnimation` (function): function useModelAnimation(scene: THREE.Object3D, clips: THREE.AnimationClip[], animationInput: ModelAnimationConfig | "auto" | "none" | undefined, instanceId?: string): void — The engine's model animation driver as a standalone hook — the same mixer `EntityModel` runs, for games that render a cloned scene themselves (custom materials, procedural composition). Handles `"auto"` derivation from the GLB's clip names, speed-driven idle/walk/run crossfades read from the entity's live position when `instanceId` is set, one-shots fired from `entity.animation` / `combat.hitReaction` / `entity.died`, held poses, and the death clamp. With `animation.graph` set, the headless `AnimGraph` runtime owns every clip's time and weight and the mixer only applies them; clip events surface as `animation.event`. Equivalent same-order config data retains playback across rerenders; actual data edits reset it. Entity-bound playback holds while context game time is frozen; unbound previews keep playing.

## @jgengine/core/anim/useRagdoll.draw

- `RagdollOptions` (interface): interface RagdollOptions — What {@link useRagdoll} needs: the rig's bone names, the physics world and what arms it.
- `useRagdoll` (function): function useRagdoll(scene: THREE.Object3D, options: RagdollOptions): void — Turns a rigged character into a physics ragdoll when `active` goes true: the bones' world poses at that moment become box bodies joined by distance links in `world`, and every frame after, each bone's world position and aim come from its body. The physics bodies carry translation only, so each bone is oriented by rotating its death-pose direction-to-child onto the current one, which is what gives the body a skeleton instead of a pile of boxes.

## @jgengine/core/area/areaEffectField

- `AreaEffectEvent` (interface): interface AreaEffectEvent<P> — One membership edge emitted by `step`, `removeSource`, or `clear`.
- `AreaEffectField` (interface): interface AreaEffectField<P> — Runtime handle tracking continuous area membership across ticks.
- `AreaEventKind` (type): type AreaEventKind = "enter" | "refresh" | "leave" — The three membership edges a step can emit.
- `AreaFieldState` (interface): interface AreaFieldState<P> — Serialized field state: source descriptors (minus their transient shape) and per-member refresh phase.
- `AreaLeaveReason` (type): type AreaLeaveReason = "exit" | "source-removed" | "disabled" | "cleared" — Why a `leave` edge fired.
- `AreaMembership` (interface): interface AreaMembership<P> — One active (source, receiver) membership — feed a receiver's list to a stacking policy.
- `AreaShape` (type): type AreaShape = | { readonly kind: "sphere"; readonly center: EntityPosition; readonly radius: number } | { readonly kind: "custom"; /** Bounding-sphere center the caller's broad-phase `candidates` query is built from. */ readonly center: EntityPosition; /** Bounding-sphere radius the caller's broa… — The area a source occupies this tick. `sphere` is first-class; `custom` leaves a seam for authored volumes and other shapes while still exposing a bounding sphere (`center`/`radius`) for the caller's broad-phase candidate query.
- `AreaSourceSpec` (interface): interface AreaSourceSpec<P> — Descriptor for one continuous area source; re-supplied each tick so its shape follows the emitter.
- `AreaStepInput` (interface): interface AreaStepInput — Per-tick inputs the field needs to reconcile membership without scanning the world.
- `createAreaEffectField` (function): function createAreaEffectField<P = unknown>(state?: AreaFieldState<P>): AreaEffectField<P> — Build a continuous area-effect field. Drive it with `setSource` (once per live source per tick, so shapes follow their emitters) and `step` (to reconcile membership and drain enter/refresh/leave edges). Optionally restore prior membership by passing a `serialize()` snapshot; re-`setSource` live shapes before the first `step` after restore, since shapes are transient.

## @jgengine/core/area/stackPolicy

- `AreaStackPolicy` (type): type AreaStackPolicy<P> = (memberships: readonly AreaMembership<P>[]) => AreaMembership<P>[] — Reduce one receiver's overlapping memberships to the subset that applies under a stacking rule.
- `MagnitudeOf` (type): type MagnitudeOf<P> = (membership: AreaMembership<P>) => number — Read a comparable magnitude from a membership (e.g. buff strength, damage per tick).
- `cappedStacks` (function): function cappedStacks<P>(limit: number, magnitudeOf?: MagnitudeOf<P>): AreaStackPolicy<P> — Keep at most `limit` memberships per `stackKey` (the highest-magnitude ones when `magnitudeOf` is given, else the first-seen). Models capped stacks — e.g. a poison that stacks up to 5 times.
- `extremumStack` (function): function extremumStack<P>(magnitudeOf: MagnitudeOf<P>, weakest = false): AreaStackPolicy<P> — Reduce to the single strongest membership overall (`weakest = false` picks the weakest); ties broken by `sourceId`. Use when only the best or worst overlapping source should apply.
- `independentStacks` (function): function independentStacks<P>(): AreaStackPolicy<P> — Every overlapping membership applies independently (no deduplication) — the default for hazards, fields, and lights where two sources genuinely stack.
- `sumMagnitude` (function): function sumMagnitude<P>(memberships: readonly AreaMembership<P>[], magnitudeOf: MagnitudeOf<P>): number — Sum a numeric magnitude across memberships — additive aggregation for a total field strength (total damage per tick, total slow). A terminal reducer, not a filter, so it returns the number.
- `uniqueByStackKey` (function): function uniqueByStackKey<P>(magnitudeOf?: MagnitudeOf<P>): AreaStackPolicy<P> — Keep at most one membership per `stackKey`. With `magnitudeOf` the strongest per key wins (ties broken by `sourceId` for determinism); without it the first-seen per key wins. Use for unique-by-key buffs where reapplying the same aura should not stack.

- `AmbienceWeight` (interface): interface AmbienceWeight — One zone's share of the ambience mix at a listener position, 0..1.
- `AmbienceZoneDef` (interface): interface AmbienceZoneDef — One ambience zone: a sound bed keyed to a volume of the scene.
- `AmbienceZoneShape` (type): type AmbienceZoneShape = | { kind: "sphere"; center: readonly [number, number, number]; radius: number } | { kind: "box"; min: readonly [number, number, number]; max: readonly [number, number, number] } — A world-space volume whose sound bed plays while the listener is inside it.

A wave start has no event of its own, so a game announces it through `notify("wave")` or `attachWaveFeedback`.

- `EventFeedbackState` (interface): interface EventFeedbackState — The cooldown clocks of an {@link EventFeedback}: when each cue last fired (ms, `now` clock) and how many triggers its cooldown folded away.

- `FeedbackScope` (type): type FeedbackScope = "local" | "remote" | "any" — Which side of an event a binding reacts to: the local player's, someone else's, or either.

- `attachEventFeedback` (function): function attachEventFeedback(events: Pick<GameEvents, "on">, feedback: EventFeedback, eventsToBind: readonly FeedbackEventName[] = Object.keys( DEFAULT_FEEDBACK_BINDINGS.reduce<Record<string, true>>((names, binding) => { names[binding.event] = true; return names; }, {}), ) as FeedbackEventName[]): (… — Subscribe the feedback seam to a game's event bus, including `feedback.cue` for moments the game announces itself. Returns the detach function; the mapping and reactions stay override-able through the seam's `retune`.

A wave has no event of its own, so this is the engine-side hookup for tower defense and wave survival games: `attachWaveFeedback(runner, ctx.game.feedback)`. Nothing is polled, the runner's own notification drives it, and one `update` that crosses two waves still fires once - the cue has a cooldown and the next boundary is announced by the next crossing.
