## @jgengine/core/audio/music

- `MusicInstrument` (type): type MusicInstrument = | "strings" | "flute" | "harp" | "horn" | "choir" | "bell" | "timpani" | "bass" | "stacc" | "pad" | "lute" | "dulcimer" | "frameDrum" | "warDrum" | "reed" | "pipe" | "squareLead" | "woodBlock" | "tinyBell" | "piano" | "shaker" | "brassStab" | "cymSwell" | "oboe" — Named synthesised instrument. Each maps to a voice in the shell's instrument library (`@jgengine/core/audio/musicVoices.view`); an unknown name falls back to a plain sine voice so a theme is never silent.
- `MusicTheme` (interface): interface MusicTheme — A through-composed, looping music track. `events` need not be sorted; the director schedules them ahead against a fixed anchor so loops are seamless.
- `NoteEvent` (interface): interface NoteEvent — One scheduled note in a theme, positioned on the loop's quarter-note grid.
- `ScheduledNote` (interface): interface ScheduledNote — A resolved note occurrence: the source note plus its absolute onset in seconds.
- `mtof` (function): function mtof(midi: number): number — Standard equal-temperament MIDI-to-frequency (A4 = 440 Hz at MIDI 69).
- `notesInWindow` (function): function notesInWindow(theme: MusicTheme, anchorSec: number, fromSec: number, toSec: number): ScheduledNote[] — Pure lookahead scheduler: every note occurrence of `theme` whose onset falls in the half-open window `(fromSec, toSec]`, given the theme's loop-zero at `anchorSec`. Handles any number of loop wraps, so a director calls it once per tick with a non-overlapping window and never double-schedules a note.
- `themeLoopSeconds` (function): function themeLoopSeconds(theme: MusicTheme): number — Loop length of a theme in seconds.

## @jgengine/core/audio/musicDirector.view

- `CrossfadeOptions` (interface): interface CrossfadeOptions — Options for a music crossfade.
- `MusicDirector` (class): class MusicDirector — Runs a set of looping {@link MusicTheme}s as crossfadeable layers on one shared Web Audio graph: master → compressor → destination, with a fixed convolution reverb send. `crossfadeTo` swaps the audible theme; a 110ms lookahead scheduler keeps each active layer's notes queued ahead of the clock so loops are seamless.

## @jgengine/core/audio/musicState

- `MusicStateConfig` (interface): interface MusicStateConfig — The tier ladder plus the release margin that keeps a hovering intensity from flapping between tiers.
- `MusicStateInput` (interface): interface MusicStateInput — The current intensity signal and clock reading for one resolve.
- `MusicStateResult` (interface): interface MusicStateResult — Next state, the theme that should be playing, and whether this advance is the one that changed it.
- `MusicStateSnapshot` (interface): interface MusicStateSnapshot — Which tier is playing and when it was entered, on the caller's clock. Serialisable.
- `MusicTier` (interface): interface MusicTier — Hysteretic music-state selector: turns a continuous intensity signal (nearby threat, alert count, chase proximity) into a stable theme id. The engine can already crossfade a soundtrack; this decides *when*, without the flapping a bare threshold produces when one enemy walks in and out of range.
- `createMusicState` (function): function createMusicState(): MusicStateSnapshot — Fresh state with no tier entered, so the first resolve always settles and reports `changed`.
- `resolveMusicState` (function): function resolveMusicState(state: MusicStateSnapshot, input: MusicStateInput, config: MusicStateConfig): MusicStateResult — Pick the theme for the current intensity. Escalation is immediate; de-escalation waits for the tier's `holdMs` and needs the intensity to fall a `release` margin below the tier it is leaving.

## @jgengine/core/audio/musicVoices.view

- `playMusicNote` (function): function playMusicNote(ctx: Ctx, event: NoteEvent, when: number, spb: number, out: GainNode, transpose = 0): void — Play one theme note through its instrument voice into `out` (a per-layer gain node the director wires to master + reverb). `spb` is seconds-per-beat and `transpose` shifts the note in semitones for per-zone key changes. This is the engine's reusable instrument library; unknown instruments fall back to a sine.

## @jgengine/core/audio/occlusion

- `AUDIO_OCCLUSION_DEFAULTS` (const): const AUDIO_OCCLUSION_DEFAULTS: { readonly maxTestsPerTick: 8; readonly intervalMs: 150; readonly attenuation: 0.55; readonly lowpassHz: 1200; readonly maxDistance: 60; } — Defaults for {@link AudioOcclusionConfig}.
- `AudioOcclusionConfig` (interface): interface AudioOcclusionConfig — Geometry occlusion for retained positional loops: a cheap line test between the listener and an emitter behind blocking geometry, bounded so a busy scene can never turn audio into a raycast pass. The shell runs the test against the scene's blockable colliders; the engine applies the resulting attenuation and low-pass to the loop it already owns.
- `ResolvedAudioOcclusionConfig` (interface): interface ResolvedAudioOcclusionConfig — A fully specified occlusion policy, with every unset field replaced by its default.
- `resolveOcclusionConfig` (function): function resolveOcclusionConfig(config: AudioOcclusionConfig | false = {}): ResolvedAudioOcclusionConfig — Fill in the occlusion defaults and clamp each field to a workable range: a finite test budget, a non-negative retest interval and distance cap, and an attenuation in `0..1`.

## @jgengine/core/audio/occlusionRaycast

- `BlockingRaycastSource` (interface): interface BlockingRaycastSource — The narrow slice of the scene a line-of-hearing test needs.
- `sceneLineBlocked` (function): function sceneLineBlocked(source: BlockingRaycastSource, from: Xyz, to: Xyz): boolean — Whether blocking world geometry (objects and wall segments, never creatures or terrain) lies between the listener and an emitter. One scene query per call; the engine owns how often it runs.

## @jgengine/core/audio/radio

- `Radio` (interface): interface Radio — A radio with a running broadcast.
- `RadioBulletin` (interface): interface RadioBulletin — A game event the radio should talk about ("shots fired in Port Carmine").
- `RadioBulletinPolicy` (interface): interface RadioBulletinPolicy — How a station reads bulletins the game reports.
- `RadioCue` (type): type RadioCue = | { kind: "segment"; station: string; segment: RadioSegment; offset: number } /** A line started: speak it. */ | { kind: "line"; station: string; segment: RadioSegment; line: RadioLine } /** The radio went silent (powered off). */ | { kind: "off" } — Something the playback should do now for the station being listened to.
- `RadioDef` (interface): interface RadioDef extends RadioTiming — A whole radio: its dial and how it times speech.
- `RadioLine` (interface): interface RadioLine — A line as scheduled inside a resolved segment.
- `RadioLineDef` (interface): interface RadioLineDef — A spoken line inside a segment. A bare string in a definition is a line in the station's default voice.
- `RadioNowPlaying` (interface): interface RadioNowPlaying — HUD view of a station's programme.
- `RadioSegment` (interface): interface RadioSegment — A segment resolved for air: lengths fixed, lines timed. Plain data, so it snapshots.
- `RadioSegmentDef` (interface): interface RadioSegmentDef — An authored programme segment: a song (a music theme id), a DJ link, an ad, a talk bit or a news item.
- `RadioSegmentKind` (type): type RadioSegmentKind = "song" | "dj" | "ad" | "talk" | "news" | "jingle" | "bulletin" — One kind of programme segment. `bulletin` is reserved for segments the radio builds from reported game events.
- `RadioSnapshot` (interface): interface RadioSnapshot — Serializable radio state: every station's place in its programme, the queues, cooldowns and the dial.
- `RadioStationDef` (interface): interface RadioStationDef — One station on the dial.
- `RadioStationKind` (type): type RadioStationKind = "music" | "talk" | "news" — What a station mostly broadcasts; a HUD can style or group stations by it.
- `RadioTiming` (interface): interface RadioTiming — Timing knobs a game may retune during play.
- `createRadio` (function): function createRadio(def: RadioDef): Radio — A pure, serializable radio: stations with their own running order of songs, DJ links, ads, talk bits and news, all broadcasting on one clock whether or not anyone listens, so tuning back lands mid-programme. Game events reported with {@link Radio.report} queue bulletins with priority, per-topic cooldown and expiry; a high enough priority breaks into the current segment. `tick` returns cues (segment on air, line started, off) that a playback seam turns into music and speech; nothing here touches audio, so it runs headless and in tests.
- `estimateSpeechSeconds` (function): function estimateSpeechSeconds(text: string, wordsPerSecond = 2.6): number — Seconds a line takes to say at `wordsPerSecond`, with a short floor so one-word stings still register.

## @jgengine/core/audio/radioPlayback

- `RadioAudioSink` (interface): interface RadioAudioSink — The audio surface radio playback drives; `ctx.game.audio` satisfies it.
- `RadioPlayback` (interface): interface RadioPlayback — Turns a {@link Radio}'s cues into music and speech.
- `RadioPlaybackSnapshot` (interface): interface RadioPlaybackSnapshot — Serializable playback state from {@link RadioPlayback.snapshot}.
- `RadioVoice` (interface): interface RadioVoice — How one radio voice id should sound when spoken by the browser's speech synthesiser.
- `SpeakOptions` (interface): interface SpeakOptions extends RadioVoice — Spoken-line options carried to the shell's speech channel.
- `createRadioPlayback` (function): function createRadioPlayback(radio: Radio, sink: RadioAudioSink, options: { voices?: Readonly<Record<string, RadioVoice>> } = {}): RadioPlayback — Plays a radio through a game's audio seam with one call per tick: songs and beds as music themes started at the station's offset (so a retune lands mid-song), lines through speech in the voice mapped from their voice id. Pausing stops music and speech but not the radio's state; resuming re-cues the current segment. Speech is best effort: with no system voice the shell drops it and the HUD's now-playing line still carries the words.

## @jgengine/core/audio/reverb

- `AudioReverbConfig` (interface): interface AudioReverbConfig — World reverb for positioned sounds. Authored zones win; outside them the shell listens for walls and a ceiling around the listener (`auto`, default on) and picks `room`, `hall` or `outdoor`.
- `EnclosureSample` (interface): interface EnclosureSample — What the listener's surroundings look like: the ceiling height and how far each wall ray ran.
- `ReverbPreset` (type): type ReverbPreset = "none" | "outdoor" | "room" | "hall" | "cave" — How a space rings. `outdoor` is a short, faint tail; `room` a tight one; `hall` long and wide; `cave` long, dark and wet. `none` is dry.
- `ReverbZoneDef` (type): type ReverbZoneDef = | { id: string; preset: ReverbPreset; center: readonly [number, number, number]; radius: number } | { id: string; preset: ReverbPreset; min: readonly [number, number, number]; max: readonly [number, number, number] } — A world region that rings a set way while the listener is inside it.
- `enclosurePreset` (function): function enclosurePreset(sample: EnclosureSample): ReverbPreset — Pick a preset from the space around the listener. A roof with walls on most sides is a room, or a hall when they are far; a roof alone (an awning, an overpass) is a room; open sky is outdoor.
- `reverbZoneAt` (function): function reverbZoneAt(zones: readonly ReverbZoneDef[], x: number, y: number, z: number): ReverbZoneDef | null — The zone holding a point, or null. Spheres and boxes; the first listed wins where they overlap.

## @jgengine/core/audio/reverbRack.view

- `EnclosureRaycastSource` (interface): interface EnclosureRaycastSource — The narrow slice of the scene an enclosure test needs.

## @jgengine/core/audio/speech.view

- `SpeechChannel` (interface): interface SpeechChannel — Text-to-speech on the browser's synthesiser with stable per-key voice choice and a silent fallback.
- `SpeechStats` (interface): interface SpeechStats — What the speech channel has done, for a debug readout or capture probe.
- `SpeechSynthesisLike` (interface): interface SpeechSynthesisLike — The slice of `window.speechSynthesis` the channel drives; inject a fake in tests.
- `SpeechUtteranceLike` (interface): interface SpeechUtteranceLike — The slice of `SpeechSynthesisUtterance` the channel writes.
- `SpeechVoiceLike` (interface): interface SpeechVoiceLike — The slice of `SpeechSynthesisVoice` the channel reads.
- `createSpeechChannel` (function): function createSpeechChannel(backend: { synth: SpeechSynthesisLike; Utterance: UtteranceCtor } | null = resolveSynth()): SpeechChannel — Speech for radio DJs, callers and announcers. Lines queue on the synthesiser; `stop` cancels the queue. Without a synthesiser or a single voice (headless Chrome, tests, some Linux browsers) a line is counted as dropped and nothing throws, so the game's on-screen text is the fallback.
- `pickSpeechVoice` (function): function pickSpeechVoice(voices: readonly SpeechVoiceLike[], options: SpeakOptions = {}): SpeechVoiceLike | null — Pick a system voice: a name hint wins, else the voice key hashes to a stable choice among the language's voices.

## @jgengine/core/audio/stepCadence

- `StepCadenceConfig` (interface): interface StepCadenceConfig — Distance-driven footstep cadence. Pure state-in/state-out: feed it how far a mover travelled this frame and it tells you how many steps landed, so foley stays locked to ground distance instead of a wall-clock timer that desyncs when speed changes.
- `StepCadenceInput` (interface): interface StepCadenceInput — What the mover did this advance: ground distance covered, whether feet are planting, and the stride multiplier.
- `StepCadenceResult` (interface): interface StepCadenceResult — Outcome of one advance: the next state plus how many steps landed and which foot led.
- `StepCadenceState` (interface): interface StepCadenceState — Cadence bookkeeping between advances — banked distance, last moving state, and the step count whose parity is the foot.
- `advanceStepCadence` (function): function advanceStepCadence(state: StepCadenceState, input: StepCadenceInput, config: StepCadenceConfig): StepCadenceResult — Bank this advance's distance and report the steps it completed. Pure — same state and input always give the same result, so footstep timing is testable headless and replays identically.
- `createStepCadenceState` (function): function createStepCadenceState(): StepCadenceState — Fresh cadence state for a mover that is standing still.

## @jgengine/core/audio/synth

- `NoiseVoice` (interface): interface NoiseVoice — A filtered white-noise burst — impacts, whooshes, breath, crackle. Realised from a shared 1s noise buffer at a randomised playback rate and start offset, decaying exponentially to silence at `duration * decay`.
- `SynthFilter` (type): type SynthFilter = "lowpass" | "highpass" | "bandpass" — Biquad filter shape a noise voice is coloured through.
- `SynthPatch` (interface): interface SynthPatch — A procedural sound cue: a set of voices triggered together, each with its own `delay`, summed into one one-shot. Pure serialisable data — the shell realises it on Web Audio, so the same catalog runs headless in tests with no `AudioContext`.
- `SynthVoice` (type): type SynthVoice = ToneVoice | NoiseVoice — One layered voice of a synth cue.
- `SynthWave` (type): type SynthWave = "sine" | "square" | "sawtooth" | "triangle" — Oscillator waveform available to a pitched synth voice.
- `ToneVoice` (interface): interface ToneVoice — A pitched oscillator voice: a 12ms linear attack to `gain`, then an exponential decay to silence across `duration`, with an optional exponential pitch slide from `freq` to `slideTo`.
- `patchDuration` (function): function patchDuration(patch: SynthPatch): number — Total wall-clock length of a patch in seconds — the latest voice end across all voices.

## @jgengine/core/audio/synthEngine.view

- `SynthPlayback` (interface): interface SynthPlayback — Scheduled procedural sources; stopping releases their source/filter/envelope graph.
- `createNoiseBuffer` (function): function createNoiseBuffer(ctx: BaseAudioContext): AudioBuffer — Build the shared 1-second mono white-noise buffer every noise voice samples from.
- `realizeSynthPatch` (function): function realizeSynthPatch(ctx: BaseAudioContext, out: AudioNode, noiseBuf: AudioBuffer, patch: SynthPatch): SynthPlayback — Realise a procedural cue on Web Audio: every voice is scheduled at `ctx.currentTime + delay` into `out`, summed into one one-shot. `noiseBuf` is the shared buffer from {@link createNoiseBuffer}.

- `VoiceAllocation` (type): type VoiceAllocation = { ok: false } | { ok: true; voiceId: number; stolen: number[] } — Admission result; stop every stolen source before starting the admitted voice.
- `VoiceAllocator` (interface): interface VoiceAllocator — Bounded reservations with higher-priority protection and oldest-first ties.
- `VoiceAllocatorConfig` (interface): interface VoiceAllocatorConfig — Playback budget. Zero disables playback; default 64.

- `VoiceAllocatorStorage` (interface): interface VoiceAllocatorStorage — Caller-owned reservation storage. Reads and writes use detached state.

Equal priorities steal the oldest reservation; lower priorities cannot interrupt higher priorities. Policy is retunable.

## @jgengine/core/buildings/buildingKit

- `BuildingKit` (interface): interface BuildingKit — Binds a building's generated part slots to models. A kit is plain serializable data — scene documents can carry one — and is deliberately unopinionated about art direction: the engine ships the seam, games ship the bindings.
- `BuildingKitBinding` (type): type BuildingKitBinding = | { readonly type: "model"; readonly part: BuildingKitPart; readonly fit: BuildingKitFit } | { readonly type: "box" } | { readonly type: "omit" } — What a renderer should do with one generated part.
- `BuildingKitFit` (type): type BuildingKitFit = "stretch" | "contain" | "cover" | "native" — How a kit model's native bounds are mapped onto the slot box `BuildingPartPlacement.scale` describes.
- `BuildingKitInput` (interface): interface BuildingKitInput — The authoring shape {@link defineBuildingKit} normalizes into a {@link BuildingKit}.
- `BuildingKitPart` (interface): interface BuildingKitPart — One bindable variant for a building part slot. `model` is an opaque reference the host resolves (an asset id, a pack-relative path, or a URL) — core never loads anything.
- `BuildingKitPartInput` (type): type BuildingKitPartInput = string | BuildingKitPart — A variant as authored: a bare model reference, or the full {@link BuildingKitPart} when it needs fit or transform tuning.
- `buildingKitVariantCounts` (function): function buildingKitVariantCounts(kit: BuildingKit): Partial<BuildingVariantCounts> — The variant counts a kit actually supplies, shaped for `BuildingConfigInput.variants`. Feed this into `generateBuilding` so seeded picks spread across exactly the models the kit binds instead of indexing past them and wrapping unevenly.
- `defineBuildingKit` (function): function defineBuildingKit(input: BuildingKitInput): BuildingKit — Validates and normalizes a kit description, accepting bare model strings as single-field variants. Throws on empty variants or invalid editor material references/selectors before loading models.
- `resolveBuildingKitPart` (function): function resolveBuildingKitPart(kit: BuildingKit | undefined, kind: BuildingPartKind, slot?: BuildingKitSlot): BuildingKitBinding — Resolves one generated part against a kit. Pass the placement's `kind` and its `kit` slot; the slot's `variant` wraps around the bound list, so a kit may carry any number of variants independent of the generator's `variants` counts.

## @jgengine/core/buildings/buildingLots

- `BuildingLotOptions` (interface): interface BuildingLotOptions — Options for {@link deriveBuildingLots}.
- `FRONTAGE_FILL_REFERENCE` (const): const FRONTAGE_FILL_REFERENCE: 0.45 — Frontage-fill reference point: at this dial value the compaction is a no-op (legacy spacing/width), so callers can leave `blockFill` unset for the classic look and this value reproduces it exactly.
- `LotArea` (interface): interface LotArea — Rectangular clip region lots must fall within (world center + half-extents).
- `PlacedBuildingLot` (interface): interface PlacedBuildingLot — One placed building lot: where a building stands and how it is turned to face its road.
- `PlotVariant` (interface): interface PlotVariant extends WorldBounds — One weighted plot size a frontage can mix in: `w` along the road, `d` into the block.
- `RoadFrontage` (interface): interface RoadFrontage — One road the frontage placer lines with buildings: a centerline polyline, its width and its sidewalks.
- `deriveBuildingLots` (function): function deriveBuildingLots(options: BuildingLotOptions): PlacedBuildingLot[] — Derive street-aligned building lots (PLOTS) from road frontage. Each side of each road walks the frontage placing plots at `plot.w + spacing` pitch — rolling the next plot size from the weighted `footprint` variants when several are given — offset outward by `width / 2 + setback + plot.d / 2` and turned to face the road. The PLOT CONTRACT is enforced here, exactly: no two plots ever overlap (true oriented-rect separation with the spacing gap, so corners and curved frontage can't stack buildings), and no plot footprint ever touches any road corridor in `roads` or `avoid` — not just its own frontage road. Deterministic: identical inputs (including seed) always yield the identical list.

## @jgengine/core/camera/cameraCollision

- `CAMERA_TRANSPARENT_USERDATA` (const): const CAMERA_TRANSPARENT_USERDATA: { readonly jgCameraTransparent: true } — userData applied to the group wrapping author `WorldOverlay` decor so the spring-arm ignores it by default.
- `CameraClearanceInput` (interface): interface CameraClearanceInput — What a camera asks `clearCameraBoom` each frame: the boom it wants and the surfaces that may stop it.
- `CameraClearanceResult` (interface): interface CameraClearanceResult — Clear camera position and the boom length to hand back next frame.
- `CameraCollisionQuery` (interface): interface CameraCollisionQuery — One collision question the camera asks: distance along a ray to the nearest surface that should stop it.
- `CameraOccluder` (interface): interface CameraOccluder — Minimal structural view of a raycast hit object: its own tags plus a parent link to walk. Keeps this filter free of a three.js import so it stays unit-testable.
- `CameraPoint` (interface): interface CameraPoint — World-space point for camera boom math, matching the rigs' `Vec3`.
- `clearCameraBoom` (function): function clearCameraBoom(input: CameraClearanceInput): CameraClearanceResult — Pull a camera in along its boom so it never sits inside world collision. A blocking surface rejects the desired position: the camera moves to `clearance` before it, and onto the pivot when the surface is closer than that (the pivot is inside, so no camera position is clear). Pulling in is immediate — a camera must not spend a frame inside a trunk — while releasing eases back at `releaseRate`, which is what makes the boom read as a spring arm instead of a hard stop.
- `isCameraOccluderTransparent` (function): function isCameraOccluderTransparent(object: CameraOccluder | null | undefined): boolean — Should the camera spring-arm ignore this raycast hit? Walks the object up its `.parent` chain and honors the nearest camera tag: `jgCameraCollide === true` blocks (opt back in), `jgCameraTransparent === true` passes through. Untagged geometry blocks as before, so engine-owned ground/entities are unaffected.
- `sceneCameraQuery` (function): function sceneCameraQuery(raycast: SceneRaycastApi["raycast"], options: { entities?: boolean; terrain?: boolean } = {}): CameraCollisionQuery — `CameraCollisionQuery` over the scene's existing collision query (`ctx.scene.raycast`), which already reads world solids, scene-object colliders and walls. Entities and terrain stay out by default: the followed body must not push its own camera, and looking down at the ground must not pull the boom.

## @jgengine/core/camera/cameraConfig

- `CAMERA_FRUSTUM_DEFAULTS` (const): const CAMERA_FRUSTUM_DEFAULTS: { readonly fov: 55; readonly near: 0.1; readonly far: 300; readonly zoom: 50; } — ⚠ undocumented
- `CameraFollowState` (interface): interface CameraFollowState { entityId: string; target: {x: number; y: number; z: number}; camera: {x: number; y: number; z: number}; distance: number } — ⚠ undocumented
- `CameraKeyframe` (interface): interface CameraKeyframe — One stop on a scripted camera path (#29).
- `CameraProjection` (type): type CameraProjection = "perspective" | "orthographic" — Canvas camera projection. "orthographic" renders a flat 2D-style view (side-scrollers, falling-block puzzles) — pair with `rig: "sideScroll"`; default "perspective".
- `CameraRigKind` (type): type CameraRigKind = | "orbit" | "first" | "topDown" | "rts" | "shoulder" | "lockOn" | "chase" | "observer" | "turntable" | "sideScroll" | "inspection" | "none" — Which camera rig the shell mounts. Every rig accepts `followEntityId: null` (avatar-less games — city-builders, card games, auto-battlers — still get a camera). Rigs are tuned through their config block below, never by writing camera positions from `onTick`. - `orbit` — third-person chase (the historical default; `perspective: "third"`). - `first` — pointer-lock mouse-look (`perspective: "first"`). - `topDown` — fixed height/pitch/yaw with decoupled follow (ARPG iso, top-down). - `rts` — free-pan / edge-scroll / rotate / zoom, optional follow. - `shoulder` — over-the-shoulder with ADS transition + shoulder swap. - `lockOn` — yaw bound to the player→target vector; move axis becomes strafe. - `chase` — speed-reactive vehicle chase (speed→FOV, spring arm, shake) + cockpit/hood/rear views. - `observer` — detached spectator/photo cam bound to any entity or fixed point; never reads player input. - `turntable` — slow auto-orbit of a fixed point: a rotating display stand for a scene. The friendly, flat spelling of `observer`'s point-orbit mode; providing `camera.turntable` selects it without an explicit `rig`. - `sideScroll` — fixed lateral follow (2.5D platformer/beat-'em-up side view); reads no player input. - `inspection` — model-viewer / editor rig (#207.7, #866): middle-drag pan, right-drag orbit, scroll zoom toward a configurable anchor; orbits a fixed point, reads no player/entity input. - `none` — no camera rig is mounted; use for HUD-only presentations or a game that manages its own camera.
- `CameraRigShakeConfig` (interface): interface CameraRigShakeConfig — Camera-shake / trauma defaults (#28). Any rig reads the trauma channel; game systems feed it via `cameraShake()`.
- `CameraWeaponView` (interface): interface CameraWeaponView — What a camera rig reads about the held weapon each frame; see `GameCameraConfig.weapon`.
- `ChaseCameraConfig` (interface): interface ChaseCameraConfig — Speed-reactive vehicle chase rig (#27) — speed→FOV, spring arm, procedural shake, interior views.
- `ChaseView` (type): type ChaseView = "chase" | "cockpit" | "hood" | "rear" — Fixed interior view for the chase rig (#27).
- `CinematicCameraConfig` (interface): interface CinematicCameraConfig — Scripted keyframe / path player (#29). When set it overrides the active rig.
- `FirstPersonCameraConfig` (interface): interface FirstPersonCameraConfig { eyeHeight?: number; sensitivity?: number; maxPitch?: number; reticle?: boolean; body?: boolean; viewmodel?: boolean; collision?: false | FirstPersonCollisionConfig } — ⚠ undocumented
- `FirstPersonCollisionConfig` (interface): interface FirstPersonCollisionConfig — Clearance tuning for the first-person camera's collision pull-in.
- `GameCameraConfig` (interface): interface GameCameraConfig — Camera tuning for the shell's rig stack: pick the rig via `rig`, then tune it through its matching config block. All fields optional — the default is the third-person orbit rig.
- `InspectionCameraConfig` (interface): interface InspectionCameraConfig — Model-viewer / inspection rig (#207.7) — orbit + pan + anchored zoom around a fixed point, never reads player input.
- `InspectionZoomAnchor` (type): type InspectionZoomAnchor = "target" | "cursor" | "center" — How scroll-zoom re-anchors the view for the inspection rig (#207.7): - `target` — dolly toward the orbit target (classic OrbitControls behavior). - `cursor` — dolly toward the point under the pointer. - `center` — dolly toward the viewport center; equivalent to `target` for an OrbitControls-driven rig, since the camera always faces `target` and that point already projects to the exact center of the viewport.
- `LockOnCameraConfig` (interface): interface LockOnCameraConfig — Lock-on / strafe rig (#26) — yaw bound to player→target, move axis becomes strafe.
- `ObserverCameraConfig` (interface): interface ObserverCameraConfig — Detached spectator/photo cam (#120) — binds to any entity or fixed point, never reads player input.
- `PixelPerfectCameraConfig` (interface): interface PixelPerfectCameraConfig — Pixel-art orthographic camera tuning. `pixelsPerUnit` is the authored pixel density.
- `PlayerFovConfig` (interface): interface PlayerFovConfig — Player-facing FOV preference applied across every perspective camera rig. Orthographic projections ignore it.
- `RtsCameraConfig` (interface): interface RtsCameraConfig extends TopDownCameraConfig — Free-pan / edge-scroll RTS rig (#24) — pan/rotate/zoom independent of any avatar.
- `ShoulderCameraConfig` (interface): interface ShoulderCameraConfig — Over-the-shoulder combat rig (#25) — offset, ADS, shoulder swap, decoupled reticle.
- `SideScrollCameraConfig` (interface): interface SideScrollCameraConfig — Fixed lateral 2.5D follow (side-on platformer cam): the camera sits perpendicular to the travel axis, tracks the followed entity, and never reads player look input.
- `TopDownCameraConfig` (interface): interface TopDownCameraConfig — Fixed top-down / isometric rig (#23) — height/pitch/yaw + decoupled follow.
- `TurntableCameraConfig` (interface): interface TurntableCameraConfig — Turntable / showcase rig — slowly auto-orbits a fixed world point (no player input), the way a museum turntable rotates an object on display. A flat, self-describing spelling of `observer`'s point-orbit mode: `target` names the point directly instead of `bind: { kind: "point", position }`. Set `camera.turntable` and the rig is inferred — you don't also write `rig`.

## @jgengine/core/camera/firstPersonBody.draw

- `FirstPersonBodyContext` (const): const FirstPersonBodyContext: React.Context<string | null> — The entity whose own body the first-person camera looks out of, or `null` when no body is drawn in first person. The shell provides it; a model instance bound to that entity collapses its head.
- `collapseHead` (function): function collapseHead(head: THREE.Object3D): void — Folds a head bone away for this frame; the animation writes its pose first, so call it after.
- `humanoidHead` (function): function humanoidHead(scene: THREE.Object3D): THREE.Object3D | null — The head bone of a humanoid rig the skeleton standard maps, or `null`. Scaling it to nothing folds the head, hair and face into the neck, so a camera at eye height sees the body's arms, hands and held items without looking out through the inside of the skull.
- `keepHeadUnderEye` (function): function keepHeadUnderEye(body: THREE.Object3D, head: THREE.Object3D, eye: THREE.Object3D, rest: THREE.Vector3): void — Slides `body` across the ground so its folded head sits straight under the `eye` camera, from `rest` (the body's own position before any slide). A walk or run clip leans the torso forward; without this the neck, nape hair and collar swing out in front of an eye-height camera. Call after `collapseHead`.
- `useFirstPersonBody` (function): function useFirstPersonBody(instanceId: string | undefined): boolean — True when `instanceId` is the body the first-person camera sits in.

- `cameraShake` (function): function cameraShake(amplitude: number, decayPerSecond?: number): void — Add camera trauma from anywhere. `decayPerSecond`, when given, retunes how fast it bleeds off.
- `createCameraShake` (function): function createCameraShake(config: CameraShakeConfig = {}): CameraShakeController — A seeded, serializable, trauma-based camera shake / impulse controller. A game calls `add(amount, kind?)` on impacts (a hit, an explosion, a landing) to raise trauma in `[0, 1]`; `update(dt)` bleeds it off over time; and `offset()` returns a pooled `{ x, y, z, pitch, yaw, roll }` kick equal to `trauma^exponent` times per-axis maxima times deterministic seeded value-noise sampled along an internal time cursor. A shell consumer applies that offset to the active camera each frame so the view visibly shakes. Nothing here is genre-specific: `kind` is a free label the game styles, all amplitudes/decay are parameters, and `snapshot`/ `restore` round-trips the shake through a save. Deterministic from `seed`: the same seed and dt sequence reproduce the same offsets.
- `defaultCameraShake` (const): const defaultCameraShake: CameraShakeController — The one camera-shake controller the rigs apply. Game systems with no React context (a `loop.onTick` reacting to `entity.died`) feed it through {@link cameraShake}; a rig reads it through {@link useCameraShake}. It is the core `createCameraShake` model, so a demo or test can drive the same controller directly.

Presentation only — it reads the controller and never interprets `kind`, mapping it through `kindLabels` for display. The shell camera rig applies the same controller's `offset()` to the camera; this panel is the on-screen readout of how much shake is in flight.

It only reads: the camera rig that applies the shake is what advances it. Returns the current trauma + kind for a HUD readout.

- `ParcelCut` (interface): interface ParcelCut — Inputs for one parcel strip cut from a block ring.

Works on any parcel polygon — no vertex correspondence needed.
- `carveCorridors` (function): function carveCorridors(poly: Vec2[], keep: Vec2, corridors: readonly { pts: readonly Vec2[]; width: number }[], margin: number): Vec2[] — Carve dead-end road corridors (cul-de-sac lanes pruned from the face graph) out of a polygon: for every corridor segment crossing it, keep the polygon piece on the side where `keep` lies.
- `conformPolygonToRing` (function): function conformPolygonToRing(poly: readonly Vec2[], ring: readonly Vec2[]): Vec2[] — Conform a polygon to a containing ring: sample every edge (a straight edge can bulge across a concave notch even when its endpoints hug the boundary), then pull each escaping point to its nearest boundary point. Callers re-run this after any operation that adds mid-edge vertices.
- `cutParcel` (function): function cutParcel(walker: RingWalker, blockRing: readonly Vec2[], cut: ParcelCut): Vec2[] | null — Cut one polygonal parcel out of a block land ring: the frontage arc between two stations, extruded inward along the station normals, clipped back to the block. Returns null when the strip collapses (over-tight corner, sliver arc).
- `extractGraphBlocks` (function): function extractGraphBlocks(nodes: readonly GraphBlockNode[], edges: readonly GraphBlockEdge[], params: { sidewalkBase: number; curbMargin: number }): { blocks: GraphBlockRings[]; deadEnds: { pts: Vec2[]; width: number; level: FabricLevel; street?: number | undefined }[] } — Extract closed blocks from an EXACT street graph — the `nodes`/`edges` a street network already carries — instead of re-deriving topology from welded polylines. Half-edges are ordered by true departure angle at each node, dangling chains are pruned first (returned as `deadEnds` for corridor carving), interior faces are traced through the rotation system, and each face is inset to its land ring by the bordering edges' half-widths (+ curb + sidewalk). Robust against wandered and arc-filleted centerlines, which defeat proximity welding. Pure bounded geometry.

- `pointsInPolygon` (function): function pointsInPolygon(ring: readonly Vec2[], count: number, rng: () => number, margin = 1.5): Vec2[] — Sample deterministic points inside a polygon by seeded rejection over its bounds.

## @jgengine/core/cutscene/sequenceDirector

- `CueListener` (type): type CueListener<Payload = unknown> = (emitted: EmittedCue<Payload>) => void — A cue listener, called once per cue as it fires. Returns nothing.
- `EmittedCue` (interface): interface EmittedCue<Payload = unknown> — A cue plus the resolved firing context passed to {@link SequenceDirector.onCue} listeners.
- `SequenceCue` (interface): interface SequenceCue<Payload = unknown> — One scheduled beat of a cutscene: a typed cue that fires when the playhead reaches `atMs`.
- `SequenceDirector` (interface): interface SequenceDirector<Payload = unknown> — A data-driven cutscene: an ordered timeline of typed cues that fire on a single injected clock. See {@link createSequenceDirector}.

- `SequenceSnapshot` (interface): interface SequenceSnapshot — Serializable snapshot — enough to resume a cutscene exactly where a save left it.

- `createSequenceDirector` (function): function createSequenceDirector<Payload = unknown>(options: SequenceDirectorOptions<Payload>): SequenceDirector<Payload> — A serializable cutscene / sequence director: an ordered timeline of typed cues (`{ atMs, kind, payload }`) advanced by one injected clock, firing each cue once and in order as its time passes — even across a large seek — with play/pause/ seek/skip/stop controls. The director only *schedules and emits* cues; it never interprets what a `kind` means, so the same primitive drives camera moves, dialogue lines, fades, or any game event. `snapshot`/`restore` round-trip the playhead and which cues have fired. Deterministic (no wall clock beyond the injected `now`) and allocation-free on the tick path.

- `CrownFire` (interface): interface CrownFire — A crown fire assessment for one place.
- `CrownFireType` (type): type CrownFireType = "surface" | "torching" | "crowning" | "conditional" — Crown fire type in Rothermel's 1991 sense (as BehavePlus): `surface` when the surface fire neither torches nor could sustain a crown fire, `torching` (passive) when it lights crowns it cannot carry, `crowning` (active) when it lights them and the crown rate passes Van Wagner's threshold, and `conditional` when an active crown fire could run but this surface fire cannot start one.
- `activeCrownCriticalRate` (function): function activeCrownCriticalRate(canopy: CanopyFuel): number — Van Wagner 1977 critical spread rate for an active crown fire, m/s: a crown fire sustains itself once it moves 3 kg/m²/min of canopy fuel, R = 3 / CBD (m/min).
- `assessCrownFire` (function): function assessCrownFire(input: { canopy: CanopyFuel; moisture: FuelMoisture; twentyFootWind: number; surfaceIntensity: number; surfaceHeatPerUnitArea: number; fm10Bed?: SurfaceFuelbed; }): CrownFire — Assess crown fire from a surface fire under a canopy: Van Wagner 1977 initiation and active thresholds, Rothermel 1991 crown spread rate and shape, Thomas 1963 flame length.
- `canopyFuelLoad` (function): function canopyFuelLoad(canopy: CanopyFuel): number — Canopy fuel load available to a crown fire, kg/m².
- `crownFlameLength` (function): function crownFlameLength(firelineIntensityKWm: number): number — Thomas 1963 crown flame length, m, from fireline intensity, kW/m: L = 0.2·I^(2/3) (ft, Btu/ft/s).
- `crownInitiationIntensity` (function): function crownInitiationIntensity(canopy: CanopyFuel): number — Van Wagner 1977 critical surface fireline intensity to ignite the crown, kW/m: I₀ = (0.010·CBH·(460 + 25.9·FMC))^1.5, CBH in m, FMC in percent (floored at 30 %).
- `crownLengthToBreadth` (function): function crownLengthToBreadth(twentyFootWind: number): number — Rothermel 1991 crown fire length-to-breadth ratio, 1 + 0.125 × the 20-ft wind in mph.
- `rothermelCrownRate` (function): function rothermelCrownRate(moisture: FuelMoisture, twentyFootWind: number, fm10Bed?: SurfaceFuelbed): number — Rothermel 1991 active crown fire spread rate, m/s: 3.34 times the surface rate of fuel model 10 at the same dead and live moisture, with midflame wind 0.4 × the 20-ft wind, on level ground.

## @jgengine/core/fire/fireLandscape

- `CanopyStand` (interface): interface CanopyStand extends CanopyFuel — A forest stand over a cell: the canopy that shelters the wind and can carry crown fire.
- `DEFAULT_FIRE_TUNING` (const): const DEFAULT_FIRE_TUNING: FireTuning — Defaults: 16-direction stencil, BehavePlus-default wind limit, crown fire and spotting on.
- `FireBurnState` (type): type FireBurnState = "unburnt" | "flaming" | "smouldering" | "burnt" — What a cell is doing: never burnt, flaming, smouldering coarse fuel, or burnt out.
- `FireCellKind` (type): type FireCellKind = "none" | "surface" | "torching" | "crowning" — How fire moved through a cell.
- `FireCellReading` (interface): interface FireCellReading — One cell's fire record, for game logic; renderers read the typed arrays of {@link FireLandscape.layers}.
- `FireLandscape` (interface): interface FireLandscape — A fire growing over a landscape of fuel, terrain and canopy.
- `FireLandscapeConfig` (interface): interface FireLandscapeConfig — Size, terrain, fuel and canopy of a fire landscape.
- `FireLandscapeSnapshot` (interface): interface FireLandscapeSnapshot — A landscape fire's whole state as JSON-safe values.
- `FireLayers` (interface): interface FireLayers — Typed per-cell outputs for renderers, row-major, updated in place every step.
- `FireMoistureField` (interface): interface FireMoistureField — Per-cell fuel moisture that changes over time (a dead-fuel moisture model, irrigation, rain).
- `FireStepStats` (interface): interface FireStepStats — Counters from the last step.
- `FireTuning` (interface): interface FireTuning — Live policy of a fire landscape; every value can change during play with `retune`.
- `FireWeather` (interface): interface FireWeather — Fire weather for one step. Directions are radians in the grid plane, from +x towards +z.
- `createFireLandscape` (function): function createFireLandscape(config: FireLandscapeConfig): FireLandscape — Grow a wildfire over a grid of fuel, terrain and canopy. Each cell spreads as a Rothermel surface fire shaped by the Anderson ellipse, or as a Rothermel 1991 crown fire once Van Wagner's 1977 thresholds are passed; arrival times follow Finney's 2002 minimum-travel-time method on an 8-, 16- or 32-direction stencil, integrating travel time through every cell a path crosses, on the slope surface, with a semi-Lagrangian triangle update so fronts also travel between stencil directions. Torching and crowning cells loft embers to Albini's maximum spotting distance, which light fuel with the NFDRS ignition probability. Cells flame for the Anderson residence time, smoulder coarse fuel out, and leave char, ash and scorch. Deterministic for a seed; cost is bounded by the event budget per step and the cells actively burning.

## @jgengine/core/fire/fuelModels

- `KJ_KG_PER_BTU_LB` (const): const KJ_KG_PER_BTU_LB: 2.326 — kJ/kg per Btu/lb.
- `MOISTURE_SCENARIOS` (const): const MOISTURE_SCENARIOS: Readonly<Record<string, FuelMoisture>> — Scott & Burgan 2005 fuel moisture scenarios: dead D1 (very low) to D4 (high) and live L1 (fully cured herbs) to L4 (fully green), keyed `D1L1`..`D4L4`.
- `M_PER_FT` (const): const M_PER_FT: 0.3048 — Metres per foot.
- `NON_BURNABLE_FUEL_MODELS` (const): const NON_BURNABLE_FUEL_MODELS: Readonly<Record<string, FuelModel>> — Non-burnable cover (urban, snow, agriculture, water, bare ground), keyed by code `NB1`..`NB9`.
- `SCOTT_BURGAN_FUEL_MODELS` (const): const SCOTT_BURGAN_FUEL_MODELS: Readonly<Record<string, FuelModel>> — The 40 standard fire behavior fuel models of Scott & Burgan 2005 (grass GR, grass-shrub GS, shrub SH, timber-understory TU, timber litter TL, slash-blowdown SB), keyed by code.
- `standardFuelModel` (function): function standardFuelModel(code: string): FuelModel | undefined — Every standard fuel model by code.
- `totalFuelLoad` (function): function totalFuelLoad(fuel: FuelModel): number — Total fuel load of a model, kg/m².

## @jgengine/core/fire/fuelMoisture

- `DEFAULT_FUEL_MOISTURE_TUNING` (const): const DEFAULT_FUEL_MOISTURE_TUNING: Readonly<FuelMoistureTuning> — NFDRS 1978 dead fuel lags and rain boundaries, NFDRS 2016 live fuel ranges.
- `FuelMoistureModel` (interface): interface FuelMoistureModel extends FireMoistureField — Per-cell dead fuel moisture and stand-wide live fuel moisture that follow the weather over time.
- `FuelMoistureSnapshot` (interface): interface FuelMoistureSnapshot — Serializable state of a fuel moisture model.
- `FuelMoistureTuning` (interface): interface FuelMoistureTuning — Live policy of a fuel moisture model; every value can change during play with `retune`.
- `MoistureWeather` (interface): interface MoistureWeather — The weather a fuel moisture model reads; the only seam between fire and a weather system.
- `createFuelMoistureModel` (function): function createFuelMoistureModel(config: { cells: number; initial: FuelMoisture; exposure?: Float32Array; /** Share of the rain that reaches each cell's fuel, 0 (under a roof) .. 1 (open); all open when omitted. */ rainShare?: Float32Array; tuning?: Partial<FuelMoistureTuning>; }): FuelMoistureModel — Fuel moisture over time from weather, one value set per fire grid cell, ready to hand to a fire landscape with `setMoistureField`. Dead fuels relax exponentially toward their equilibrium moisture (Simard 1968 at fuel-level conditions for 1-h and 10-h, air conditions for 100-h) with NFDRS 1978 time lags and rain boundaries; live fuels start at `initial` and follow a Jolly 2005 growing season index mapped onto the NFDRS 2016 live moisture ranges, averaged over the index's window. `exposure` (0..1 per cell) is how much sun reaches the fuel.
- `equilibriumMoistureContent` (function): function equilibriumMoistureContent(temperatureC: number, relativeHumidity: number): number — Equilibrium moisture content of dead wood, fraction of dry mass, from temperature (°C) and relative humidity (0..1): Simard 1968's three-part regression as used by the 1978 NFDRS.
- `fuelLevelWeather` (function): function fuelLevelWeather(temperatureC: number, relativeHumidity: number, cloudCover: number, sun: number): { temperatureC: number; relativeHumidity: number } — Temperature and humidity at the surface of sunlit fuel (Cohen & Deeming 1985): sun heats the fuel above the air and dries the air next to it, more under clear sky than overcast. `sun` scales the correction from none (night or full shade) to the full table value.
- `growingSeasonIndex` (function): function growingSeasonIndex(minimumTemperatureC: number, vaporPressureDeficitPa: number, dayLengthHours: number): number — Jolly et al. 2005 growing season index, 0..1: the product of ramps on daily minimum temperature (−2..5 °C), vapour pressure deficit (900..4100 Pa, inverted) and day length (10..11 h).
- `vaporPressureDeficit` (function): function vaporPressureDeficit(temperatureC: number, relativeHumidity: number): number — Vapour pressure deficit, Pa, from temperature (°C) and relative humidity (0..1), Tetens saturation pressure.

## @jgengine/core/fire/fuelSources

- `FireGridFrame` (interface): interface FireGridFrame — Where a fire grid sits in the world.
- `PlantCanopyFuel` (interface): interface PlantCanopyFuel — The crown fuel one grown plant carries.
- `plantCanopyFuel` (function): function plantCanopyFuel(structure: PlantStructure, species: PlantSpecies, leafAreaM2: number, options: { fineWoodRadiusM?: number } = {}): PlantCanopyFuel — Read a grown plant's crown fuel without changing it: foliage mass is its leaf area (from `PlantGrowth.stats().leafAreaM2`) over the species' specific leaf area; fine branchwood is the skeleton segments thinner than `fineWoodRadiusM` times the species' wood density.
- `rasterizeCanopyFuel` (function): function rasterizeCanopyFuel(frame: FireGridFrame, plants: readonly { x: number; z: number; fuel: PlantCanopyFuel }[], options: { foliarMoisture?: number } = {}): { canopies: CanopyStand[]; canopy: Int32Array } — Spread plants' crown fuel over a fire grid as canopy stands: each crown's available fuel is shared between the cells its disc overlaps, by overlap area; a cell's cover is the crown area over it (capped at 1), its height the tallest crown, its base the lowest, and its bulk density the load over that crown depth.
- `sampleFireGround` (function): function sampleFireGround(frame: FireGridFrame, sample: { heightAt?: (x: number, z: number) => number; fuelAt: (x: number, z: number) => string }): { elevation: Float32Array; fuels: FuelModel[]; fuel: Uint8Array } — Build a fire grid's ground from samplers: elevation at each cell centre and a standard fuel model code (Scott & Burgan `GR2`, Anderson `FM8`, non-burnable `NB9`, ...) for what covers the ground. The game owns the mapping from its terrain, biomes or ground layers to fuel codes.
- `sunExposure` (function): function sunExposure(frame: FireGridFrame, elevation: ArrayLike<number>, sun: { azimuth: number; elevation: number }, canopy?: { canopies: readonly CanopyStand[]; canopy: ArrayLike<number> }): Float32Array — Share of the sun reaching each cell's surface fuel, 0..1, for a fuel moisture model's `exposure`: the cosine of the sun on the cell's slope relative to flat ground (capped at 1), times the gaps between crowns. `sunAzimuth` is radians in the grid plane from +x towards +z; elevation is above the horizon.

## @jgengine/core/fire/spotting

- `SpotDistance` (interface): interface SpotDistance — How far embers from a source travel, and how high they were lofted.
- `SpotTerrain` (interface): interface SpotTerrain — The ground downwind of a fire, where embers fall.
- `TorchingSpecies` (type): type TorchingSpecies = | "engelmannSpruce" | "douglasFir" | "subalpineFir" | "westernHemlock" | "ponderosaPine" | "lodgepolePine" | "westernWhitePine" | "grandFir" | "balsamFir" | "slashPine" | "longleafPine" | "pondPine" | "shortleafPine" | "loblollyPine" — Albini 1979 torching-tree flame height and duration coefficients by species group.
- `emberIgnitionProbability` (function): function emberIgnitionProbability(oneHourMoisture: number, fuelTemperatureC: number): number — Probability that a firebrand landing in fine dead fuel starts a fire (Schroeder 1969, in the NFDRS form of Cohen & Deeming 1985): from 1-h fuel moisture and the fuel's temperature, 0..1.
- `surfaceFireSpotDistance` (function): function surfaceFireSpotDistance(flameLengthM: number, twentyFootWind: number, terrain: SpotTerrain): SpotDistance — Maximum spotting distance from a wind-driven surface fire (Albini 1983 as in BehavePlus): the firebrand is lofted by the flame's plume, then carried by the 20-ft wind over the downwind cover.
- `torchingTreeSpotDistance` (function): function torchingTreeSpotDistance(input: { species: TorchingSpecies; dbhM: number; treeHeightM: number; trees: number; twentyFootWind: number; terrain: SpotTerrain; }): SpotDistance — Maximum spotting distance from torching trees (Albini 1979): steady flame height and duration from species, DBH and number of trees torching together, the loft that flame gives a firebrand, and its drift over the downwind cover.

## @jgengine/core/fire/surfaceFire

- `KW_M_PER_BTU_FT_S` (const): const KW_M_PER_BTU_FT_S: number — kW/m per Btu/ft/s.
- `MPS_PER_MPH` (const): const MPS_PER_MPH: 0.44704 — m/s per mile/hour.
- `SpreadConditions` (interface): interface SpreadConditions — Wind and terrain under which a fuel bed spreads.
- `SurfaceFuelbed` (interface): interface SurfaceFuelbed — A fuel bed reduced to the wind- and slope-independent terms of Rothermel's model. Compute it once per fuel and moisture, then spread it under any wind and slope with {@link surfaceSpread}.
- `SurfaceSpread` (interface): interface SurfaceSpread — The head of a surface fire: its rate, direction, intensity and the ellipse it grows in.
- `WindLimit` (type): type WindLimit = "none" | "rothermel1972" | "andrews2013" — How the effective wind speed is capped. `none` is BehavePlus's default; `rothermel1972` caps it at 0.9·I_R ft/min; `andrews2013` uses the revised limit 96.8·I_R^(1/3) ft/min (Andrews, Cruz & Rothermel 2013).
- `curedHerbFraction` (function): function curedHerbFraction(liveHerbMoisture: number): number — Herbaceous load that has cured to dead in a dynamic fuel model: all of it at or below 30 % herb moisture, none from about 120 % (Scott & Burgan 2005), on the line BehavePlus uses.
- `ellipseEccentricity` (function): function ellipseEccentricity(lb: number): number — Eccentricity of a fire ellipse with length-to-breadth ratio `lb`.
- `firelineIntensity` (function): function firelineIntensity(heatPerUnitArea: number, rate: number): number — Byram 1959 fireline intensity I = H·R, kW/m, from heat per unit area (kJ/m²) and spread rate (m/s).
- `flameLength` (function): function flameLength(firelineIntensityKWm: number): number — Byram 1959 flame length L = 0.45·I^0.46 (ft, Btu/ft/s), in metres from kW/m.
- `intensityForFlameLength` (function): function intensityForFlameLength(flameLengthM: number): number — Fireline intensity (kW/m) that gives a flame length (m); the inverse of {@link flameLength}.
- `normalSpreadRate` (function): function normalSpreadRate(spread: SurfaceSpread, angle: number): number — Rate at which the fire front advances along its outward normal at `angle` radians from the heading, for the ellipse of `spread` (the support function of the ellipse; BehavePlus's "from perimeter" rate). Huygens-type growth models advance the front at this rate.
- `rayFromIgnitionRate` (function): function rayFromIgnitionRate(spread: SurfaceSpread, angle: number): number — Rate at which the fire travels along a ray at `angle` radians from the heading, measured from the ignition point at the rear focus of the ellipse (BehavePlus's "from ignition point" rate).
- `scorchHeight` (function): function scorchHeight(firelineIntensityKWm: number, midflameWind: number, airTemperatureC: number): number — Van Wagner 1973 crown scorch height, m, from fireline intensity (kW/m), midflame wind (m/s) and air temperature (°C).
- `surfaceFuelbed` (function): function surfaceFuelbed(fuel: FuelModel, moisture: FuelMoisture): SurfaceFuelbed — Reduce a fuel model at a moisture state to Rothermel's 1972 fuel bed terms, with Albini's 1976 corrections: size-class weighting of net load, the live moisture of extinction and the computer-model forms of A and Γ'. Dynamic models first cure live herbs to dead.
- `surfaceLengthToBreadth` (function): function surfaceLengthToBreadth(effectiveWind: number): number — Anderson 1983 length-to-breadth ratio of a wind-driven surface fire from the midflame effective wind (m/s), in the mile-per-hour form BehavePlus and Andrews 2018 publish, capped at 8.
- `surfaceSpread` (function): function surfaceSpread(bed: SurfaceFuelbed, conditions: SpreadConditions): SurfaceSpread — Spread a fuel bed under wind and slope: Rothermel's wind and slope factors combined as vectors (Albini & Chase 1980, as in BehavePlus), the effective wind speed, the Anderson 1983 ellipse and Byram intensity and flame length at the head.

## @jgengine/core/fire/windAdjustment

- `CanopyShelter` (interface): interface CanopyShelter — The forest canopy over a surface fuel bed, if any.
- `twentyFootWind` (function): function twentyFootWind(tenMetreWind: number): number — 20-ft wind from a 10-m wind: divide by 1.15 (Turner & Lawson 1978, as in BehavePlus).
- `windAdjustmentFactor` (function): function windAdjustmentFactor(fuelbedDepthM: number, canopy?: CanopyShelter): number — Wind adjustment factor from the 20-ft (6.1 m) open wind to midflame wind (Albini & Baughman 1979; Baughman & Albini 1980; Andrews 2012). Unsheltered fuel uses the fuel bed depth; fuel under a canopy that fills at least 5 % of the crown space and stands 6 ft or taller is sheltered.

## @jgengine/core/flight/aircraftDynamics

- `AircraftAssistCommand` (interface): interface AircraftAssistCommand — Control commands, `-1..1`, that drive the actuators after the assists.
- `AircraftAssistContext` (interface): interface AircraftAssistContext — What an assist sees each substep, derived from the integrator state so it replays deterministically.
- `AircraftAssistTuning` (interface): interface AircraftAssistTuning — Flight assists. Each one moves the same actuators the pilot does, so a stronger assist still flies within the airframe's authority. Strengths are `0..1`; an axis the pilot is deflecting gets less help the further the stick is pushed, so full stick is always the pilot's.
- `AircraftControlChannel` (interface): interface AircraftControlChannel — One control channel's actuator: how far the surfaces move and how fast.
- `AircraftEngineTuning` (interface): interface AircraftEngineTuning — A thrust source fixed to the body.
- `AircraftGearTuning` (interface): interface AircraftGearTuning — Wheels or skids: what the body rests on when it touches the ground.
- `AircraftMotorTuning` (interface): interface AircraftMotorTuning — A rocket motor: thrust follows a curve over burn time, propellant leaves at a mass flow so the body gets lighter and easier to turn, and the nozzle gimbals on the pitch and yaw channels. Stage by `retune`-ing to the next stage's mass and motor.
- `AircraftQuaternion` (type): type AircraftQuaternion = readonly [number, number, number, number] — Unit quaternion `[x, y, z, w]` taking body-frame vectors to world space.
- `AircraftRotorTuning` (interface): interface AircraftRotorTuning — A main rotor. Collective sets blade pitch, throttle sets rotor speed, and cyclic (the pitch and roll channels) tilts the disc. Its drag torque yaws the body the other way unless a tail rotor, a second rotor or a pedal input cancels it.
- `AircraftSurface` (interface): interface AircraftSurface — One lifting surface: a wing panel, a tailplane, a fin, a canard. Its lift acts at `at`, so the moments that pitch, roll and yaw the body come from where the surfaces sit, not from commanded rates.
- `AircraftVector` (type): type AircraftVector = readonly [number, number, number] — Body-frame or world-frame vector, m or N. The body frame is `[left, up, forward]` about the centre of mass.
- `RigidAircraft` (interface): interface RigidAircraft — A force-and-torque aircraft on the same tick/snapshot/retune contract as `VehicleDynamics`.
- `RigidAircraftInput` (interface): interface RigidAircraftInput — Pilot input for one tick.
- `RigidAircraftModifiers` (interface): interface RigidAircraftModifiers — Per-tick overrides layered over tuning: damage, icing, boost, gusts. Each scale defaults to `1`.
- `RigidAircraftOptions` (interface): interface RigidAircraftOptions — World hooks for one aircraft instance.
- `RigidAircraftState` (interface): interface RigidAircraftState — Serializable integrator state: everything `restore` needs to resume bit-for-bit.
- `RigidAircraftStep` (interface): interface RigidAircraftStep — One aircraft tick: pose plus the telemetry HUDs, camera, sound and probes read.
- `RigidAircraftTuning` (interface): interface RigidAircraftTuning — A rigid aircraft in physical units. There is no aircraft type: a jet, a glider and a paper plane differ only in these numbers. Rotation comes from surface forces acting on the inertia tensor, so loops, rolls, stalls and weathervaning are outcomes, not special cases.
- `aircraftAttitudeQuaternion` (function): function aircraftAttitudeQuaternion(heading: number, pitch: number, bank: number): AircraftQuaternion — Quaternion from heading, nose-up pitch and right bank, rad — the inverse of a step's `heading`/`pitch`/`bank`. Matches three.js `Euler(-pitch, heading, bank, "YXZ")`.
- `aircraftHeadingQuaternion` (function): function aircraftHeadingQuaternion(heading: number): AircraftQuaternion — Quaternion for a heading about world up, forward `[sin h, 0, cos h]`.
- `createRigidAircraft` (function): function createRigidAircraft(initial: RigidAircraftTuning, options: RigidAircraftOptions = {}): RigidAircraft — Creates a {@link RigidAircraft}: a quaternion rigid body with a diagonal inertia tensor, pushed by lifting surfaces, fuselage drag, an engine and gravity. Controls deflect surfaces through rate-limited actuators; nothing commands a rotation rate, so a jet loops when its tail can push the nose around and a glider stalls when it runs out of speed. Fixed internal substeps make it deterministic for a given `dt` sequence.

## @jgengine/core/flight/freeFlight

- `CREATIVE_FLIGHT_TUNING` (const): const CREATIVE_FLIGHT_TUNING: FreeFlightTuning — Preset for Minecraft-like creative flight — weightless, collides, yaw-relative strafe.
- `FreeFlightBindings` (interface): interface FreeFlightBindings — Per-axis bindings for free-flight — which actions drive each flight axis. Positive is forward/right/up.
- `FreeFlightController` (interface): interface FreeFlightController — Stateful handle for any free-flight actor with snapshot/restore/retune.
- `FreeFlightIntent` (interface): interface FreeFlightIntent — Intent for one free-flight tick — forward/right from WASD/analog, vertical from jump/crouch.
- `FreeFlightMode` (type): type FreeFlightMode = "creative" | "spectator" | "noclip" | "hover" — Free-flight families — character-scale 6DOF movement, distinct from vehicle aerodynamics.
- `FreeFlightState` (interface): interface FreeFlightState — Velocity state for a free-flight actor — serializable and ownable by the caller.
- `FreeFlightStep` (interface): interface FreeFlightStep — World displacement produced by one free-flight tick.
- `FreeFlightTuning` (interface): interface FreeFlightTuning — Data-first tuning for one free-flight profile.
- `HOVER_FLIGHT_TUNING` (const): const HOVER_FLIGHT_TUNING: FreeFlightTuning — Preset for hover/jetpack — gravity + thrust, useful for short bursts.
- `NOCLIP_FLIGHT_TUNING` (const): const NOCLIP_FLIGHT_TUNING: FreeFlightTuning — Preset for noclip — weightless, noclips, yaw-relative with independent vertical.
- `SPECTATOR_FLIGHT_TUNING` (const): const SPECTATOR_FLIGHT_TUNING: FreeFlightTuning — Preset for spectator — weightless, noclips, flies where the camera looks.
- `advanceFreeFlight` (function): function advanceFreeFlight(state: FreeFlightState, intent: FreeFlightIntent, yaw: number, pitch: number | undefined, dt: number, tuning: FreeFlightTuning, options?: Pick<MotionFrameOptions, "authoritativeStep">): FreeFlightStep — Advance one frame of free-flight kinematics. Horizontal uses yaw-relative strafe (A = left, D = right) — never roll/bank. Vertical is independent of pitch unless `alignWithLook` is true (spectator).
- `createFreeFlightController` (function): function createFreeFlightController(initialTuning: FreeFlightTuning, options: { yaw?: number; pitch?: number; state?: FreeFlightState } = {}): FreeFlightController — Totally free flight for any actor — character, camera, drone, or debug rig. Horizontal is always yaw-relative strafe; vertical is jump/crouch. Use `alignWithLook` for a 6DOF spectator that flies where the camera looks.
- `createFreeFlightState` (function): function createFreeFlightState(): FreeFlightState — Create an empty flight velocity state.
- `resolveFlightStep` (function): function resolveFlightStep(position: readonly [number, number, number], stepX: number, stepY: number, stepZ: number, obstacles: readonly CollisionObstacle[], radius: number = DEFAULT_OBSTACLE_PLAYER_RADIUS): { stepX: number; stepY: number; stepZ: number } — Resolve a flight step against world solids (XZ slide + Y clamp).
- `resolveFreeFlightIntent` (function): function resolveFreeFlightIntent(keys: MovementKeysState, analog: AnalogMoveIntent | null | undefined): FreeFlightIntent — Translate held keys + analog into a free-flight intent. Vertical is `space - (control|c)` so jump ascends and crouch descends — the same keys that walk/jump/crouch use, re-mapped for flight without re-binding.
- `resolveFreeFlightIntentFromInput` (function): function resolveFreeFlightIntentFromInput(isDown: (action: string) => boolean, value: (action: string) => number, pointer: PointerAxisState | null, bindings?: FreeFlightBindings): FreeFlightIntent — Translate live input (held actions + analog + pointer) into a flight intent using per-profile axis bindings. Unlisted bindings fall back to the defaults above so existing games keep WASD/Space/Ctrl/Shift without declaring anything.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/aircraftTrim

- `FlightLinearization` (interface): interface FlightLinearization — Small-perturbation model about a trim point.
- `FlightMode` (interface): interface FlightMode — One dynamic mode read from eigenvalues.
- `TrimCondition` (interface): interface TrimCondition — A steady flight condition to trim for.
- `TrimResult` (interface): interface TrimResult — A trimmed steady flight point.
- `WindAxisState` (interface): interface WindAxisState — Flight state in wind axes and Euler angles, the form Stevens & Lewis tabulate: SI units and radians.
- `linearizeReferenceAircraft` (function): function linearizeReferenceAircraft(aircraft: ReferenceAircraft, trim: TrimResult): FlightLinearization — Linearizes a reference aircraft about a trim point by central differences of the wind-axis equations, with propulsion and actuator states held, and names the classical modes: short period and phugoid from the longitudinal matrix, dutch roll, roll subsidence and spiral from the lateral one.
- `referenceStateFromWindAxes` (function): function referenceStateFromWindAxes(flight: WindAxisState, surfaces: ReferenceSurfaces, propulsion: readonly number[]): ReferenceAircraftState — Builds a reference state from wind-axis flight variables, still air.
- `steadyAirData` (function): function steadyAirData(aircraft: ReferenceAircraft, altitude: number, airspeed: number, alpha: number, beta: number): ReferenceAirData — Air data for a reference aircraft at rest in steady flight: no body rates, height above the ground at the origin.
- `trimReferenceAircraft` (function): function trimReferenceAircraft(aircraft: ReferenceAircraft, condition: TrimCondition, initial: { alpha?: number; throttle?: number } = {}): TrimResult — Trims a reference aircraft for steady wings-level flight at a speed, altitude and flight path angle: solves angle of attack, sideslip, throttle, elevator, aileron and rudder so every body acceleration vanishes, with the propulsion states at their steady values. Newton's method on a finite-difference Jacobian with a backtracking line search.
- `windAxesOf` (function): function windAxesOf(state: ReferenceAircraftState): WindAxisState — Wind-axis flight variables of a reference state, still air.
- `windAxisRates` (function): function windAxisRates(aircraft: ReferenceAircraft, state: ReferenceAircraftState, input: ReferencePilotInput): WindAxisState — Time derivative of the wind-axis variables at a state: airspeed, α and β rates from the body accelerations, Euler rates from the body rates, and the navigation rates. Still air.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/bo105Helicopter

- `BO105_DESIGN` (const): const BO105_DESIGN: HelicopterDesign — The MBB Bo-105 at 2200 kg: Peterson's main rotor, Padfield's mass, inertia, hub and tail rotor placement (hub 1.48 m above the centre of gravity, shaft tilted 3° forward, tail rotor 6 m aft), two Allison 250-C20B turboshafts at 313 kW each, and a 1.2 m² drag area: the airframe drag the NASA wind-tunnel rotor was trimmed to carry in its flight-matched runs (TM-110356 appendix D, propulsive force at μ ≥ 0.2). Control ranges, tail surfaces and skids are estimates.
- `BO105_FORWARD_FLIGHT_DATA` (const): const BO105_FORWARD_FLIGHT_DATA: readonly { advanceRatio: number; shaftAngle: number; thrust: number; power: number; longitudinalCyclic: number }[] — Bo-105 full-scale rotor in the flight-matched wind-tunnel runs (TM-110356 appendix D, runs 43 and 46): advance ratio, shaft angle (rad, aft positive), `CT/σ`, and `CP/σ` and longitudinal cyclic (rad) averaged over the repeat points.
- `BO105_HOVER_DATA` (const): const BO105_HOVER_DATA: readonly { advanceRatio: number; thrust: number; power: number }[] — Bo-105 full-scale rotor hover data, NASA Ames 40×80 ft tunnel with the doors open, shaft at −10° (TM-110356 appendix B, run 12): advance ratio, `CT/σ` along the shaft and `CP/σ`.
- `BO105_MAIN_ROTOR` (const): const BO105_MAIN_ROTOR: RotorDesign — MBB Bo-105 main rotor from NASA TM-110356 (Peterson, 1995), table 1: hingeless, four blades, 16.11 ft radius, 0.886 ft chord, −8° linear twist, 2.5° precone, 717 ft/s tip speed, NACA 23012. The hingeless blade is a centre spring with Padfield's Bo-105 flap inertia (231.7 kg·m²) and stiffness (113 330 N·m/rad), a flap frequency of 1.12 per rev. The 20% root cutout is an estimate.
- `BO105_TAIL_ROTOR` (const): const BO105_TAIL_ROTOR: RotorDesign — Bo-105 tail rotor: two blades, 0.95 m radius, 0.179 m chord, 233 rad/s, untwisted (Padfield's Bo-105 data).
- `BO105_TUNNEL_AIR` (const): const BO105_TUNNEL_AIR: { hoverDensity: number; forwardDensity: number; speedOfSound: number; } — Air density and tip Mach number of the TM-110356 runs.
- `createBo105Model` (function): function createBo105Model(options: HelicopterModelOptions = {}): HelicopterModel — Creates the Bo-105 reference helicopter.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/cessna172Aircraft

- `C172_PROPELLER` (const): const C172_PROPELLER: PropellerGeometry — McCauley 1C160/DTM7553 fixed-pitch propeller: 75 in diameter, 53 in geometric pitch, two blades. The planform is a representative metal GA blade (activity factor about 85), widest near 45% radius.
- `createCessna172Model` (function): function createCessna172Model(): ReferenceAircraftModel — A Cessna 172N at its 2300 lb gross weight, flaps up. Geometry, weights and control travel come from the 172N handbook and FAA type certificate; stability and control derivatives from Roskam's data for the Cessna 182, which flies the same wing; maximum lift from NACA 2412 section data; post-stall lift and drag from Viterna–Corrigan; inertia from Roskam scaled to this weight. Ground effect cuts induced drag (McCormick's high-wing factor). Power is a Lycoming O-320-H2AD with Gagg–Ferrar altitude lapse driving a blade-element McCauley 1C160 propeller, with the shaft speed integrated, its gyroscopic momentum and its torque reaction on the airframe.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/coefficientTable

- `CoefficientTable` (interface): interface CoefficientTable — A gridded table over any number of axes with multilinear interpolation.
- `CoefficientTableAxis` (interface): interface CoefficientTableAxis — One axis of a {@link CoefficientTable}: strictly increasing breakpoints and what happens past the ends.
- `createCoefficientTable` (function): function createCoefficientTable(axes: readonly CoefficientTableAxis[], values: readonly number[]): CoefficientTable — Creates a gridded {@link CoefficientTable}, the form aerodynamic data comes in (alpha by beta by Mach by deflection). `values` is row-major: the last axis varies fastest. Interpolation is multilinear across all axes and allocates nothing per sample.
- `evenBreakpoints` (function): function evenBreakpoints(start: number, end: number, count: number): number[] — Evenly spaced breakpoints from `start` to `end` inclusive.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/f16Aircraft

- `F16ModelOptions` (interface): interface F16ModelOptions — Options for {@link createF16Model}.
- `STEVENS_LEWIS_GRAVITY` (const): const STEVENS_LEWIS_GRAVITY: number — Stevens & Lewis gravity, 32.17 ft/s², in m/s².
- `createF16Model` (function): function createF16Model(options: F16ModelOptions = {}): ReferenceAircraftModel — The F-16 of Stevens & Lewis, *Aircraft Control and Simulation* (2nd ed., Appendix A): NASA TP-1538 (Nguyen et al., 1979) wind-tunnel data reduced to coefficient tables in angle of attack (−10° to 45°), sideslip and elevator, damping derivatives by angle of attack, the F100 thrust table by altitude and Mach with its power-lag dynamics, and engine gyroscopic momentum. 20 500 lb, 300 ft² wing. Subsonic and below 45° angle of attack; outside that the tables extrapolate. Elevator, aileron and rudder actuators are the book's 20.2 rad/s first-order lags with 60, 80 and 120 °/s rate limits. Gear geometry is estimated (see source).
- `f16CycleEngine` (function): function f16CycleEngine(): GasTurbineEngine — The F100-PW-220 cycle engine the F-16 shares across instances (its operating-line tables fill in as it flies).
- `f16PowerCommand` (function): function f16PowerCommand(throttle: number): number — Commanded power level, percent, for a throttle position `0..1` (the throttle gearing; 77% throttle is military power).
- `f16Thrust` (function): function f16Thrust(power: number, altitude: number, mach: number): number — Installed thrust, N, at a power level (percent), altitude (m) and Mach: idle to military below 50%, military to full afterburner above.
- `stevensLewisAtmosphere` (function): function stevensLewisAtmosphere(altitude: number): AtmosphereSample — The air-data model Stevens & Lewis run the F-16 with (their `ADC` routine): a linear-lapse troposphere density fit and a 390 °R stratosphere above 35 000 ft. Use it to reproduce the book's numbers; use `standardAtmosphere` otherwise.

- `ComparisonTable` (interface): interface ComparisonTable — Any game / reference / real comparison {@link formatFlightComparison} can print.

The game aircraft fly with their own assists, as players fly them.
