## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/flightTests

- `FlightTestControls` (interface): interface FlightTestControls — Stick, throttle and brakes, the `RigidAircraftInput` shape.
- `FlightTestOptions` (interface): interface FlightTestOptions — Scenario settings.
- `FlightTestReport` (interface): interface FlightTestReport — Results of {@link runFlightTests}, SI units. `NaN` where a test could not finish.
- `FlightTestSample` (interface): interface FlightTestSample — What a flight test reads each tick, in the same units and signs for every subject.
- `FlightTestSubject` (interface): interface FlightTestSubject — Anything the flight tests can fly: the reference sim or a game model behind an adapter.
- `KNOTS_PER_MPS` (const): const KNOTS_PER_MPS: number — Knots in one m/s.
- `referenceFlightSubject` (function): function referenceFlightSubject(model: ReferenceAircraftModel, cruiseSpeed: number, options: ReferenceAircraftOptions = {}): FlightTestSubject & { maxMach: number } — Wraps a reference model as a {@link FlightTestSubject}. Airborne starts are trimmed, so a scenario begins in steady flight; the air is sea-level standard at the start and the ground far below unless the test is on the runway.
- `rigidAircraftFlightSubject` (function): function rigidAircraftFlightSubject(name: string, tuning: RigidAircraftTuning, cruiseSpeed: number, options: RigidAircraftOptions = {}): FlightTestSubject — Wraps a game `RigidAircraftTuning` as a {@link FlightTestSubject}, flown exactly as the game runs it: its assists stay on, air density is the model's default, and the ground is flat at `y = 0`.
- `runFlightTests` (function): function runFlightTests(subject: FlightTestSubject, options: FlightTestOptions = {}): FlightTestReport — Flies one subject through the standard flight tests with simple deterministic autopilots: the idle stall at constant altitude, full-throttle level top speed, a constant-speed climb sweep, a full-aileron roll at twice the stall speed, a sustained turn found by bisecting the bank to zero excess power at each speed, and a full-throttle take-off. Every subject flies the same manoeuvres, so a game model and a reference airframe compare metric by metric.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/gasTurbine

- `GasModel` (interface): interface GasModel — Thermodynamic properties of air and of air with burnt fuel, per kg of mixture. Enthalpy is zero at 298.15 K; the entropy function is `∫cp/T dT`, so an isentrope between two pressures is `Δφ = R·ln(P₂/P₁)`.
- `GasStream` (interface): interface GasStream — A gas stream: air and fuel mass flow, kg/s, total temperature, K, and total pressure, Pa.
- `GasTurbineComponents` (interface): interface GasTurbineComponents — Component losses and efficiencies. Polytropic efficiencies hold across the operating range.
- `GasTurbineCycle` (interface): interface GasTurbineCycle — A sized gas turbine cycle that solves steady off-design points.
- `GasTurbineDesign` (interface): interface GasTurbineDesign — A two-spool gas turbine at its design point: a turbojet (`bypassRatio: 0`, `fanPressureRatio: 1`), a separate-flow turbofan or a mixed-flow turbofan, with or without an afterburner. SI units.
- `GasTurbineFlight` (interface): interface GasTurbineFlight — Free-stream flight condition.
- `GasTurbinePoint` (interface): interface GasTurbinePoint — One steady operating point. Forces in N, flows in kg/s, temperatures in K, pressures in Pa, powers in W.
- `InletKind` (type): type InletKind = "mil-e-5007d" | "normal-shock" — How the inlet loses total pressure with flight Mach number.
- `WALSH_FLETCHER_GAS` (const): const WALSH_FLETCHER_GAS: GasModel — Dry air and kerosene combustion products with temperature-dependent specific heat, from the polynomials of Walsh & Fletcher, *Gas Turbine Performance* (2nd ed., 2004). R = 287.05 J/(kg·K) for both, as they take it.
- `createGasTurbineCycle` (function): function createGasTurbineCycle(design: GasTurbineDesign): GasTurbineCycle — Sizes a two-spool gas turbine at its design point and returns a cycle that solves steady off-design points by component matching in the manner of Mattingly's performance method (*Elements of Propulsion*, 2006, ch. 8), on real gas properties: both turbine nozzles choked, so the high-pressure turbine runs at a near-fixed expansion ratio; constant polytropic efficiencies; fan and compressor work from the spool power balances; bypass ratio from the fan nozzle's flow (separate exhausts) or the mixer's static pressure match (mixed exhaust, whose variable nozzle holds the low-pressure turbine ratio, as an augmented turbofan's control does). Spool speeds follow Euler's turbine relation, work ∝ N². Turbine cooling air and power offtake are not modelled.
- `inletShockRecovery` (function): function inletShockRecovery(kind: InletKind, mach: number): number — Inlet total pressure recovery from shock losses alone: MIL-E-5007D's `1 − 0.075·(M − 1)^1.35` above Mach 1, or the total pressure ratio across a normal shock for a fixed pitot inlet such as the F-16's.
- `perfectGas` (function): function perfectGas(cp: number, gamma: number): GasModel — A calorically perfect gas, fuel ignored: the textbook ideal-cycle check.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/gasTurbineEngine

- `GasTurbineCommand` (interface): interface GasTurbineCommand — Power lever split: `dry` runs idle to maximum dry thrust, `afterburner` adds afterburning on top.
- `GasTurbineEngine` (interface): interface GasTurbineEngine — A gas turbine with spool dynamics, flying a {@link GasTurbineCycle}'s operating line.
- `GasTurbineEngineOptions` (interface): interface GasTurbineEngineOptions — Rotor dynamics and fuel control of a {@link GasTurbineEngine}.
- `GasTurbineEngineOutput` (interface): interface GasTurbineEngineOutput — What {@link GasTurbineEngine.evaluate} writes.
- `createGasTurbineEngine` (function): function createGasTurbineEngine(cycle: GasTurbineCycle, options: GasTurbineEngineOptions): GasTurbineEngine — Creates a {@link GasTurbineEngine}: two spools with real inertia flying the cycle's steady operating line, in the quasi-steady manner of simplified engine transient models. Each spool speeds up by its shaft power surplus over its inertia, `J·ω·dω/dt = P_turbine − P_compressor`: the compressor works on its steady line at the current speed, and burner fuel above the steady flow at that speed heats the turbines (linearised about the line). A fuel control meters fuel by a speed governor inside acceleration and deceleration limits, as real controls guard surge and flame-out. The throttle is linear in steady thrust from idle to maximum dry; the afterburner lights at maximum dry and modulates its exit temperature at a rate. Steady performance comes from tables of cycle solutions over flight Mach and ambient temperature, built on first use of each flight condition; thrust and fuel scale with ambient pressure.
- `gasTurbinePropulsion` (function): function gasTurbinePropulsion(engine: GasTurbineEngine, command: (throttle: number) => GasTurbineCommand): ReferencePropulsion — A {@link ReferencePropulsion} driving a {@link GasTurbineEngine} along body x: thrust, fuel-burning spool states and the spools' gyroscopic momentum. `command` maps the pilot's throttle to the engine's power lever.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/helicopter

- `HelicopterDesign` (interface): interface HelicopterDesign — A single-main-rotor helicopter with a tail rotor, a turboshaft and a speed governor. Body axes: x forward, y right, z down.
- `HelicopterModel` (interface): interface HelicopterModel extends ReferenceAircraftModel — A helicopter model with its design and per-rotor telemetry.
- `HelicopterModelOptions` (interface): interface HelicopterModelOptions — Options for {@link createHelicopterModel}.
- `HelicopterRotorTelemetry` (interface): interface HelicopterRotorTelemetry — What the rotors did at the last evaluation.
- `HelicopterSurface` (interface): interface HelicopterSurface — A small lifting surface on the airframe (tailplane or fin), sized and placed in body axes.
- `HelicopterTrim` (interface): interface HelicopterTrim — A trimmed helicopter: attitude, controls and the power it takes.
- `HelicopterTrimCondition` (interface): interface HelicopterTrimCondition — A steady helicopter flight condition: ground speed along the heading and climb rate, still air.
- `createHelicopterModel` (function): function createHelicopterModel(design: HelicopterDesign, options: HelicopterModelOptions = {}): HelicopterModel — Builds a reference helicopter: the airframe flies on {@link createReferenceAircraft}'s 6-DOF, the main and tail rotors are blade-element rotors with flapping and dynamic inflow ({@link evaluateRotor}), a governor holds rotor speed with the engine's power and lets the rotor freewheel when the engine cannot drive it (autorotation), and the fuselage, tailplane and fin add drag, damping and weathercock stability. The pilot's throttle is the collective lever; pitch, roll and yaw move the swashplate and the tail rotor pitch through servos.
- `trimHelicopter` (function): function trimHelicopter(aircraft: ReferenceAircraft, model: HelicopterModel, condition: HelicopterTrimCondition): HelicopterTrim — Trims a reference helicopter for steady flight with no sideslip: solves pitch, bank, collective, both cyclics and pedal so every body acceleration vanishes with the rotors' flapping, inflow and speed steady.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/helicopterRotor

- `IsolatedRotorCondition` (interface): interface IsolatedRotorCondition — A wind-tunnel operating point for an isolated rotor.
- `IsolatedRotorTrim` (interface): interface IsolatedRotorTrim — An isolated rotor trimmed to a thrust with its first-harmonic flapping (so its hub moment) zeroed.
- `RotorDesign` (interface): interface RotorDesign — A rotor's blades, hub and the section they are made of. A counter-clockwise rotor seen from above (the US and Bo-105 sense).
- `RotorFlow` (interface): interface RotorFlow — What a rotor flies through, all in shaft axes: x forward in the disc, y right, z down the shaft.
- `RotorLoads` (interface): interface RotorLoads — Loads one {@link evaluateRotor} call writes. Force and moment act on the hub, in shaft axes.
- `RotorPitch` (interface): interface RotorPitch — Blade pitch, rad: `θ = collective + twist·(r/R − 0.75) + cosine·cos ψ + sine·sin ψ`, ψ from the tail in the direction of rotation.
- `createRotorLoads` (function): function createRotorLoads(design: RotorDesign): RotorLoads — Fresh output buffers for {@link evaluateRotor}.
- `evaluateRotor` (function): function evaluateRotor(design: RotorDesign, flow: RotorFlow, pitch: RotorPitch, speed: number, state: readonly number[], out: RotorLoads): void — Evaluates a rotor: blade-element loads over the disc (each station and azimuth sees its own pitch, flapping, inflow and Mach number), hub forces and moments, aerodynamic torque, and the rates of its states. The flap states are multiblade coning and first-harmonic tilt with their rates, driven by aerodynamic flap moments, centrifugal and spring stiffness and the airframe's pitch and roll rates. The inflow is dynamic blade-element momentum theory: each annulus carries its own momentum inflow with Prandtl's tip loss and Pitt–Peters apparent mass, and the first harmonics follow the Pitt–Peters (1981) skewed-wake model. Near the ground the induced velocity falls by Cheeseman–Bennett; in the vortex ring state it follows Leishman's empirical curve.
- `naca23012RotorSection` (function): function naca23012RotorSection(alpha: number, mach: number): { cl: number; cd: number } — NACA 23012 rotor section: lift slope 6.0 per radian and zero lift at −1.2° (NACA Report 824), Prandtl–Glauert to Mach 0.7, a maximum lift of 1.5 that falls with Mach past 0.3, Bailey's rotor profile-drag polar `0.0087 − 0.0216α + 0.400α²` (NACA Report 716), a quadratic drag rise past a critical Mach of 0.72 (less with lift) and flat-plate behaviour past the stall and in reversed flow.
- `rotorStateCount` (function): function rotorStateCount(design: RotorDesign): number — Number of states a rotor carries: three flap angles, their rates, two inflow harmonics and one inflow per station.
- `rotorStateNames` (function): function rotorStateNames(design: RotorDesign, prefix: string): string[] — Names of a rotor's states, in order.
- `settleRotor` (function): function settleRotor(design: RotorDesign, flow: RotorFlow, pitch: RotorPitch, speed: number, state: number[]): boolean — Writes a rotor's steady flapping and inflow at a fixed speed, pitch and flow into `state` (rates zero), by Newton's method from a momentum-theory start. Returns whether it converged.
- `solveNewton` (function): function solveNewton(residual: (x: readonly number[]) => number[], start: readonly number[], options: { iterations?: number; tolerance?: number; step?: readonly number[] } = {}): { x: number[]; norm: number } — Newton's method with a forward-difference Jacobian and a backtracking line search; returns the last iterate and its residual norm.
- `trimIsolatedRotor` (function): function trimIsolatedRotor(design: RotorDesign, condition: IsolatedRotorCondition): IsolatedRotorTrim — Trims an isolated rotor the way a wind tunnel does: at an advance ratio and shaft angle, solves collective and both cyclics so the thrust matches and first-harmonic flapping vanishes, with flapping and inflow steady.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/jetEngineComparison

- `JetComparison` (interface): interface JetComparison — A game jet's engine metrics beside the F100-PW-220 cycle engine's and the real engine's.
- `JetComparisonAircraft` (interface): interface JetComparisonAircraft — A game jet to measure: its tuning and the thrust multiplier its afterburner applies, if it has one.
- `JetComparisonRow` (interface): interface JetComparisonRow — One metric: the game jet, the F100 cycle engine and the published or NASA-table figure; `real` is absent where none exists.
- `compareJetEngines` (function): function compareJetEngines(aircraft: readonly JetComparisonAircraft[]): JetComparison[] — Measures each game jet's engine against the F100-PW-220 cycle engine and real F100 figures: dry thrust, how it lapses with altitude and Mach, the afterburner ratio and spool-up time. Real values are the NASA TP-1538 F-16 installed thrust tables, the published F100 ratings and Stevens & Lewis's power lag. Game values come from ticking the game's own `createRigidAircraft`, so a model whose thrust ignores air density and speed shows a ratio of 1 where the real engine loses half its thrust.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/propeller

- `BladeSection` (type): type BladeSection = (alpha: number, mach: number, radiusFraction: number) => { cl: number; cd: number } — Lift and drag of one blade section at an angle of attack and Mach number.
- `PropellerGeometry` (interface): interface PropellerGeometry — A fixed-pitch propeller's geometry.
- `PropellerMap` (interface): interface PropellerMap — Thrust and power coefficients `CT = T/(ρn²D⁴)`, `CP = P/(ρn³D⁵)` by advance ratio `J = V/(nD)` and tip Mach.
- `clarkYPropellerSection` (function): function clarkYPropellerSection(alpha: number, mach: number, radiusFraction: number): { cl: number; cd: number } — The section data of a flat-bottomed propeller airfoil in the Clark Y family: a thin-airfoil lift slope corrected by Prandtl–Glauert up to Mach 0.7, zero lift at −4° to the flat lower surface, a stall near `cl = 1.2` that falls to flat-plate lift, a parabolic drag bucket, Lock's compressibility drag rise past a critical Mach that drops as the section thickens toward the hub, and flat-plate drag past the stall.
- `createPropellerMap` (function): function createPropellerMap(geometry: PropellerGeometry, advanceRatios = evenBreakpoints(0, 1.5, 31), tipMachs = evenBreakpoints(0.2, 0.95, 6)): PropellerMap — Tabulates a propeller's `CT` and `CP` over advance ratio and tip Mach with {@link solvePropeller}, so a simulation interpolates instead of solving momentum balances every step.
- `solvePropeller` (function): function solvePropeller(geometry: PropellerGeometry, advanceRatio: number, tipMach: number, speedOfSound = 340.294): { ct: number; cp: number } — Solves blade-element momentum theory for one operating point: each annulus balances the thrust and torque its blade sections make against the axial and swirl momentum it puts into the slipstream, with Prandtl's tip and hub loss. Returns `CT` and `CP`; `J` is the advance ratio and `tipMach` the tip's rotational Mach number.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/referenceAircraft

- `ReferenceActuator` (interface): interface ReferenceActuator — One surface actuator: where full pilot input puts it, and how fast it gets there.
- `ReferenceAeroCoefficients` (interface): interface ReferenceAeroCoefficients — Body-axis aerodynamic coefficients about the centre of gravity, written by a model's `aerodynamics`. Forces are `q̄·S·C`, rolling and yawing moments `q̄·S·b·C`, pitching moment `q̄·S·c̄·C`.
- `ReferenceAirData` (interface): interface ReferenceAirData — Air data the aerodynamic model reads, SI units and radians.
- `ReferenceAircraft` (interface): interface ReferenceAircraft — A reference 6-DOF aircraft: rigid body, quaternion attitude, fixed-step RK4.
- `ReferenceAircraftModel` (interface): interface ReferenceAircraftModel — A complete reference airframe: geometry, mass, aerodynamics, controls, propulsion and gear.
- `ReferenceAircraftOptions` (interface): interface ReferenceAircraftOptions — World hooks for a reference aircraft.
- `ReferenceAircraftSample` (interface): interface ReferenceAircraftSample — Telemetry for the current state.
- `ReferenceAircraftState` (interface): interface ReferenceAircraftState — Serializable integrator state.
- `ReferenceGearLeg` (interface): interface ReferenceGearLeg — One landing gear leg: a massless strut spring-damper at the wheel's contact point and a tyre with rolling resistance, brakes and slip-angle side force that saturates at the friction limit.
- `ReferenceInitialCondition` (interface): interface ReferenceInitialCondition — Where and how a reference aircraft starts.
- `ReferenceMassProperties` (interface): interface ReferenceMassProperties — Mass and inertia about the centre of gravity, body axes.
- `ReferencePilotInput` (interface): interface ReferencePilotInput — Pilot input, the same shape as `RigidAircraftInput`.
- `ReferencePropulsion` (interface): interface ReferencePropulsion — An engine and whatever it drives, with its own integrated states.
- `ReferencePropulsionOutput` (interface): interface ReferencePropulsionOutput — What a propulsion model writes each evaluation: body-axis force and moment, rotor angular momentum, state rates.
- `ReferenceSurfaces` (interface): interface ReferenceSurfaces — Surface deflections, rad, in the model's own sign convention.
- `ReferenceVector` (type): type ReferenceVector = [number, number, number] — Three numbers, body axes (x forward, y right, z down) or north-east-down axes.
- `ReferenceWind` (type): type ReferenceWind = (position: ReferenceVector, time: number) => ReferenceVector — Wind at a point and time: mean wind plus any turbulence, north-east-down m/s.
- `createReferenceAircraft` (function): function createReferenceAircraft(model: ReferenceAircraftModel, options: ReferenceAircraftOptions = {}): ReferenceAircraft — Creates a {@link ReferenceAircraft}: a flat, non-rotating Earth 6-DOF rigid body with quaternion attitude, a full inertia tensor (with the `Ixz` product) plus gyroscopic engine momentum, gravity falling off with altitude, an injected atmosphere and wind, the α̇ aerodynamic terms solved implicitly, first-order rate-limited actuators, propulsion states, and spring-damper gear with tyre friction. Integrates with classic fourth-order Runge–Kutta at a fixed step, so halving the step cuts the error about sixteen-fold. It is a measuring stick for game flight models, not a game's runtime.
- `referenceEuler` (function): function referenceEuler(q: readonly [number, number, number, number]): { heading: number; pitch: number; bank: number } — Yaw-pitch-roll Euler angles, rad, of a body-to-NED quaternion `[w, x, y, z]`.
- `referenceQuaternion` (function): function referenceQuaternion(heading: number, pitch: number, bank: number): [number, number, number, number] — Quaternion `[w, x, y, z]` from yaw-pitch-roll Euler angles, rad.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/referenceEngines

- `F100_PW_220` (const): const F100_PW_220: GasTurbineDesign — Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-220 (F-16C/D), sized at sea-level static from its published figures: 228 lb/s airflow, bypass ratio 0.63, overall pressure ratio 25. Fitted: the turbine inlet temperature so military thrust is 14 590 lbf, the afterburner temperature so full afterburner is 23 770 lbf, and the control schedule (5% temperature margin over the sea-level point, corrected fan speed rising 0.2 per unit cold inlet ratio) to the NASA TP-1538 installed thrust tables. The fan pressure ratio comes from the mixed-flow rule (≈ 3.0). Mattingly level 3 components.
- `F100_PW_220_DYNAMICS` (const): const F100_PW_220_DYNAMICS: GasTurbineEngineOptions — F100-PW-220 rotor dynamics. Inertias are estimates from the engine's published size and weight (about 30% of its 1467 kg rotating, at half the 0.44 m fan tip radius), not published figures; speeds are typical of the family. Installation is the TP-1538 sea-level static military thrust over the uninstalled rating, 12 680 / 14 590 lbf.
- `F100_PW_220_PUBLISHED` (const): const F100_PW_220_PUBLISHED: { militaryThrust: number; militaryTsfc: number; afterburnerThrust: number; } — F100-PW-220 published sea-level static ratings (uninstalled): military 14 590 lbf at 0.73 lb/(lbf·h), afterburner 23 770 lbf.
- `MATTINGLY_LEVEL_3` (const): const MATTINGLY_LEVEL_3: GasTurbineComponents — Component technology level 3 (about 1965–1985) of Mattingly, *Elements of Propulsion* (2006), table 4.4: polytropic fan 0.86, compressor 0.88, cooled turbine 0.87, uncooled 0.89; burner 0.99 efficiency, 0.94 pressure ratio.
- `MATTINGLY_LEVEL_4` (const): const MATTINGLY_LEVEL_4: GasTurbineComponents — Component technology level 4 (about 1985–2005) of Mattingly's table 4.4: fan 0.89, compressor 0.90, turbines 0.89/0.90.
- `V2500_A1` (const): const V2500_A1: GasTurbineDesign — IAE V2500-A1 (A320), sized at sea-level static from Jenkinson, Simpkin & Rhodes, *Civil Jet Aircraft Design* (1999), engine data file: 781 lb/s, bypass ratio 5.4, overall pressure ratio 29.4. Fitted: turbine inlet temperature so take-off thrust is 25 000 lbf. The fan pressure ratio, 1.7, is an estimate (not published). Mattingly level 4 components; climb limited to 100% fan speed.
- `V2500_A1_PUBLISHED` (const): const V2500_A1_PUBLISHED: { takeoffThrust: number; takeoffTsfc: number; climbThrust: number; cruiseThrust: number; cruiseTsfc: number; cruiseAltitude: number; cruiseMach: number; } — IAE V2500-A1 figures from Jenkinson et al. (1999): take-off 25 000 lbf at 0.35 lb/(lbf·h) (ISA sea-level static); maximum climb 5620 lbf and cruise 5070 lbf at 0.581 lb/(lbf·h), both at 35 000 ft and Mach 0.8.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/rocket

- `EarthModel` (interface): interface EarthModel — An Earth: gravity with the J2 oblateness term, an ellipsoid surface for altitude, and a rotation rate.
- `GravityTurnProgram` (interface): interface GravityTurnProgram — A gravity-turn ascent: vertical rise, a pitch-over kick along the launch azimuth, then the axis follows the Earth-relative velocity.
- `Rocket` (interface): interface Rocket — A rocket in flight.
- `RocketAero` (interface): interface RocketAero — Axial-force coefficient by Mach number and the normal-force slope, for one stack configuration.
- `RocketControl` (interface): interface RocketControl — Gimbal commands, `-1..1` of the stage's largest angle: positive pitch turns the vehicle about body +y (nose toward −z), positive yaw about body +z (nose toward +y).
- `RocketDesign` (interface): interface RocketDesign — A vehicle: its stages from the first to burn upward, and a payload riding on top of the last one.
- `RocketEngine` (interface): interface RocketEngine — One engine. Thrust is given in vacuum; at altitude it loses ambient pressure times its nozzle exit area.
- `RocketLaunch` (interface): interface RocketLaunch — Where and how the vehicle stands at its first step.
- `RocketOptions` (interface): interface RocketOptions — Options: Earth and atmosphere models and the integration step.
- `RocketSample` (interface): interface RocketSample — One readout. Angles in rad, SI units; directions are inertial unit vectors.
- `RocketStage` (interface): interface RocketStage — A stage: a uniform cylinder of structure and propellant, its engines, and the aerodynamics of the stack it is the bottom of.
- `RocketState` (interface): interface RocketState — Serializable integrator state: position and velocity in Earth-centred inertial axes (z north, x through the launch meridian at `t = 0`).
- `RocketSteeringGains` (interface): interface RocketSteeringGains — Steering gains for {@link steerRocket}: attitude error and rate to gimbal command.
- `WGS84_EARTH` (const): const WGS84_EARTH: EarthModel — WGS 84 Earth (NIMA TR8350.2): μ, equatorial radius, flattening, J2 and rotation rate.
- `createRocket` (function): function createRocket(design: RocketDesign, launch: RocketLaunch, options: RocketOptions = {}): Rocket — Creates a {@link Rocket}: a 6-DOF rigid body in Earth-centred inertial axes on a rotating ellipsoidal Earth, gravity with J2, the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 moving with the Earth, stages that burn, lose mass and inertia and drop away, vacuum thrust less ambient pressure on each nozzle exit, gimballed engines on rate-limited actuators, jet damping, and axial and normal aerodynamic force through Mach. Each stage is a uniform cylinder, so the centre of mass and inertia follow the propellant down. RK4 over position, velocity, attitude quaternion, body rates, gimbal angles and propellant.
- `earthFixedToGeodetic` (function): function earthFixedToGeodetic(earth: EarthModel, point: readonly number[]): { latitude: number; longitude: number; altitude: number } — Geodetic latitude, longitude and height of an Earth-fixed point by Bowring's method (millimetre accurate near the surface).
- `earthGravity` (function): function earthGravity(earth: EarthModel, position: readonly number[], out: Vec3 = [0, 0, 0]): Vec3 — Gravitational acceleration with the J2 term, m/s², inertial axes with z along the rotation axis.
- `geodeticToEarthFixed` (function): function geodeticToEarthFixed(earth: EarthModel, latitude: number, longitude: number, altitude: number): Vec3 — Earth-centred Earth-fixed position of a geodetic point, m.
- `gravityTurnTarget` (function): function gravityTurnTarget(sample: RocketSample, program: GravityTurnProgram): Vec3 — Where a gravity-turn ascent points the vehicle axis at a sample: the local vertical, then tilted toward the azimuth through the kick, then along the Earth-relative velocity (zero angle of attack, the low-load path through max-Q).
- `steerRocket` (function): function steerRocket(sample: RocketSample, target: readonly number[], gains: RocketSteeringGains): RocketControl — Gimbal commands that turn the vehicle axis toward `target` (an inertial direction): proportional on the attitude error, damped on body rate, limited to `-1..1`.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/rocketComparison

- `compareRocketAscent` (function): function compareRocketAscent(tuning: RigidAircraftTuning = saturnVGameTuning(), name = "Saturn V S-IC (game motor build)"): ComparisonTable — Flies the Saturn V AS-506 S-IC ascent three ways and lines them up: the game's rigid-body `motor` model built from the published numbers ({@link saturnVGameTuning}), the reference rocket ({@link createRocket}), and the flight evaluation report. Both models fly the same gravity turn. The game model has a flat, non-rotating Earth, constant gravity, thrust that ignores ambient pressure and a drag area that ignores Mach, so its velocities are Earth-relative and it falls short of the real ascent; the rows show by how much.
- `saturnVGameTuning` (function): function saturnVGameTuning(): RigidAircraftTuning — The AS-506 S-IC flight as a game author would build it on {@link createRigidAircraft}'s `motor`: the published 34 MN liftoff thrust held to centre engine cutoff, then four fifths of it; the report's propellant and stage flow; the stage and upper stack as dry mass; the subsonic axial-force coefficient times the reference area as drag area.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/rotorcraftComparison

- `RotorcraftComparison` (interface): interface RotorcraftComparison — A game rotor's metrics beside the Bo-105 reference helicopter's and the measured Bo-105 rotor's.
- `RotorcraftComparisonAircraft` (interface): interface RotorcraftComparisonAircraft — A game rotorcraft to measure: its tuning, with a `rotor` block.
- `RotorcraftComparisonRow` (interface): interface RotorcraftComparisonRow — One metric: the game rotor, the Bo-105 reference and the NASA wind-tunnel figure; `real` is absent where none exists.
- `compareRotorcraft` (function): function compareRotorcraft(aircraft: readonly RotorcraftComparisonAircraft[]): RotorcraftComparison[] — Measures each game rotor (an {@link RigidAircraftTuning} `rotor` block) against the Bo-105 reference helicopter at the same normalised conditions: thrust at fixed collective climbing, descending, edgewise and in ground effect (all over hover thrust, speeds in hover induced velocities `v_h`), hover torque over thrust × radius, forward-flight power and rotor speed after an engine failure. Real values are the NASA TM-110356 Bo-105 full-scale rotor data. The game rotor has no power, so its power row is blank, and its rotor speed follows the throttle, so it cannot autorotate.

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/saturnV

- `F1_ENGINE` (const): const F1_ENGINE: RocketEngine — Rocketdyne F-1 as flown on AS-506, read from the flight evaluation report's S-IC stage performance (MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, figure 5-3): 34.0 MN stage thrust at liftoff and about 39.8 MN near vacuum give 6.80 MN per engine at sea level and 7.955 MN in vacuum, so an 11.4 m² exit area; the 2655 kg/s propellant flow per engine that empties the stage at 161.6 s gives a vacuum specific impulse of 305.5 s.
- `SATURN_V_AS506` (const): const SATURN_V_AS506: RocketDesign — Saturn V AS-506 (Apollo 11) through the S-IC burn, from its flight evaluation report (MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, 1969, public domain), tables 20-1 and 5-1: 2 899 008 kg at hold-down release, the S-IC's 2 071 716 kg of propellant used to outboard engine cutoff and its 168 015 kg at cutoff (structure and residuals), the 659 277 kg upper stack, centre engine cutoff at 135.2 s. Stage size is the published 42 m by 10.06 m; the axial-force coefficient through Mach, normal-force slope, centre of pressure and gimbal station are estimates for a finned cylinder of this shape, not measured Saturn V data.
- `SATURN_V_AS506_ASCENT` (const): const SATURN_V_AS506_ASCENT: GravityTurnProgram — A gravity turn standing in for the AS-506 tilt program: vertical to tower clearance and the roll, then a pitch-over whose size is the one free parameter, chosen so the flight path angle at outboard engine cutoff matches the report.
- `SATURN_V_AS506_EVENTS` (const): const SATURN_V_AS506_EVENTS: { readonly mach1: { readonly time: 66.3; readonly altitude: 7800; }; readonly maxDynamicPressure: { readonly time: 83; readonly pressure: 35200; readonly altitude: 13600; }; readonly centerEngineCutoff: { readonly time: 135.2; readonly altitude: 44000; readonly velocity:… — AS-506 measured trajectory events (MPR-SAT-FE-69-9 tables 4-1 and 4-2): times are range time, s; altitudes are metres; velocities are space-fixed, m/s; flight path angles are space-fixed, rad; surface range, m.
- `SATURN_V_AS506_LAUNCH` (const): const SATURN_V_AS506_LAUNCH: RocketLaunch — Launch Complex 39A, the Apollo 11 flight azimuth of 72.058°, the clock at hold-down release (0.3 s range time).

## @jgengine/core/flight/reference/standardAtmosphere

- `AtmosphereModel` (type): type AtmosphereModel = (altitude: number) => AtmosphereSample — An air model: geometric altitude above mean sea level, m, to the air state there.
- `AtmosphereSample` (interface): interface AtmosphereSample — Air state at one altitude, SI units.
- `SEA_LEVEL_DENSITY` (const): const SEA_LEVEL_DENSITY: 1.225 — Sea-level standard density, kg/m³.
- `SEA_LEVEL_PRESSURE` (const): const SEA_LEVEL_PRESSURE: 101325 — Sea-level standard pressure, Pa.
- `SEA_LEVEL_SPEED_OF_SOUND` (const): const SEA_LEVEL_SPEED_OF_SOUND: 340.294 — Sea-level standard speed of sound, m/s.
- `STANDARD_EARTH_RADIUS` (const): const STANDARD_EARTH_RADIUS: 6356766 — Effective Earth radius the 1976 standard uses for geopotential altitude and gravity, m.
- `STANDARD_GRAVITY` (const): const STANDARD_GRAVITY: 9.80665 — Standard sea-level gravity, m/s².
- `calibratedAirspeed` (function): function calibratedAirspeed(trueAirspeed: number, air: AtmosphereSample): number — Calibrated airspeed, m/s, for a true airspeed in an air state: the subsonic isentropic pitot relation referred to sea-level standard conditions, which is what an airspeed indicator without position error reads.
- `geopotentialAltitude` (function): function geopotentialAltitude(altitude: number): number — Geopotential altitude, m', of a geometric altitude, m.
- `standardAtmosphere` (function): function standardAtmosphere(altitude: number): AtmosphereSample — The U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (NOAA/NASA/USAF, NOAA-S/T 76-1562) from −5 km to 86 km geometric altitude: the seven geopotential layers with their molecular-scale temperature gradients, hydrostatic pressure, the molecular weight change between 80 and 86 km, the speed of sound and Sutherland's viscosity. Above 86 km it continues the 86 km layer isothermally, which the standard does not define.
- `standardGravity` (function): function standardGravity(altitude: number): number — Gravity at a geometric altitude, m/s², by the inverse-square law the 1976 standard uses.

## @jgengine/core/generator/generator

- `BakedGeneratorVariant` (interface): interface BakedGeneratorVariant<Schema extends ParamSchema, Output> — One baked variant: the variant and its output at each detail level, highest detail first.

- `GeneratorDefinition` (interface): interface GeneratorDefinition<Schema extends ParamSchema = ParamSchema, Output = unknown> — A procedural generator. `generate` must be pure: no `Math.random`, clock or global state, so a placed instance can store only its params and seed and regrow the same output anywhere.
- `GeneratorOutput` (type): type GeneratorOutput<Definition> = Definition extends GeneratorDefinition<ParamSchema, infer Output> ? Output : never — The output type of a generator.
- `GeneratorVariant` (interface): interface GeneratorVariant<Schema extends ParamSchema = ParamSchema> — One seeded variant: the `meta` it would write, and its parsed params and seed.
- `GeneratorVariantOptions` (interface): interface GeneratorVariantOptions — Options for {@link generatorVariants}.
- `RunGeneratorOptions` (interface): interface RunGeneratorOptions — Options for {@link runGenerator}.
- `bakeGeneratorVariants` (function): function bakeGeneratorVariants<Schema extends ParamSchema, Output>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, Output>, base: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined, options: GeneratorVariantOptions = {}): BakedGeneratorVariant<Schema, Output>[] — Bake N variants of a generator at each of its `lods` — the set an instanced renderer draws from (pick one per instance with {@link variantIndexAt}) and the editor's variant grid previews.
- `defineGenerator` (function): function defineGenerator<Schema extends ParamSchema, Output>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, Output>): GeneratorDefinition<Schema, Output> — Declare a generator with its schema and output types inferred.
- `generatorSeed` (function): function generatorSeed(schema: ParamSchema, meta: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined, fallback: string): string — The seed an object's `meta` resolves to: the schema's `seed` field when it is set, else a `meta.seed` string, else `fallback` (an editor object passes its id, so two objects differ).
- `generatorVariantFor` (function): function generatorVariantFor<Schema extends ParamSchema>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, unknown>, base: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined, key: string, options: Pick<GeneratorVariantOptions, "seed" | "explore"> = {}): GeneratorVariant<Schema> — The one variant of `base` that belongs to `key` (a placement id): its own seed, and params nudged by `explore` from a stream seeded by the key. The same key always gives the same variant, so a field can grow every placement as its own plant and regrow any of them anywhere.
- `generatorVariants` (function): function generatorVariants<Schema extends ParamSchema>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, unknown>, base: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined, options: GeneratorVariantOptions = {}): GeneratorVariant<Schema>[] — A grid of seeded variants around `base`: kept variants first, then the base itself, then fresh ones, each with its own seed and params nudged by `explore`. Pure — the same base and options always give the same grid, which is what the editor's variant panel and the `generator_variants` verb show.
- `getGenerator` (function): function getGenerator(id: string): GeneratorDefinition | undefined — The registered generator for an id, or undefined.
- `listGenerators` (function): function listGenerators(output?: string): GeneratorDefinition[] — Every registered generator, in registration order, optionally of one output family.
- `prepareGenerator` (function): function prepareGenerator<Schema extends ParamSchema, Output>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, Output>, meta: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined, options: RunGeneratorOptions = {}): Promise<void> — Await a generator's `prepare` for the output {@link runGenerator} would return with the same arguments. Resolves at once for a generator without one.
- `prepareGeneratorVariants` (function): function prepareGeneratorVariants<Schema extends ParamSchema, Output>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, Output>, base: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined, options: GeneratorVariantOptions = {}): Promise<void> — Await `prepare` for every variant and detail level {@link bakeGeneratorVariants} would bake with the same arguments, all at once, so a generator that prepares off the main thread (a worker pool) runs them in parallel and a bake right after it is fast.
- `registerGenerator` (function): function registerGenerator<Schema extends ParamSchema, Output>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, Output>): void — Register a generator so the editor, the asset catalog and agents can find it. Last registration per id wins.
- `runGenerator` (function): function runGenerator<Schema extends ParamSchema, Output>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, Output>, meta: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined, options: RunGeneratorOptions = {}): Output — Parse `meta` against the generator's schema, resolve its seed and generate.
- `untypedGenerator` (function): function untypedGenerator<Schema extends ParamSchema, Output>(definition: GeneratorDefinition<Schema, Output>): GeneratorDefinition — The untyped view of a typed generator, for code that holds raw meta bags (the editor, the variant grid): its `generate` parses params against the schema first. Registered generators are already this shape.
- `variantIndexAt` (function): function variantIndexAt(count: number, seed: string, key: string | number): number — A stable variant index in `[0, count)` for one placed instance key (an id, a grid cell).

## @jgengine/core/generator/paramSchema

- `ActionParamField` (interface): interface ActionParamField — A button row that runs a built-in inspector action on its group — currently `"randomize"` (reroll the group's numeric/seed/bool/select fields within their bounds) or `"reset"` (restore group defaults). Carries no persisted value; purely a control.
- `BoolParamField` (interface): interface BoolParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A checkbox.
- `ColorExplore` (interface): interface ColorExplore — How far variant exploration may shift a colour at full explore, so a variant keeps the colour's character instead of drifting to black or white.
- `ColorParamField` (interface): interface ColorParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A hex colour picker.
- `CurveParamField` (interface): interface CurveParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A curve over 0..1: control points the generator samples with {@link sampleCurve} (a height profile, a falloff, a density-by-distance ramp). `y` is clamped to `[min, max]`.
- `CurvePoint` (interface): interface CurvePoint — One control point of a `curve` param: `x` in 0..1 along the curve, `y` its value.
- `GradientParamField` (interface): interface GradientParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A colour ramp over 0..1 the generator samples with {@link sampleGradient}.
- `GradientStop` (interface): interface GradientStop — One stop of a `gradient` param: `at` in 0..1 and a hex colour.
- `NumberParamField` (interface): interface NumberParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A free numeric input, optionally clamped.
- `ParamField` (type): type ParamField = | RangeParamField | NumberParamField | BoolParamField | SelectParamField | ColorParamField | TextParamField | SeedParamField | WeightedListParamField | CurveParamField | GradientParamField | ActionParamField — One row in a parameter schema — the union the generic inspector knows how to render.
- `ParamGroup` (interface): interface ParamGroup — A named, optionally collapsed section the inspector groups fields under (by `field.group === id`).
- `ParamIssue` (interface): interface ParamIssue — One validation problem found by {@link validateParams}: which field and why.
- `ParamPreset` (interface): interface ParamPreset — A named slider/weight bundle — a saved set of field values the inspector (or the `apply_preset` verb) writes into an object's `meta` in one patch, ready to tweak afterwards. Presets are plain data on the schema, so a generator ships starting looks and games can override the registration.
- `ParamSchema` (interface): interface ParamSchema<Fields extends readonly ParamField[] = readonly ParamField[]> — A full parameter surface: an ordered list of fields the inspector renders top to bottom.
- `ParamValue` (type): type ParamValue<Field extends ParamField> = Field extends RangeParamField | NumberParamField ? number : Field extends BoolParamField ? boolean : Field extends SelectParamField ? Field["options"][number]["value"] : Field extends ColorParamField | TextParamField | SeedParamField ? string : Field exten… — The parsed value one field yields.
- `ParamsOf` (type): type ParamsOf<Schema extends ParamSchema> = string extends ValueField<Schema>["key"] ? ParsedParams : { [Field in ValueField<Schema> as Field["key"]]: ParamValue<Field> } — The typed params a schema parses to: one property per non-action field, keyed by its `key`. A schema declared with {@link defineParamSchema} keeps literal keys, so `ParamsOf<typeof SCHEMA>` is an exact object type; a plain `ParamSchema` falls back to {@link ParsedParams}.
- `ParsedParams` (type): type ParsedParams = Record<string, number | boolean | string | WeightedParamEntry[] | CurvePoint[] | GradientStop[]> — Parsed params after `parseParams` on an untyped schema: every field present, validated and defaulted.
- `RangeParamField` (interface): interface RangeParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A numeric slider row: bounded range with a live readout.
- `SeedParamField` (interface): interface SeedParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A seed string with a reroll button — same seed reproduces the same generated result.
- `SelectParamField` (interface): interface SelectParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A dropdown of fixed string options.
- `TextParamField` (interface): interface TextParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A free string input.
- `WeightedListParamField` (interface): interface WeightedListParamField extends ParamFieldBase — A repeatable list of weighted `{ item, weight }` rows (species palette, book set, …).
- `WeightedParamEntry` (interface): interface WeightedParamEntry — The typed parameter schema every generator and studio shares: an ordered list of fields (sliders, toggles, colours, enums, seeds, weighted lists, curves, gradients) in optionally nested groups, plus presets. One schema drives the editor inspector, `meta` parsing and validation, randomize and reset, and the seeded variant grid, so a new generator writes no UI or parsing code of its own. Declare a schema with {@link defineParamSchema} and {@link ParamsOf} gives the parsed params' type.
- `childParamGroups` (function): function childParamGroups(schema: ParamSchema, parent: string | undefined): ParamGroup[] — The groups nested directly under `parent` (top-level groups when `parent` is undefined), in declared order.
- `defineParamSchema` (function): function defineParamSchema<const Fields extends readonly ParamField[]>(schema: ParamSchema<Fields>): ParamSchema<Fields> — Declare a schema and keep its field keys and option values as literal types, so {@link ParamsOf} and {@link parseParams} return an exact params object instead of a loose record.
- `findSchemaPreset` (function): function findSchemaPreset(schema: ParamSchema, id: string): ParamPreset | undefined — Look up a schema preset by id, or undefined — the seam `apply_preset` and games resolve bundles through.
- `jitterParams` (function): function jitterParams(schema: ParamSchema, base: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined, random: () => number, amount: number): Record<string, unknown> — A `meta` patch that nudges every variable field of `base` by up to `amount` (0..1) of its range — the variant grid's "explore around this" step. Numbers move within their bounds, colours drift toward a random tone, bools and selects flip with probability `amount / 2`, curves move their points. Fields marked `vary: false`, seeds, text and weighted lists stay as they are.
- `parseParams` (function): function parseParams<Schema extends ParamSchema>(schema: Schema, meta: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined): ParamsOf<Schema> — Parse a raw `meta` bag against a schema into typed params — every field present, invalid or missing values replaced by the field default, numbers clamped to their range (and rounded when `step >= 1`), colours checked as hex. The single parser every generator and studio shares.
- `sampleCurve` (function): function sampleCurve(points: readonly CurvePoint[], x: number): number — The value of a curve at `x` (0..1), linear between control points and flat past the ends.
- `sampleGradient` (function): function sampleGradient(stops: readonly GradientStop[], t: number): string — The hex colour of a gradient at `t` (0..1), mixed between neighbouring stops.

## @jgengine/core/grass/GrassCover.draw

- `GrassCover` (function): function GrassCover({ area, seed, colorBase, colorTip, strength, edgeFeather, heightAt, coverageAt, segments, lift, stripeAt, position, }: GrassCoverProps): React.JSX.Element | null — The turf surface under one authored `grass_field` patch: a ground-draped, edge-feathered mat that turns a bare pavement footprint into grass the blade field stands in. Bounded to one draw and a {@link GRASS_COVER_MAX_SEGMENTS}² grid, so a large park still costs a single mesh.
- `GrassCoverProps` (interface): interface GrassCoverProps — Props for {@link GrassCover}: one authored patch's footprint, colours and drape samplers.

## @jgengine/core/grass/GrassPatch.draw

- `GrassPatch` (function): function GrassPatch({ look, area, seed, edgeFeather, exclude, heightAt, coverageAt, baseHeight, groundColor, castShadow = false, receiveShadow = true, frustumCulled = true, ...groupProps }: GrassPatchProps): React.JSX.Element — The engine's one grass renderer: a camera-streamed blade field over a turf mat. Work follows the camera — nodes near it bake every tuft, far ones a thinning share, and nothing past the distance where a blade would be under a pixel — so a patch of any size costs what the view shows.

## @jgengine/core/grass/grassBake.draw

- `GRASS_CELL_SIZE` (const): const GRASS_CELL_SIZE: 8 — Side of one base grass cell in metres: the unit of seeded tuft generation. Coarser stream nodes cover power-of-two blocks of cells.
- `GrassBakeOptions` (interface): interface GrassBakeOptions — Inputs for {@link resolveGrassBake}: one patch's look, footprint and ground samplers.
- `GrassExclusion` (interface): interface GrassExclusion — A rectangle (patch-local XZ) the grass keeps clear — soil patches, water, plazas.
- `GrassTufts` (interface): interface GrassTufts — The tufts one stream node draws, sorted by rank. A tuft's rank is its place in its cell's seeded order, so the first `n` tufts are an even thinning of the node: drawing fewer for a far camera just shortens the instance count, and a finer node re-baked nearer the camera regrows the same tufts in the same places.
- `ResolvedGrassBake` (interface): interface ResolvedGrassBake — A patch ready to bake: the look plus every derived number the bake and stream share.
- `bakeGrassNode` (function): function bakeGrassNode(bake: ResolvedGrassBake, level: number, ix: number, iz: number, share: number): GrassTufts — Seeded tufts for one stream node at `share` of full detail (0..1]. Each base cell inside the node grows its own seeded sequence, so the result never depends on which node asked or how big it is.
- `grassFieldColors` (function): function grassFieldColors(look: GrassLook): { base: THREE.Color; tip: THREE.Color } — The look's colours after season and dryness, as the turf mat and far field show them. Mirrors the blade shader's colour path at the field's average tone.
- `grassNodeRect` (function): function grassNodeRect(bake: ResolvedGrassBake, level: number, ix: number, iz: number): [number, number, number, number] — Patch-local XZ rectangle a node covers, clipped to the patch: `[x0, z0, x1, z1]`.
- `grassTuftsBelow` (function): function grassTuftsBelow(ranks: Float32Array, share: number): number — Number of sorted tufts whose rank is below `share`.
- `resolveGrassBake` (function): function resolveGrassBake(options: GrassBakeOptions): ResolvedGrassBake — Resolve a patch's bake inputs once; the stream and every node bake read the result.

Detail picks the blade segments (4 at full detail, 2 at half, 1 at a quarter), so a baked variant carries its LODs.
- `GRASS_PRESETS` (const): const GRASS_PRESETS: { id: string; label: string; values: { density: number; bladeHeight: number; heightVariation: number; bladeWidth: number; widthVariation: number; profile: number; curvature: number; stiffness: number; tuftSpread: number; tuftBlades: number; baseColor: string; tipColor: string; g… — Starting looks the inspector applies in one click; each is a full knob set, so any can be tweaked from there.

- `GrassLook` (interface): interface GrassLook — Fully-defaulted, clamped grass look, read from a volume's `meta` or a `grass()` config.
- `ResolvedGrass` (interface): interface ResolvedGrass — A resolved grass patch: world-space area center at ground height, footprint size (XZ), and look.
- `grassBladeDensity` (function): function grassBladeDensity(look: GrassLook): number — Blades per square metre at full detail. Fullness sets how much of the ground the blades cover, and the count follows from blade size: thin or short blades need more of them to cover the same ground, so no width, height or fullness can leave bare gaps between tufts.

## @jgengine/core/grass/grassStream.draw

- `GRASS_SCREEN_DENSITY` (const): const GRASS_SCREEN_DENSITY: number — Blades per CSS pixel² the field aims for beyond the near zone. Inside the zone every tuft draws; past it the share falls with the square of distance, so the blades on screen stay about constant however far the field runs and however dense the look is.
- `GrassStream` (class): class GrassStream — Camera-streamed grass for one patch. A quadtree over the patch's base cells splits near the camera and stays coarse far away; each leaf node bakes only the share of tufts its distance needs, so resident and drawn work follow what the camera sees rather than the patch area. Leaves are three meshes under {@link GrassStream.group}; three frustum-culls them per camera, and each draw trims its instance count and segment detail to that camera's distance.
- `GrassStreamOptions` (interface): interface GrassStreamOptions — Options for {@link GrassStream}.
- `GrassStreamStats` (interface): interface GrassStreamStats — Per-frame bookkeeping the stream reports, for tests and devtools.

- `ActionBinding` (interface): interface ActionBinding<TCode extends string = string> — Action-binding model: games bind semantic actions ("jump", "interact") to physical control codes; capture layers resolve raw events through this map so gameplay code never sees keycodes. In a `defineGame({ input })`, pressing an action runs the same-named command with `{ yaw, pitch, aim, held }`; `repeatMs` re-fires it while held (automatic weapons), with `held: true` on those re-fires so one binding can drive a single-shot pistol (ignore `held`) and an automatic rifle (accept it).

- `ActionStateTracker` (interface): interface ActionStateTracker<TAction extends string> { handleDown(code: string): TAction | null; handleUp(code: string): TAction | null; isDown(action: TAction): boolean; wasPressed(action: TAction): boolean; endFrame(): void; reset(): void; rebind(map: ActionStateBindingMap<TAction, string>)… — ⚠ undocumented · used by `rebindGamepadPoll` (@jgengine/core/input/gamepadPoll): Swap the pad bindings mid-game (a context push) without touching keyboard state: release the codes of pad-held actions whose pad codes chang…
- `DEFAULT_DRIVE_CODES` (const): const DEFAULT_DRIVE_CODES: { readonly throttle: readonly ["KeyW", "ArrowUp"]; readonly brake: readonly ["KeyS", "ArrowDown"]; readonly steerLeft: readonly ["KeyA", "ArrowLeft"]; readonly steerRight: readonly ["KeyD", "ArrowRight"]; readonly handbrake: readonly ["Space"]; } — Stock keyboard codes for driving a vehicle: WASD or the arrows for throttle, brake and steering, Space for the handbrake. Spread it as the base of a racing map and override what the game uses differently (`input: { ...DEFAULT_DRIVE_CODES, handbrake: ["KeyX"], hop: ["Space"] }`).
- `DEFAULT_WALK_CODES` (const): const DEFAULT_WALK_CODES: { readonly moveForward: readonly ["KeyW"]; readonly moveBack: readonly ["KeyS"]; readonly moveLeft: readonly ["KeyA"]; readonly moveRight: readonly ["KeyD"]; readonly jump: readonly ["Space"]; } — Stock keyboard codes for the shell walk controller: WASD to move, Space to jump. Spread it as the base of a game's map (`input: { ...DEFAULT_WALK_CODES, sprint: ["ShiftLeft"], interact: ["KeyE"] }`) instead of re-typing the same five bindings in every game.

- `hotbarSlotBindings` (function): function hotbarSlotBindings(count: number, options?: { action?: (slot: number) => string }): ActionCodesMap — Number-row bindings for `count` numbered actions: slot 1 on Digit1 through slot 10 on Digit0. Name the actions with `action` (`hotbarSlotBindings(4, { action: (slot) => `buildTower${slot}` })`); the default names are `hotbarSlot1`…, which the shell routes to the hotbar on its own.

It maps the classic control- group idiom — Ctrl+digit binds, digit recalls, a second digit tap within a window focuses — onto opaque bookmark keys, without pulling input mapping into the store. Games that want a different scheme (named bookmarks, gamepad, touch) skip this and call the store directly.

The `data-jg-kbd-hint` marker is also hidden by an engine stylesheet as a hydration-safe backstop, so a hint stays hidden on touch even before this component's effect runs. Put the touch equivalent (a `TouchControls` dock, a tappable button) on the coarse branch instead.

## @jgengine/core/input/rebindSession

- `RebindActionConfig` (interface): interface RebindActionConfig — One rebindable action as declared to {@link createRebindSession}. The `id` and `label` are FREE strings the session never interprets — the game owns their meaning and display text. `defaultCodes` is the authored binding the session resets back to.
- `RebindConflict` (interface): interface RebindConflict — A group of actions bound to the same normalized code — the conflict this session detects.
- `RebindRow` (interface): interface RebindRow — One controls-list row: an action, its effective binding, and any conflicts.
- `RebindSession` (interface): interface RebindSession — A live, observable, conflict-aware key-remap editor over the action-binding model.
- `RebindSessionActionsConfig` (interface): interface RebindSessionActionsConfig extends RebindSessionCommon — Declare actions explicitly, in list order.
- `RebindSessionConfig` (type): type RebindSessionConfig = RebindSessionActionsConfig | RebindSessionMapConfig — Config for {@link createRebindSession}: an explicit action list, or an {@link ActionCodesMap} + labels.
- `RebindSessionMapConfig` (interface): interface RebindSessionMapConfig extends RebindSessionCommon — Declare actions from an authored {@link ActionCodesMap}, labelled by `labels` (falling back to the id).
- `RebindSessionSnapshot` (interface): interface RebindSessionSnapshot — Serializable session state for save/restore.
- `createRebindSession` (function): function createRebindSession(config: RebindSessionConfig): RebindSession — A conflict-aware key-remap session over the action-binding model — the missing editor behind a controls-settings menu. It takes the game's authored actions ({@link RebindActionConfig}s, or an {@link ActionCodesMap} + labels) plus the player's saved {@link BindingOverrides}, and tracks the *effective* binding per action (default merged with the override via `applyBindingOverrides`). `rows()` exposes each action's label, current key glyph (via `bindingLabel`), whether it is still the default, and which other actions it collides with; `conflicts()` groups every action pair sharing a normalized code (the value-add a raw override map can't give you). `beginCapture`/`capture`/`cancelCapture` drive a "press a key" rebind (codes normalized via `normalizeKeyCode`), `reset`/ `resetAll` return to defaults, and `overrides()`/`apply()` hand the caller the `BindingOverrides` to persist. Nothing here is genre-specific: action ids and labels are free strings the session never interprets, and hold/toggle/repeat binding shapes survive a rebind. `snapshot`/`restore` round-trips the editor (including the in-flight capture) through a save.

## @jgengine/core/instancing/instanceCells

- `InstanceCell` (interface): interface InstanceCell<T> — Spatial cells for instanced draws: bucket placements into a uniform XZ grid so a dense field renders as many small draw units instead of one huge mesh. Each cell carries its own bounds, is frustum-culled on its own, and costs nothing offscreen. Pure and deterministic.
- `groupInstancesByCell` (function): function groupInstancesByCell<T>(items: readonly T[], cellSize: number, at: (item: T) => readonly [number, number]): InstanceCell<T>[] — Bucket `items` into `cellSize`-meter XZ cells by the point `at` returns for each. Empty cells are omitted; cells come out row-major by grid coordinate (z rows, then x) and items keep their input order, so the result is deterministic.

## @jgengine/core/interaction/interactionPrompt.view

- `InteractionPrompt` (function): function InteractionPrompt({ registry, playerPosition, theme, accentFor, keyFor, gaugeProgress, anchor = "bottom-center", zIndex = 40, className, style, }: InteractionPromptProps): ReactNode — A screen-anchored "Press E to …" interaction callout that renders the active prompt of a {@link PromptRegistry}. It subscribes to the registry and — when given `playerPosition` — re-resolves as the hero moves, showing the nearest in-range interactable and switching to a closer/higher-priority one as they cross radii. Each display kind renders as itself: a `keybind` shows a key cap plus its label ("Press [E] Open"), a `gauge` shows a hold bar filling with `gaugeProgress`, and a `label` shows plain text. Presentation only — the registry never branches on a prompt's meaning; the game colors each via `accentFor` and maps action ids to key glyphs via `keyFor`. HudTheme-skinnable through `--jg-accent` and {@link InteractionPromptTheme}.
- `InteractionPromptAnchor` (type): type InteractionPromptAnchor = "bottom-center" | "top-center" | "center" — Where the callout sits over the scene.
- `InteractionPromptProps` (interface): interface InteractionPromptProps — Props for {@link InteractionPrompt}.
- `InteractionPromptTheme` (interface): interface InteractionPromptTheme — Reskin tokens for {@link InteractionPrompt}.
- `useInteractionPrompt` (function): function useInteractionPrompt(registry: PromptRegistry, playerPosition: PromptPoint): PositionedPrompt | null — Subscribe to a {@link PromptRegistry} and re-`resolve` it whenever the player moves, returning the prompt to draw right now — or `null` when the player is out of range of every interactable. The registry notifies only on active-prompt *changes*, so this re-renders on transitions rather than every frame the hero moves. Feed it the player's `{ x, z }` position each frame; identical positions do no work.

- `LockAction` (type): type LockAction = "hardSet" | "set" | "steady" | "ease" | "drop" — One discrete pick move: how far the pick drives into the lock this step.

- `LockSpec` (interface): interface LockSpec — A generated lock board. `open[col]` holds every enterable row in that column.
- `LockStepResult` (type): type LockStepResult = "advanced" | "slip" | "bind" | "trap" | "success" — Outcome of one {@link stepLock} call: `advanced`/`success` move the pick, `slip`/`bind`/`trap` do not and should cost a life.
- `LockTierSpec` (interface): interface LockTierSpec — Difficulty dials for one lock: board size, forgiveness band, gates, fog window, traps.

Deterministic: the same (seed, tier) always yields the same board.

- `solveLockPath` (function): function solveLockPath(spec: LockSpec): number[] | null — Return a concrete row-per-column solution, or null if the board is unsolvable.

The caller owns the lives economy: a slip/bind/trap does not advance the pick and should cost a life; advanced/success move the pick.
- `visibleCells` (function): function visibleCells(spec: LockSpec, col: number, window: number): LockCell[] — The render-safe slice: every open cell in columns [0, col + window]. The single source of truth for fog and the anti-cheat boundary — never serialize the full spec to a client.

## @jgengine/core/interaction/promptRegistry

- `PositionedPromptPatch` (type): type PositionedPromptPatch = Partial<Omit<PositionedPrompt, "id">> — A partial edit applied to an already-registered {@link PositionedPrompt} by {@link PromptRegistry.update}. Any subset of the mutable fields — everything but the stable `id` — may be supplied; omitted fields keep their prior value.
- `PromptRegistry` (interface): interface PromptRegistry — A live, observable set of interaction prompts that OWNS the registered {@link PositionedPrompt}s and tracks which one is active for a player. It is a thin stateful layer over {@link resolveActivePrompt}: registration/order lives here, the nearest-within-radius / higher-priority selection stays in the pure resolver. {@link resolve} is the per-frame hot path — call it as the player moves; subscribers fire only when the active prompt actually CHANGES.
- `PromptRegistrySnapshot` (interface): interface PromptRegistrySnapshot — The serializable shape {@link PromptRegistry.snapshot} returns and {@link PromptRegistry.restore} consumes: the full set of positioned prompts (in registration order) plus the id of the prompt that was active when the snapshot was taken. Prompt display/command payloads are free strings and ids — keep them serializable and this round-trips through a save cleanly.
- `createPromptRegistry` (function): function createPromptRegistry(): PromptRegistry — Create a live, observable interaction-prompt registry over the pure {@link resolveActivePrompt} resolver. Register positioned "press E" prompts, `resolve(playerPosition)` each frame as the hero moves, and read `active()` — the nearest strictly-in-range prompt (higher `priority` beats closer). The set is owned here (register/update/unregister/clear/all); selection stays pure. Subscribers are notified only when the active prompt *changes*, so a HUD does not thrash per frame, and `snapshot`/`restore` round-trip the prompts plus the active id through a save (display payloads are free strings/ids the game owns — the registry never branches on their meaning). Allocation-aware: `all()` and `resolve()` reuse a cached array instead of rebuilding per call.

## @jgengine/core/lighting/lightProbes

- `IrradianceBakeInput` (interface): interface IrradianceBakeInput — Everything a bake needs for one volume: where the grid sits, how much sky reaches it, and what fills the dark.
- `IrradianceBakeSettings` (interface): interface IrradianceBakeSettings — Authored bake inputs stored beside the samples so a volume can be re-baked without the editor.
- `IrradianceVolume` (interface): interface IrradianceVolume — One irradiance volume authored on a scene document.

- `SH_COEFFICIENTS` (const): const SH_COEFFICIENTS: 9 — Baked irradiance volume: a grid of second-order (9-coefficient, RGB) spherical-harmonic probes over a box region, sampled at runtime for ambient lighting. It is the datum an interior has that a hemisphere light cannot: a room's fill is its own, not the sky's, and it varies across the space.
- `bakeIrradianceVolume` (function): function bakeIrradianceVolume(input: IrradianceBakeInput): IrradianceVolume — Bakes an irradiance volume from authored inputs: sky radiance where the region is open, an authored ceiling/floor fill where it is enclosed, plus inverse-square lamp radiance. Each probe projects its directional radiance into L2 SH, so ambient varies across the grid and keeps a lit side instead of flattening to one number.

Returns the input unchanged when there is nothing to adjust.

The editor runs this as a bake action and stores the result on the scene document; runtime feeds it straight into the existing `Minimap` / `WorldMap` `background` + `mapBounds` props — no new runtime render path, and the same authored world always bakes the same image (safe for verify/CI). Deterministic for a fixed source. The bounds are preserved so a player-centered minimap pans the image correctly.

## @jgengine/core/math/linearAlgebra

- `Eigenvalue` (interface): interface Eigenvalue — One eigenvalue `re + i·im`, 1/s for a linearised plant.
- `matrixEigenvalues` (function): function matrixEigenvalues(matrix: ArrayLike<number>, n: number): Eigenvalue[] — Eigenvalues of a real square matrix (row-major, `n × n`): balancing, reduction to upper Hessenberg form by stabilised elimination, then the Francis double-shift QR iteration (Wilkinson & Reinsch, *Handbook for Automatic Computation* II, the EISPACK `balanc`/`elmhes`/`hqr` scheme). Complex pairs come out together. The input is not modified. Sorted by real part, then imaginary part, descending.
- `solveLinearSystem` (function): function solveLinearSystem(m: Float64Array, b: Float64Array, n: number): void — Solve `m·x = b` in place (n×n, row-major; `m` is overwritten and `b` becomes `x`) by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. A singular pivot leaves that unknown at `0`.

## @jgengine/core/movement/formation

- `BoxFormationOptions` (interface): interface BoxFormationOptions — Options for {@link boxFormation}.
- `CircleFormationOptions` (interface): interface CircleFormationOptions — Options for {@link circleFormation}.
- `FormationSlotGenerator` (type): type FormationSlotGenerator = (count: number) => Vec2[] — Produces `count` slot offsets in the group's local frame — `[right, forward]` where `+forward` points where the group faces. Index order is the slot order; a generator must be pure (same `count` → same offsets) so placement stays deterministic. Sample generators below cover common shapes; games pass their own for anything else (crowds, convoys, sports positions) with no engine edit.
- `LineFormationOptions` (interface): interface LineFormationOptions — Options for {@link lineFormation}.
- `SlotAssignmentOptions` (interface): interface SlotAssignmentOptions — Tuning for {@link assignFormationSlots}' stable, low-churn matching.
- `WedgeFormationOptions` (interface): interface WedgeFormationOptions — Options for {@link wedgeFormation}.
- `assignFormationSlots` (function): function assignFormationSlots(members: readonly Vec2[], slots: readonly Vec2[], options: SlotAssignmentOptions = {}): number[] — Match `members` to `slots` by a deterministic greedy nearest assignment: every (member, slot) pair is ranked by squared travel distance (minus a stickiness bonus for a member's previous slot) and assigned in order while both ends are free. Returns `assignment[member] = slot`, or `-1` for members left unmatched when there are fewer slots than members. Ties break by member then slot index, so the result is stable across runs and independent of input ordering — the property replay and lockstep multiplayer rely on. Groups are bounded, so the `O(members·slots·log)` sort is fine; this is not a per-frame whole-world pass.
- `boxFormation` (function): function boxFormation(options: BoxFormationOptions): FormationSlotGenerator — A rectangular grid centered on the destination, front row toward `+forward` — a marching block or a phalanx. Rows fill front-to-back, left-to-right.
- `circleFormation` (function): function circleFormation(options: CircleFormationOptions): FormationSlotGenerator — An evenly spaced ring around the destination — a guard cordon, a huddle, or a surround. Slot 0 sits `startAngle` from forward; slots advance evenly around the circle.
- `facingYaw` (function): function facingYaw(from: Vec2, to: Vec2): number — Engine yaw (`rotationY`, radians) that faces from `from` toward `to` on the XZ plane, matching the `forward = (sin yaw, cos yaw)` convention. Feed the result as the `facing` of {@link placeFormation} to orient a formation along its travel direction. Returns `0` when the points coincide.
- `lineFormation` (function): function lineFormation(options: LineFormationOptions): FormationSlotGenerator — A single rank abreast, centered on the destination and facing forward — a skirmish line or a chorus row. Slots run left→right along the group's right axis.
- `placeFormation` (function): function placeFormation(destination: Vec2, facing: number, count: number, generator: FormationSlotGenerator): Vec2[] — Transform a generator's local slot offsets into world XZ positions around a `destination`, rotated by `facing` (engine yaw). Slot `i` in the returned array is `generator(count)[i]` mapped through the group frame, so it stays aligned with {@link assignFormationSlots}' slot indices. Pure and allocation- light: one array of `count` points, no per-call closures retained.
- `wedgeFormation` (function): function wedgeFormation(options: WedgeFormationOptions): FormationSlotGenerator — A "V"/arrowhead with the apex at the destination and arms trailing back — a flying-wedge charge or a goose skein. Slot 0 is the tip; later slots alternate right then left, each rank stepping one `spacing` outward and backward.

- `MovementReport` (interface): interface MovementReport — Deterministic walk-feel metrics. `Infinity` means the target was never reached.
- `measureMovement` (function): function measureMovement(subject: MovementProbeSubject = {}, options: MovementProbeOptions = {}): MovementReport — Drives a walk character through fixed scenarios (standing start, release to stop, reversal, a standing jump, a tapped jump, a strafed jump) on the same integrator `stepPlayerMovement` uses, and reports the feel metrics a test can assert. Deterministic: the same subject and options always produce the same report, so a feel change shows up as a number moving. Collision, terrain and swimming are out of scope; it measures flat ground.

## @jgengine/core/movement/movementSpeed

- `MovementSpeedConfig` (interface): interface MovementSpeedConfig { baseSpeed: number; multiplierStat?: string; flatBonusStat?: string } — ⚠ undocumented · used by `applyStatDrivenSpeed`: Recomputes `movement.walkSpeed` for an entity from its stats and writes it back via `deps.entities.update`.
- `MovementSpeedDeps` (interface): interface MovementSpeedDeps { stats: {get(instanceId: string, statId: string): StatValue | null}; entities: {get(id: string): {movement?: {walkSpeed?: number}} | null; update(id: string, patch: {movement: {walkSpeed: number}}): boolean;} } — ⚠ undocumented · used by `applyStatDrivenSpeed`: Recomputes `movement.walkSpeed` for an entity from its stats and writes it back via `deps.entities.update`.
- `MovementSpeedModifiers` (interface): interface MovementSpeedModifiers { multiplier?: number | undefined; flatBonus?: number | undefined } — ⚠ undocumented · used by `deriveWalkSpeed`: `base * (multiplier ?? 1) + (flatBonus ?? 0)`, clamped to never go negative.
- `applyStatDrivenSpeed` (function): function applyStatDrivenSpeed(deps: MovementSpeedDeps, instanceId: string, config: MovementSpeedConfig): boolean — Recomputes `movement.walkSpeed` for an entity from its stats and writes it back via `deps.entities.update`. Either stat id is optional; an omitted or unresolved stat contributes its neutral value (multiplier 1, flat bonus 0) rather than failing. Returns false only when the entity itself doesn't exist.
- `deriveWalkSpeed` (function): function deriveWalkSpeed(base: number, modifiers: MovementSpeedModifiers): number — `base * (multiplier ?? 1) + (flatBonus ?? 0)`, clamped to never go negative.

## @jgengine/core/movement/playerMovement

- `PlayerMovementSnapshot` (interface): interface PlayerMovementSnapshot — One player's serializable movement state: heading, facing, velocities, jump latch and controller capsule. The entity pose lives in the entity store.
- `PlayerMovementTelemetry` (interface): interface PlayerMovementTelemetry — Last completed shared movement step for one entity; a live read-only view, not a save snapshot.
- `PlayerMovementTuning` (interface): interface PlayerMovementTuning — The resolved, per-world movement configuration {@link stepPlayerMovement} integrates against — the same inputs the shell FrameDriver used to read piecemeal, gathered into one struct so single-player and host movement run identical math.
- `forgetPlayerMovement` (function): function forgetPlayerMovement(ctx: GameContext, userId: string): void — Drop a player's retained movement state (heading + kinematic body) — call on leave so a rejoin starts fresh instead of resuming stale velocity.
- `playerMovementHeading` (function): function playerMovementHeading(ctx: GameContext, userId: string): number — One player's current heading (radians), integrated by {@link stepPlayerMovement} — the shell reads it back into its camera/aim yaw.
- `playerMovementTelemetry` (function): function playerMovementTelemetry(ctx: GameContext, entityId: string): Readonly<PlayerMovementTelemetry> | null — Read the entity's last shared movement result through indexed possession ownership. Returns `null` before a step, after movement restore/forget, when a commit policy replaces the motor proposal, or for an entity not currently driven by this motor. Reuses one live view; custom movers supply their own animation parameters. Flight never reports ground contact or a walking crouch.
- `resolvePhysicsTuning` (function): function resolvePhysicsTuning(physics: PhysicsConfig | undefined): MovementTuningOverrides | undefined — Maps a game's declared `physics` onto the movement controllers' tuning. `PhysicsConfig.gravity` is a signed world acceleration (negative points down), but the controllers integrate `velocityY -= gravityAcceleration * dt` and expect a positive downward magnitude — so gravity is negated here to keep down-pointing gravity pulling down.
- `resolvePlayerMovementTuning` (function): function resolvePlayerMovementTuning(opts: { collision?: VoxelCollisionConfig | undefined; movement?: PlayerMovementConfig | undefined; physics?: PhysicsConfig | undefined; world?: WorldFeature | undefined; }): PlayerMovementTuning — Gather a game's collision/movement/physics/world config into a {@link PlayerMovementTuning} — call once per world; both the shell and a host pass the result to {@link stepPlayerMovement}.
- `restorePlayerMovement` (function): function restorePlayerMovement(ctx: GameContext, userId: string, snapshot: PlayerMovementSnapshot): void — Put a player's movement state back to a {@link snapshotPlayerMovement} copy. Pending state survives until first spawn; a driven actor's despawn clears it.
- `snapshotPlayerMovement` (function): function snapshotPlayerMovement(ctx: GameContext, userId: string): PlayerMovementSnapshot | null — Copy one player's movement state for prediction, rollback or a save; `null` when the player has not moved yet.
- `stepPlayerMovement` (function): function stepPlayerMovement(ctx: GameContext, userId: string, input: InputFrame, dt: number, tuning: PlayerMovementTuning, heading?: number, pitch?: number): void — Integrate one player's movement for a tick from their held-input frame and commit the pose — the single genre-agnostic controller both the shell (its local player) and a host (each connected player in `onTick`) call, so single-player and server-authoritative movement are identical. Reads the player's controlled entity, terrain, scene solids, and pending motion impulses; writes the entity pose via `setPose`. Retains heading + kinematic body per `userId` on the `ctx`. Pass `heading` to override the internally-integrated yaw (the shell owns yaw for its camera); omit it and the controller turns from the frame's `turnLeft`/`turnRight` actions. Pass `pitch` for 6DOF spectator flight when `alignWithLook` is set.
