## @jgengine/core/movement/solidObstacles

- `ObstacleReach` (interface): interface ObstacleReach — Largest blocking-collider extent in the scene, split so tower height cannot inflate the XZ query.
- `ObstacleReachCache` (interface): interface ObstacleReachCache — Mutable reach cache; one per source, invalidated by object count or by the source's version.
- `SolidObstacleSource` (interface): interface SolidObstacleSource — The slice of the scene's object store this query needs. Narrow on purpose: the scene context wires its own store here while it is still being constructed, `ctx.scene.object` satisfies it as-is, and a pure rules package with no `GameContext` to import can satisfy it from its own object list.
- `createObstacleReachCache` (function): function createObstacleReachCache(): ObstacleReachCache — A fresh {@link ObstacleReachCache} for a caller that owns its own source.
- `obstacleFromSolid` (function): function obstacleFromSolid(solid: WorldSolid): CollisionObstacle — A {@link WorldSolid} as a {@link CollisionObstacle}. Axis-aligned solids are one box; a yawed solid is cut into strips along its long axis, each fitted with an AABB, so a turned building does not block the street beside it the way a single enclosing box would.
- `resolveSourceWalkerStep` (function): function resolveSourceWalkerStep(source: SolidObstacleSource, cache: ObstacleReachCache, position: EntityPosition, stepX: number, stepZ: number, options: { radius?: number; stepUpHeight?: number } = {}): { stepX: number; stepZ: number } — {@link resolveWalkerStep} with no `GameContext`: gather plus slide against a bare {@link SolidObstacleSource} and a caller-owned {@link ObstacleReachCache}.
- `resolveWalkerStep` (function): function resolveWalkerStep(ctx: GameContext, position: EntityPosition, stepX: number, stepZ: number, options: { radius?: number; stepUpHeight?: number } = {}): { stepX: number; stepZ: number } — Slide a walker's horizontal step against the same solid geometry that stops the player, returning the X/Z it may actually take this tick. A step into a wall is cut on the blocked axis and preserved on the other, exactly as {@link stepPlayerMovement} resolves the player's.
- `slideStep` (function): function slideStep(position: EntityPosition, stepX: number, stepZ: number, obstacles: readonly CollisionObstacle[], radius = DEFAULT_OBSTACLE_PLAYER_RADIUS, stepUpHeight = 0): { stepX: number; stepZ: number } — {@link resolveWalkerStep} against an already-gathered obstacle set.
- `solidObstaclesNear` (function): function solidObstaclesNear(ctx: GameContext, position: EntityPosition, reachX: number, reachZ: number, height = WALKER_HEIGHT): CollisionObstacle[] — Every blocking physical obstacle overlapping the box `position` ± `reachX`/`reachZ`, read from the scene's resolved colliders and `ctx.world.solids`.
- `sourceObstacleReach` (function): function sourceObstacleReach(source: SolidObstacleSource, cache: ObstacleReachCache): ObstacleReach — {@link solidObstacleReach} against a bare source and caller-owned cache.
- `sourceObstaclesNear` (function): function sourceObstaclesNear(source: SolidObstacleSource, reach: ObstacleReach, position: EntityPosition, reachX: number, reachZ: number, height = WALKER_HEIGHT, cache?: ObstacleReachCache): CollisionObstacle[] — {@link solidObstaclesNear} against a bare source and an already-resolved reach. Pass the source's {@link ObstacleReachCache} to use the version-keyed obstacle index; a source that reports no `version()` keeps the per-query `inBox` gather.

## @jgengine/core/movement/steering

- `YawVectorXZ` (type): type YawVectorXZ = readonly [number, number] — Yaw-frame steering math. The engine's heading convention is `forward = (sin yaw, cos yaw)` on the XZ plane with +Y up, which makes a positive yaw increment rotate counterclockwise seen from above — a turn to the entity's LEFT on screen. Every hand-written `heading += steer * rate * dt` therefore turns the wrong way; integrate steering through `steerYaw` instead.
- `steerToward` (function): function steerToward(yaw: number, desiredYaw: number): number — Signed steer-right input that closes on `desiredYaw` when integrated through `steerYaw` — the seek half every AI driver and homing script needs. Magnitude is the wrapped radian error in (−π, π]; scale and clamp it into [-1, 1] at the call site.
- `steerYaw` (function): function steerYaw(yaw: number, steerRight: number, turnRatePerSecond: number, dt: number): number — Integrate one steering step. `steerRight` is the signed steer input (+1 = turn right, matching `DRIVE_AXIS_BINDINGS`' KeyD/ArrowRight), `turnRatePerSecond` is radians per second at full lock. Steering right decreases yaw in the engine frame; this helper owns that sign so game code never re-derives it.
- `yawForward` (function): function yawForward(yaw: number): YawVectorXZ — XZ forward direction of a yaw (`rotationY`): `(sin yaw, cos yaw)`.
- `yawRight` (function): function yawRight(yaw: number): YawVectorXZ — XZ screen-right of a yaw — `forward × up` with up = +Y: `(-cos yaw, sin yaw)`.

## @jgengine/core/movement/teleport

- `teleportPlayer` (function): function teleportPlayer(ctx: GameContext, userId: string, to: TeleportTarget): string | null — Move a player to a point in one frame: the body they control (their mount while riding, so the rider comes along on the seat), facing `yaw`, with the camera swung round behind. The walk controller's carried velocity and capsule are dropped so the next step starts from rest at the new spot instead of pulling the body back, and the renderer snaps rather than gliding across the map. Returns the id of the entity that moved, or `null` when the player has no body yet.

## @jgengine/core/nature/natureMesh

- `BlobOptions` (interface): interface BlobOptions — Options for {@link addBlob}.
- `ConeOptions` (interface): interface ConeOptions — Options for {@link addCone}.
- `FrondOptions` (interface): interface FrondOptions — Options for {@link addFrond}.
- `LeafClusterOptions` (interface): interface LeafClusterOptions — Options for {@link addLeafCluster}.
- `NatureMesh` (interface): interface NatureMesh — Indexed triangle mesh with per-vertex sRGB colours, in metres with the base at y = 0.
- `NatureMeshPart` (interface): interface NatureMeshPart — One run of a nature mesh's index buffer drawn with one surface (none: plain vertex colour).
- `NatureRgb` (type): type NatureRgb = readonly [number, number, number] — An sRGB colour, 0..1 per channel.
- `NatureSurface` (type): type NatureSurface = "rock" | "bark" | "leaf" — Generated surface materials a nature mesh can be drawn with; `"leaf"` is vertex colour lit from both faces.
- `NatureVec` (type): type NatureVec = readonly [number, number, number] — A point or direction in a nature mesh's local space.
- `StoneOptions` (interface): interface StoneOptions — Options for {@link addStone}.
- `TubeOptions` (interface): interface TubeOptions — Options for {@link addTube}.
- `addBlob` (function): function addBlob(builder: NatureMeshBuilder, options: BlobOptions): void — A lumpy ellipsoid: a leaf cluster, a bush clump, a coconut.
- `addCone` (function): function addCone(builder: NatureMeshBuilder, options: ConeOptions): void — A closed, drooping cone: one conifer tier.
- `addFrond` (function): function addFrond(builder: NatureMeshBuilder, options: FrondOptions): void — A folded, drooping leaf blade: palm and cycad fronds, fern fronds, broad bush leaves. Both faces are emitted (the shared material is single-sided) with normals leaning up, so the underside of a raised frond reads as lit foliage rather than a black sliver.
- `addLeafCluster` (function): function addLeafCluster(builder: NatureMeshBuilder, options: LeafClusterOptions): void — A leafy cluster: a shaded core with folded leaf blades fanned out over its shell, so a canopy or a bush reads as foliage with a broken edge instead of a smooth ball. The blades are single-sided; draw them with the `"leaf"` surface, which lights both faces.
- `addStone` (function): function addStone(builder: NatureMeshBuilder, options: StoneOptions): void — One stone: an icosphere displaced by noise, sliced by `facets` random planes (sharp edges), with `erosion` blending the cuts back toward smooth, moss on the faces that look up, and a flat buried base. Vertices are not shared between faces, so it shades faceted like a real low-poly rock.
- `addTube` (function): function addTube(builder: NatureMeshBuilder, path: readonly NatureVec[], radii: readonly number[], options: TubeOptions): void — A tapered tube along `path` with radius `radii[i]` at each point: trunks, branches, logs. Rings follow the path's tangent with a rotation-minimising frame so a bent trunk does not twist.
- `isNatureMesh` (function): function isNatureMesh(value: unknown): value is NatureMesh — True when a generator output is a {@link NatureMesh}.

The caller owns and disposes the geometries.

Rocks and wood (`surface`) add the generated rock or bark grain, normal, roughness and AO, projected in world space so the meshes need no UVs.

## @jgengine/core/nav/navCrowd

- `NavCrowd` (interface): interface NavCrowd — Agents that cross an editor-baked nav mesh: each one plans a corridor with {@link NavRuntime}, walks the funnel-smoothed waypoints, and keeps its distance through reciprocal velocity obstacle avoidance. Goals, arrivals and replans are serializable; a mesh edit only re-plans the agents whose remaining route actually crossed the rebuilt region.

## @jgengine/core/orders/orderQueue

- `Order` (interface): interface Order<TPayload = unknown> — One issued order. Fully serializable: `kind` is a registry key (not a closure), `payload` is the caller's plain data, and `state` is the kind's own plain progress scratch (e.g. a patrol waypoint index) written during `start`/`update`. Never holds functions, so the whole queue round-trips through `JSON`/`structuredClone`.
- `OrderCancelReason` (type): type OrderCancelReason = "replaced" | "preempted" | "requested" | "invalid" | "failed" | "cleared" — Why an order left the queue without completing. `replaced`/`preempted` come from a newer order taking over; `requested` from explicit `cancelActive`; `invalid` when the kind's `start` rejects; `failed` when `update` reports failure; `cleared` from a full `clear`/`cancelAll`.
- `OrderEvent` (interface): interface OrderEvent — A lifecycle event emitted synchronously as orders move through the queue.
- `OrderIssueResult` (type): type OrderIssueResult<TPayload = unknown> = | { status: "accepted"; order: Order<TPayload> } | { status: "queued"; order: Order<TPayload> } | { status: "rejected"; reason: string } — Outcome of `issue`: `accepted` entered the queue, `queued` entered behind an uninterruptible/active order, `rejected` was refused (validation or `reject` policy).
- `OrderKind` (interface): interface OrderKind<TCtx, TPayload = unknown> — The composition seam for one order verb. `TCtx` is the game's world adapter (movement, targeting, effects) shared by every kind in a registry; `TPayload` is this verb's caller data. `start` seeds `order.state`, `update` advances it and reports lifecycle, and `finish` releases anything the kind held. Kinds are pure over their injected `ctx` -- no globals, no direct scene reach.
- `OrderOutcome` (interface): interface OrderOutcome — Terminal outcome handed to a kind's `finish` cleanup hook.
- `OrderPhase` (type): type OrderPhase = "queued" | "active" | "completed" | "canceled" — Lifecycle phase of a single order. `queued` waits behind the active order; `active` is ticking; `completed`/`canceled` are terminal.
- `OrderProgress` (type): type OrderProgress = { status: "running" } | { status: "completed" } | { status: "failed"; reason: string } — Result of a kind's `update` tick. `running` keeps the order active; the completion predicate lives in the kind (returns `completed`); `failed` cancels the order (reason `failed`) so the queue advances to the next one.
- `OrderQueue` (interface): interface OrderQueue<TCtx, TPayload = unknown> — A per-entity order queue: one commandable unit's lifecycle of intent. The game ticks it with its world adapter; it activates, advances, completes, and cancels orders and enforces preemption policy. State is serializable for save and host-authoritative replication.
- `OrderQueueOptions` (interface): interface OrderQueueOptions<TPayload = unknown> — Construction options for a queue.
- `OrderQueuePolicy` (type): type OrderQueuePolicy = "replace" | "append" | "front" | "reject" — How a newly issued order interacts with what's already queued. `replace` preempts the active order and clears pending; `append` queues it behind everything (shift-queue); `front` makes it the next to run without touching the active order; `reject` refuses it while anything is queued.
- `OrderQueueState` (interface): interface OrderQueueState<TPayload = unknown> — Serializable snapshot of a queue: the active order plus the pending list, in order.
- `OrderRegistry` (interface): interface OrderRegistry<TCtx> — Registry of order kinds keyed by verb string; the queue dispatches through it so engine code never switches on a verb.
- `OrderRejection` (interface): interface OrderRejection — A kind's refusal of a payload (from `validate`) — surfaced to the issuer as a rejection reason.
- `OrderRequest` (interface): interface OrderRequest<TPayload = unknown> — A request to issue an order; `policy` defaults to `replace`, `id` is generated when omitted.
- `OrderStartResult` (type): type OrderStartResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: string } — Result of a kind's `start`: `ok:false` skips the order and cancels it with reason `invalid`. The kind seeds `order.state` directly when `ok:true`.
- `OrderTickReport` (interface): interface OrderTickReport<TPayload = unknown> — What one `tick` did this frame, for tests and game reactions (play a bark on activation, flash on completion). Bounded per tick.
- `OrderVec3` (type): type OrderVec3 = readonly [number, number, number] — Composable entity orders: a serializable command queue with lifecycle, preemption, and pluggable order kinds (#912). Player- or AI-issued intent ("move here", "attack that", "patrol this route") becomes reusable data instead of a hard-coded RTS verb kit. The queue owns issue -> activate -> tick -> complete/cancel lifecycle and deterministic preemption policy; each order KIND owns what "running" means, composed over narrow world adapters. Engine code never branches on `move`, `attack`, or any game verb -- kinds are looked up by string in a registry, so a game adds a verb by registering data.
- `createOrderQueue` (function): function createOrderQueue<TCtx, TPayload = unknown>(registry: OrderRegistry<TCtx>, options: OrderQueueOptions<TPayload> = {}): OrderQueue<TCtx, TPayload> — Create a per-entity order queue over a shared kind registry. The queue owns the deterministic lifecycle and preemption policy; the kinds own behavior. Nothing here is random or unbounded: id generation is injected, activation is bounded by the pending count, and a single `tick` advances at most the active order plus one activation.
- `createOrderRegistry` (function): function createOrderRegistry<TCtx>(): OrderRegistry<TCtx> — Build an empty order-kind registry. Register the built-in compositions from `orders/orderKinds` or your own verbs, then hand it to `createOrderQueue`. One registry is shared by many per-entity queues.

- `BoatTuning` (interface): interface BoatTuning — A powered hull in physical units. Drag rises toward hull speed (`√(g·L)·1.34`) and then falls away once the hull planes, the keel resists sliding sideways, and the prop's thrust fades as the boat approaches the prop's speed.
- `createBoatDynamics` (function): function createBoatDynamics(initial: BoatTuning, options: BoatOptions = {}): BoatDynamics — Creates a {@link BoatDynamics}: throttle drives the prop, brake reverses it, steer swings the rudder or outboard. A rudder boat barely turns at rest unless the prop is washing over it; an outboard turns at rest because it swings the thrust itself. Deterministic for a given `dt` sequence.

## @jgengine/core/physics/buoyancy

- `BuoyantBody` (class): class BuoyantBody — Floats a {@link PhysicsWorld} body on a CPU {@link WaterSurface}: each hull sample point pushes the body up by its submerged depth (Archimedes, coarse), with vertical and horizontal water drag so the hull settles at the waterline and rides the Gerstner waves. Passing an {@link AxisInput} drives it as a boat — throttle thrusts along the heading, steer yaws, a keel bleeds sideways slip. Call `update(dt, time, input?)` before the shared `world.step(dt)`.
- `BuoyantBodyConfig` (interface): interface BuoyantBodyConfig { body: number; water: WaterSurface; heading?: number; hullPoints?: readonly (readonly [number, number])[]; hullDepth?: number; buoyancy?: number; verticalDrag?: number; linearDrag?: number; engineAccel?: number; reverseAccel?: number; topS… — ⚠ undocumented
- `createBuoyantBody` (function): function createBuoyantBody(world: PhysicsWorld, config: BuoyantBodyConfig): BuoyantBody — ⚠ undocumented

## @jgengine/core/physics/carryable

- `Carryable` (class): class Carryable — A grabbed physics object following a moving hold point through a spring constraint (the pick — a raycast — is the caller's/shell's job; core owns the constraint). Supports shared multi-owner carry (the follow point is the average of owners' hold points), an encumbrance read, and drop/throw. Reuses `PhysicsWorld.springJoint` to a world anchor moved each frame.
- `CarryableConfig` (interface): interface CarryableConfig { followStiffness?: number; followDamping?: number; maxForce?: number; carryCapacity?: number } — ⚠ undocumented
- `carrySpeedMultiplier` (function): function carrySpeedMultiplier(mass: number, carryCapacity: number, owners: number): number — Movement multiplier (1 = unhindered, →0 = crushed) for a body of `mass` carried by `owners`. Pure — the HUD/movement kit reads it to slow a laden hauler (Lethal Company) and to gate items that need 2+ people (R.E.P.O.).

## @jgengine/core/physics/damageZones

- `DamageModel` (class): class DamageModel — Coarse crash-damage model (issue #86 — stages, not soft-body). Each zone accumulates contact impulse fed from G3's `onCollision` `CollisionEvent`; crossing a threshold bumps the zone to the next discrete stage (the caller swaps the visual/collider), an optional `detachStage` ejects a part as debris once, and a total-impulse `disableAt` flips the whole body to a disabled state. `absorb` returns a transition only when something actually changed, so it doubles as the event source for HUD/feed.
- `DamageModelConfig` (interface): interface DamageModelConfig { zones: readonly DamageZoneDef[]; disableAt?: number; onStage?: (transition: DamageTransition) => void; onDetach?: (zoneId: string, accumulated: number) => void } — ⚠ undocumented
- `DamageTransition` (interface): interface DamageTransition { zone: string; stage: number; previousStage: number; detached: boolean; disabled: boolean; accumulated: number; total: number } — ⚠ undocumented
- `DamageZoneDef` (interface): interface DamageZoneDef { id: string; thresholds: readonly number[]; detachStage?: number } — ⚠ undocumented
- `DamageZoneState` (interface): interface DamageZoneState { id: string; accumulated: number; stage: number; detached: boolean } — ⚠ undocumented
- `createDamageModel` (function): function createDamageModel(config: DamageModelConfig): DamageModel — ⚠ undocumented

## @jgengine/core/physics/drivableVehicle

- `DrivableTireEffects` (interface): interface DrivableTireEffects — Where a car's sliding tires leave their trace: skid marks on the ground and smoke in the air.
- `DrivableVehicleOptions` (interface): interface DrivableVehicleOptions — Options for {@link tickDrivableVehicle} — ground snapping, per-tick modifiers and tire effects.

Ground-snaps the result when `groundHeight` is given (terrain-following cars, not just flat racetracks), and with `tires` lays skid marks and plays tire smoke while the car slides. Pair with `scene/vehicleSeat` for who is allowed to drive and where the camera points.

## @jgengine/core/physics/gripCurve

- `DEFAULT_GRIP_CURVE` (const): const DEFAULT_GRIP_CURVE: GripCurve — A street tire: full grip to slip `0.2`, then it lets go to 55% fully sideways.
- `GripCurve` (interface): interface GripCurve — A piecewise-linear curve of `[x, y]` points in ascending `x`: tire grip against slip, engine torque against rpm.
- `gripCurvePeak` (function): function gripCurvePeak(curve: GripCurve): { peakGrip: number; peakSlip: number; slideGrip: number } — The peak of a grip curve: its highest grip, the far end of a flat plateau as the breakaway slip, and the grip left at slip `1`.
- `sampleGripCurve` (function): function sampleGripCurve(curve: GripCurve, slip: number): number — Piecewise-linear tire-grip curve: normalized lateral slip → available grip (0..1). Grip peaks near the breakaway slip then falls off as the tire slides — the shape that separates a planted corner from a drift. Points are read in ascending slip order; ends clamp.

## @jgengine/core/physics/handlingProbe

- `AirReport` (interface): interface AirReport — Deterministic jump and air-control metrics.
- `AirSubject` (interface): interface AirSubject — The slice of a jumping vehicle sim {@link measureAir} drives; a `VehicleDynamics` with `suspension`, `jump` and `air` fits.
- `CourseProbeOptions` (interface): interface CourseProbeOptions — Settings for {@link measureCourse}; every field but `wheelbase` has a default.
- `CourseReport` (interface): interface CourseReport — Deterministic driven-course metrics.
- `CourseSubject` (interface): interface CourseSubject — A vehicle sim {@link measureCourse} can drive along a line: a {@link HandlingSubject} that also reports its pose and front-wheel angle.
- `FlightProbeOptions` (interface): interface FlightProbeOptions — Scenario settings for {@link measureFlight}.
- `FlightReport` (interface): interface FlightReport — Deterministic flight metrics. Fields that don't apply to the aircraft are `NaN`: turn and stall need wings, hover drift needs a rotor.
- `FlightSpawn` (interface): interface FlightSpawn — Where {@link measureFlight} spawns each fresh aircraft: level, heading `0` (forward `+z`).
- `HandlingProbeOptions` (interface): interface HandlingProbeOptions — Scenario settings for {@link measureHandling}; every field has a default.
- `HandlingReport` (interface): interface HandlingReport — Deterministic feel metrics, in the units drivers and reviewers use. `Infinity` means the target was never reached.
- `HandlingSubject` (interface): interface HandlingSubject — The slice of a vehicle sim {@link measureHandling} drives; `VehicleDynamics` fits.
- `LeanReport` (interface): interface LeanReport — Deterministic lean metrics for a motorcycle or bicycle.
- `LeanSubject` (interface): interface LeanSubject — The slice of a single-track sim {@link measureLean} drives; a `VehicleDynamics` with a `lean` block fits.
- `RideReport` (interface): interface RideReport — Deterministic ride metrics for a sprung vehicle.
- `RideSubject` (interface): interface RideSubject — The slice of a sprung vehicle sim {@link measureRide} drives; a `VehicleDynamics` with `suspension` fits.
- `measureAir` (function): function measureAir(create: () => AirSubject, options: { dt?: number } = {}): AirReport — Jumps a fresh vehicle from rest and holds full air input on each axis, reporting jump height and timing, double-jump height, and how fast the body rotates in the air.
- `measureCourse` (function): function measureCourse(create: () => CourseSubject, options: CourseProbeOptions): CourseReport — Drives a fresh vehicle from `create` through a steer ramp, a skidpad and a slalom with simple deterministic drivers, and reports understeer gradient, skidpad g and the fastest clean slalom.
- `measureFlight` (function): function measureFlight(create: (spawn: FlightSpawn) => RigidAircraft, options: FlightProbeOptions = {}): FlightReport — Flies fresh aircraft from `create` through fixed scenarios with simple deterministic autopilots: a full-aileron roll, banked turns at full throttle, an idle deceleration holding altitude, a full-throttle climb at cruise speed, a throttle step from idle, and a hands-off hover. `create` gets a spawn to pass straight into `createRigidAircraft`. Deterministic, so a tuning change shows up as a number moving.
- `measureHandling` (function): function measureHandling(create: () => HandlingSubject, options: HandlingProbeOptions = {}): HandlingReport — Drives fresh instances from `create` through fixed scenarios (launch, top speed, braking, a slow steer ramp, a step steer, a mid-corner lift-off, a handbrake pull, full throttle with full steer) and reports the feel metrics a test can assert. Deterministic: the same subject and options always produce the same report, so a tuning change shows up as a number moving, not an opinion.
- `measureLean` (function): function measureLean(create: () => LeanSubject, options: { dt?: number; speed?: number } = {}): LeanReport — Brings a fresh bike to `speed` and holds full steer, reporting how far and how fast it leans and how much it tips the other way first.
- `measureRide` (function): function measureRide(create: () => RideSubject, options: { dt?: number } = {}): RideReport — Drives fresh sprung vehicles from `create` through a vertical kick, a hard stop, a steady corner and a launch-and-land, and reports how the body moves: how fast it settles, how much it dives and rolls, and whether a landing bounces.

## @jgengine/core/physics/physicsBackend

- `BodyDesc` (interface): interface BodyDesc — Everything a backend needs to create a body. Rotation-free backends ignore `rotation` and `angularVelocity` and say so in {@link PhysicsCapabilities}.
- `BodyHandle` (type): type BodyHandle = number — Backend-issued body id; stable for the body's lifetime and across snapshot/restore.
- `BodyKind` (type): type BodyKind = "dynamic" | "kinematic" | "static" — `dynamic` integrates under forces, `kinematic` moves only through {@link PhysicsBackend.setKinematicTarget}, `static` never moves.
- `BodyShape` (type): type BodyShape = | { kind: "box"; halfExtents: PhysicsVec3 } | { kind: "sphere"; radius: number } | { kind: "capsule"; radius: number; halfHeight: number } | { kind: "convex"; points: readonly PhysicsVec3[] } | { kind: "trimesh"; vertices: ArrayLike<number>; indices: ArrayLike<number> } | { kind: "h… — Collision shape of a body or a cast. Capsules stand along +Y; a trimesh or heightfield is static-only on every backend.
- `BodyShapeKind` (type): type BodyShapeKind = BodyShape["kind"] — Shape discriminator, as listed in {@link PhysicsCapabilities.shapes}.
- `BodyState` (interface): interface BodyState — A body's live pose and motion. Rotation-free backends report identity rotation and zero angular velocity.
- `ContactEvent` (interface): interface ContactEvent — A contact reported during {@link PhysicsBackend.step}; the object is reused between calls, so copy what you keep.
- `IDENTITY_QUAT` (const): const IDENTITY_QUAT: PhysicsQuat — The identity rotation.
- `JointDesc` (interface): interface JointDesc — Joint between two bodies, or between `bodyA` and a world anchor when `bodyB` is omitted.
- `JointHandle` (type): type JointHandle = number — Backend-issued joint id.
- `OverlapDesc` (interface): interface OverlapDesc — Which bodies a shape placed at `position` intersects.
- `PhysicsBackend` (interface): interface PhysicsBackend — The seam every physics consumer talks to: the in-tree `PhysicsWorld` behind `createPhysicsWorldBackend`, or a native solver such as Rapier behind its own adapter. Handles are backend-issued and survive snapshot/restore, so gameplay state can store them.
- `PhysicsBackendConfig` (interface): interface PhysicsBackendConfig — Solver-wide knobs a backend accepts at creation and through `retune`.
- `PhysicsCapabilities` (interface): interface PhysicsCapabilities — What a backend can actually simulate, so a game or the conformance suite can adapt instead of guessing.
- `PhysicsQuat` (type): type PhysicsQuat = readonly [number, number, number, number] — Unit quaternion `[x, y, z, w]`; `[0, 0, 0, 1]` is identity.
- `PhysicsVec3` (type): type PhysicsVec3 = readonly [number, number, number] — `[x, y, z]`.
- `RayDesc` (interface): interface RayDesc — A ray query.
- `RayHit` (interface): interface RayHit — Nearest surface a ray reached.
- `ShapeCastDesc` (interface): interface ShapeCastDesc — Sweep `shape` from `position` along `motion` and report the first body it touches.
- `ShapeCastHit` (interface): interface ShapeCastHit — First contact of a shape sweep.
- `isIdentityQuat` (function): function isIdentityQuat(q: PhysicsQuat | undefined): boolean — True for an absent or identity rotation.
- `shapeHalfExtents` (function): function shapeHalfExtents(shape: BodyShape): [number, number, number] — Axis-aligned bounds of a shape at identity rotation, as half extents.

## @jgengine/core/physics/physicsBackendConformance

- `ConformanceHarness` (interface): interface ConformanceHarness — The slice of a test runner the conformance suite needs; `bun:test` satisfies it directly.
- `runPhysicsBackendConformance` (function): function runPhysicsBackendConformance(create: () => PhysicsBackend, harness: ConformanceHarness): void — Behavioral contract every {@link PhysicsBackend} must pass: bodies rest on floors, casts and rays report the first surface with an outward normal, kinematic targets produce velocity, masks filter, and snapshot/restore round-trips with stable handles. Backends declare what they cannot do through `capabilities`; the suite reads it. Expects `create()` to return a fresh backend whose world spans at least ±50 on every axis with a floor at y=0.

## @jgengine/core/physics/radialImpulse

- `RadialFalloff` (type): type RadialFalloff = "linear" | "quadratic" | "none" — How a radial impulse fades from the blast center to its edge.
- `RadialImpulse` (interface): interface RadialImpulse — A radial push: the impulse vector plus the 0..1 falloff sampled at the target.

Returns `null` when the target sits at or beyond the radius (unaffected), so callers can early-out. At the exact center the direction is zero. This is the explosion/knockback/ shockwave push — every arena game hand-rolled the distance, falloff, and normalize.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/boatComparison

- `BoatComparisonSubject` (interface): interface BoatComparisonSubject — A reference boat with the game build of it and the published figures it carries.

- `kvlcc2Subject` (function): function kvlcc2Subject(): BoatComparisonSubject — The KVLCC2 L7 tanker model as a reference boat: its MMG model for resistance and manoeuvring, a game build with the same mass, rudder, steering rate and propeller (bollard thrust and zero-thrust speed at the self-propulsion revolutions), and MARIN's free-running turning and zig-zag results.
- `referenceBoatSubjects` (function): function referenceBoatSubjects(): BoatComparisonSubject[] — The reference boats every comparison run includes.
- `referenceSubjectFor` (function): function referenceSubjectFor(name: string, tuning: BoatTuning): BoatComparisonSubject — Builds a reference boat for any game tuning: a planing hull (`planingSpeed` set) becomes an 18° deadrise prismatic hull of its length, beam and mass; a displacement hull becomes a Holtrop–Mennen hull of its length, beam and mass with workboat coefficients (`C_B 0.55`, `C_M 0.85`, `C_WP 0.75`, LCB 1.5% aft).
- `speedboatSubject` (function): function speedboatSubject(): BoatComparisonSubject — The 6 m outboard speedboat of the `boatDynamics` docs as a reference boat: an 18° deadrise prismatic planing hull of the same beam and mass, centre of gravity 38% of the length forward of the transom, run through Savitsky's equations.
- `surgeAddedMass` (function): function surgeAddedMass(massKg: number, length: number, density = RHO): number — Surge added mass of a hull as the half of a prolate spheroid of the same length and twice its volume (the double-body image across the still surface): Lamb's `k₁ = α₀/(2 − α₀)` times the displaced mass.
- `wigleyStandIn` (function): function wigleyStandIn(tuning: BoatTuning): StripHull — A Wigley hull (`C_B` 4/9) with a boat tuning's length, beam and mass, floating level with G on the waterline: the seakeeping stand-in for a boat whose real lines are unknown.

- `MotorcyclePublishedCheck` (interface): interface MotorcyclePublishedCheck — One published number checked against the reference motorcycle.
- `PUBLISHED_TOLERANCES` (const): const PUBLISHED_TOLERANCES: { readonly zeroTo100: 0.05; readonly brake100To0: 0.05; readonly skidpadG: 0.03; } — How close the reference car must land to each published number: 0–100 km/h and 100–0 km/h braking within 5%, skidpad within 0.03 g.
- `PublishedCheck` (interface): interface PublishedCheck — One published number checked against the reference car by {@link checkReferenceAgainstPublished}.
- `VehicleHandlingComparison` (interface): interface VehicleHandlingComparison — Result of {@link compareVehicleTuning}.
- `checkReferenceAgainstPublished` (function): function checkReferenceAgainstPublished(car: RealCar, reference: ComparableHandlingMetrics): PublishedCheck[] — Check a real car's measured reference metrics against its published test numbers within {@link PUBLISHED_TOLERANCES}.
- `checkReferenceMotorcycle` (function): function checkReferenceMotorcycle(bike: RealMotorcycle, reference: BikeHandlingMetrics): MotorcyclePublishedCheck[] — Check a real motorcycle's measured reference metrics against its published tests within {@link MOTORCYCLE_PUBLISHED_TOLERANCES}.
- `compareBikeMetrics` (function): function compareBikeMetrics(game: BikeHandlingMetrics, reference: BikeHandlingMetrics, real?: PublishedMotorcyclePerformance): HandlingComparisonRow<keyof BikeHandlingMetrics>[] — Line up a game bike's and the reference motorcycle's measured bike metrics and, optionally, the real bike's published numbers.
- `compareBikeTuning` (function): function compareBikeTuning(tuning: VehicleDynamicsTuning, bike: RealMotorcycle, reference?: BikeHandlingMetrics): BikeHandlingComparison — Score a game's single-track `VehicleDynamics` tuning (one with a `lean` block) against the multibody reference motorcycle ridden by its steering-torque rider and the real bike's published tests: launch, braking, lean, countersteer, lane change and slalom, game / reference / real per metric.
- `compareHandlingMetrics` (function): function compareHandlingMetrics(game: ComparableHandlingMetrics, reference: ComparableHandlingMetrics, real?: RealCarTestData): HandlingComparisonRow[] — Line up two measured metric sets and, optionally, a real car's published numbers.
- `compareVehicleTuning` (function): function compareVehicleTuning(tuning: VehicleDynamicsTuning, car: RealCar, reference?: ComparableHandlingMetrics): VehicleHandlingComparison — Score a game's `VehicleDynamics` tuning against real physics: run the same scenarios on the game model and on the multi-body reference model of `car`, and line up game / reference / real per metric. A bad feel becomes a named number ("the game pulls 1.4 g on the skidpad where the reference and the real car pull 0.9 g").
- `formatHandlingComparison` (function): function formatHandlingComparison(title: string, rows: readonly HandlingComparisonRow<string>[]): string — Plain-text table of comparison rows: metric, unit, game, reference, real, and game − reference.

- `measureReferenceCar` (function): function measureReferenceCar(car: RealCar, dt?: number): ComparableHandlingMetrics — Measure a real car's reference model; pass the result to {@link compareVehicleTuning} to reuse it across many game cars.
- `measureReferenceMotorcycle` (function): function measureReferenceMotorcycle(bike: RealMotorcycle, options: { dt?: number; tests?: readonly BikeScenario[] } = {}): BikeHandlingMetrics — Measure a real motorcycle's reference model with its rider; pass the result to {@link compareBikeTuning} to reuse it.
- `validateReferenceCars` (function): function validateReferenceCars(cars: readonly RealCar[] = REAL_CARS): { car: RealCar; metrics: ComparableHandlingMetrics; checks: PublishedCheck[] }[] — Measure every real car's reference model and check it against the published numbers: the full validation behind `bun run games:capabilities handling --validate`.
- `validateReferenceMotorcycles` (function): function validateReferenceMotorcycles(bikes: readonly RealMotorcycle[] = REAL_MOTORCYCLES): { bike: RealMotorcycle; metrics: BikeHandlingMetrics; checks: MotorcyclePublishedCheck[] }[] — Measure every real motorcycle's reference model and check it against its published tests: the bike half of `bun run games:capabilities handling --validate`.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/eigenvalues

- `polynomialRoots` (function): function polynomialRoots(coefficients: readonly number[]): Eigenvalue[] — Roots of the real polynomial `c[0] + c[1]·λ + … + c[n]·λⁿ` (`c[n] ≠ 0`): the companion-matrix eigenvalues, then two Newton steps on the polynomial itself to recover full double precision.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/hullForm

- `HullMesh` (interface): interface HullMesh — A closed, outward-facing triangle mesh in hull axes: `positions` holds `x, y, z` triples, `triangles` index triples.
- `HullOffsets` (interface): interface HullOffsets — A hull as a table of offsets, the way lines plans publish it. Hull axes: `x` forward from the aft end of the table, `y` to port, `z` up from the baseline (keel). The top waterline is the deck edge.
- `PrismaticPlaningHullOptions` (interface): interface PrismaticPlaningHullOptions — Dimensions of a {@link prismaticPlaningHull}.
- `WigleyHullOptions` (interface): interface WigleyHullOptions — Dimensions of a {@link wigleyHull}.
- `boxBarge` (function): function boxBarge(length: number, beam: number, depth: number, stations = 3, waterlines = 3): HullOffsets — A rectangular box barge `length × beam × depth`: the textbook hull whose large-angle righting arm has a closed form.
- `hullMeshFromOffsets` (function): function hullMeshFromOffsets(offsets: HullOffsets): HullMesh — Builds a closed, outward-facing triangle mesh from a table of offsets: the two hull sides, the deck, and flat end caps where a station has breadth (a transom). Every section is a closed ring from the keel up the starboard side, across the deck and down the port side.
- `meshVolume` (function): function meshVolume(mesh: HullMesh): number — Signed volume enclosed by a mesh, m³ (positive when its triangles face outward).
- `prismaticPlaningHull` (function): function prismaticPlaningHull(options: PrismaticPlaningHullOptions): HullOffsets — A constant-deadrise planing hull: a V bottom of the given deadrise up to a hard chine, vertical topsides above it, a flat transom aft and a bow that narrows to a point over `bowLength`. The prismatic hull Savitsky's equations describe.
- `wigleyHull` (function): function wigleyHull(options: WigleyHullOptions): HullOffsets — The Wigley parabolic hull, `y = B/2 · (1 − (2x/L)²) · (1 − (z/T)²)` below the waterline, with vertical topsides above it — the standard mathematical test hull of ship hydrodynamics. Its hydrostatics are known in closed form: `C_B = 4/9`, `C_WP = 2/3`, `KB = 5T/8`, `BM_T = 3B²/(35T)`, `BM_L = 3L²/(40T)`. The table's `x` runs `0..L` from the stern.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/hullHydrostatics

- `FloatingAttitude` (interface): interface FloatingAttitude — A hull's floating attitude.
- `FloatingCondition` (interface): interface FloatingCondition — Mass properties of a floating hull, hull axes.
- `HullIntegrator` (interface): interface HullIntegrator — Integrates water pressure over a hull mesh in any pose.
- `HullLoads` (interface): interface HullLoads — Pressure loads and submerged geometry of a posed hull, earth axes.
- `HullWater` (interface): interface HullWater — The water a hull sits in, sampled at earth points (`x`, `y` horizontal, `z` up). `submergence` is how far below the free surface a point is (negative above it); `pressure` is the gauge pressure there, Pa. Still water: `submergence = −z`, `pressure = ρ·g·max(0, −z)`.
- `HydrostaticParticulars` (interface): interface HydrostaticParticulars — Upright hydrostatic particulars at the free-floating attitude, hull axes.
- `MARINE_GRAVITY` (const): const MARINE_GRAVITY: 9.80665 — Standard gravity, m/s².
- `RightingArmPoint` (interface): interface RightingArmPoint — One point of a righting-arm curve.
- `SEA_WATER_DENSITY` (const): const SEA_WATER_DENSITY: 1025.9 — Sea water at 15 °C (ITTC 7.5-02-01-03), kg/m³.
- `StabilitySummary` (interface): interface StabilitySummary — Stability figures read off a GZ curve, the ones intact-stability criteria (IMO IS Code 2008, 2.2) ask for.
- `createHullIntegrator` (function): function createHullIntegrator(mesh: HullMesh): HullIntegrator — Creates a {@link HullIntegrator} for a closed, outward-facing mesh. Pressure is taken linear over each (cut) triangle, which is exact for still water, so buoyancy, its centre and the waterplane come straight out of the geometry; the submerged volume and its centroid use the divergence theorem over the wetted surface alone (the waterplane carries none of it). Scratch buffers are allocated once.
- `createHullLoads` (function): function createHullLoads(): HullLoads — Creates an empty {@link HullLoads} to pass to {@link HullIntegrator.integrate}.
- `floatingEquilibrium` (function): function floatingEquilibrium(mesh: HullMesh, condition: FloatingCondition, guess?: FloatingAttitude): FloatingAttitude — Finds where a hull floats freely in still water: the height, heel and trim at which buoyancy carries the weight and passes through the centre of gravity.
- `heelTrimRotation` (function): function heelTrimRotation(phi: number, theta: number, out: Float64Array = new Float64Array(9)): Float64Array — Row-major rotation for heel `phi` (about +x, positive heels to starboard) then trim `theta` (about +y, positive bow down).
- `hydrostaticParticulars` (function): function hydrostaticParticulars(mesh: HullMesh, condition: FloatingCondition): HydrostaticParticulars — Floats a hull and reads its hydrostatics off the integrated geometry: volume, centre of buoyancy, waterplane, metacentric radii (`I/∇` of the cut waterplane) and metacentric heights.
- `rightingArmCurve` (function): function rightingArmCurve(mesh: HullMesh, condition: FloatingCondition, heels: readonly number[]): RightingArmPoint[] — The statical stability (GZ) curve with free trim: at each heel the hull sinks and trims until buoyancy carries the weight with no trimming moment, and the remaining heeling moment over the weight is the righting arm. Heels in rad.
- `stillWater` (function): function stillWater(density = SEA_WATER_DENSITY, gravity = MARINE_GRAVITY, level = 0): HullWater — Still water with its surface at `level`.
- `summarizeStability` (function): function summarizeStability(curve: readonly RightingArmPoint[]): StabilitySummary — Reads the {@link StabilitySummary} off a GZ curve (trapezoidal areas).

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/magicFormulaTire

- `MagicFormulaCoefficients` (type): type MagicFormulaCoefficients = typeof TNO_VALUES — Pacejka Magic Formula 6.1 coefficients, named after the keys of a TNO `.tir` property file in camelCase (`PCX1` → `pcx1`, `UNLOADED_RADIUS` → `unloadedRadius`, `Q_FZ2` → `qFz2`). SI units: m, N, rad, kg, s, Pa. {@link parseTirFile} reads a `.tir` file into this shape.
- `MagicFormulaContactState` (interface): interface MagicFormulaContactState — Contact deflections of a transient tyre: longitudinal `u` and lateral `v`, m, and lagged spin slip `phi`, 1/m.
- `MagicFormulaInput` (interface): interface MagicFormulaInput — One steady-state evaluation of {@link magicFormula}. Angles in rad, ISO-W axes (x forward, y left, z up).
- `MagicFormulaOutput` (interface): interface MagicFormulaOutput — Forces and moments from {@link magicFormula}, in the tyre's ISO-W axes.
- `MagicFormulaTire` (interface): interface MagicFormulaTire — A transient Magic Formula tyre: relaxation-length dynamics on top of {@link magicFormula}.
- `MagicFormulaTireOptions` (interface): interface MagicFormulaTireOptions — Options for {@link createMagicFormulaTire}.
- `MagicFormulaTireState` (interface): interface MagicFormulaTireState — Serializable transient state of a {@link MagicFormulaTire}: contact deflections and the last slip velocities.
- `MagicFormulaTireStep` (interface): interface MagicFormulaTireStep extends MagicFormulaOutput — {@link MagicFormulaTire.step} result: forces and moments plus the lagged slips that produced them.
- `MagicFormulaTireStepInput` (interface): interface MagicFormulaTireStepInput — One {@link MagicFormulaTire.step} input: the wheel's motion in its own ISO-W axes.
- `MagicFormulaVerticalInput` (interface): interface MagicFormulaVerticalInput — Inputs to {@link magicFormulaVerticalForce}.
- `TNO_205_60R15` (const): const TNO_205_60R15: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients> — The TNO 205/60 R15 passenger-car tyre (`TNO_car205_60R15.tir`, MF-Tyre/MF-Swift 6.2 fit, Delft-Tyre 2013), the parameter set listed in Pacejka, *Tire and Vehicle Dynamics*, 3rd ed. (2012), Appendix 3. Dry asphalt, 2.2 bar, 4000 N nominal load: μx ≈ 1.04, μy ≈ 0.88, cornering stiffness ≈ 53 kN/rad at nominal load. A left tyre (`TYRESIDE = 'Left'`); {@link createMagicFormulaTire} mirrors it for the right side.
- `createMagicFormulaTire` (function): function createMagicFormulaTire(coefficients: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients>, options: MagicFormulaTireOptions = {}): MagicFormulaTire — A transient Magic Formula 6.1 tyre (Pacejka 2012 §7.2, the MF-Tyre "linear relaxation" contact): the contact patch deflects by `du/dt = −Vsx − |Vx|·u/σκ` and `dv/dt = Vsy − |Vx|·v/σα` with load- and pressure-dependent relaxation lengths `σ = slip stiffness / carcass stiffness`, and the forces come from the lagged slips `κ′ = u/σκ`, `tan α′ = v/σα` (spin slip lags on σα too). Each step is the exact solution for inputs that change linearly across the step, so it stays stable at standstill and converges at second order as `dt` halves. Below `VXLOW` the contact gains Pacejka's low-speed damping, so a parked car holds still on its tyres' carcass springs. Tyre temperature is not modelled: MF 6.1 has no thermal terms and no thermal parameter set is published for this tyre.
- `magicFormula` (function): function magicFormula(p: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients>, input: MagicFormulaInput): MagicFormulaOutput — The Magic Formula 6.1 steady-state tyre (Pacejka 2012, §4.3.2–4.3.3 and Appendix 3; MF-Tyre 6.1 as in Besselink, Schmeitz and Pacejka 2010): pure longitudinal and lateral slip with load, camber and inflation-pressure dependence; combined slip through the weighting functions Gxα and Gyκ and the κ-induced side force SVyκ; aligning moment from pneumatic trail on the γ = 0 side force, residual torque and the Fx moment arm; overturning moment; rolling resistance; and, when `phi`/`phit` are given, turn and spin slip (ζ0–ζ8) including the parking torque. Below `VXLOW` the curve shifts fade out so a standing wheel carries no offset force. Pure and allocation-light; call it once per wheel per step.
- `magicFormulaContact` (function): function magicFormulaContact(coefficients: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients>, contact: Readonly<MagicFormulaContactState>, input: MagicFormulaTireStepInput, options: MagicFormulaTireOptions = {}): { forces: MagicFormulaTireStep; du: number; dv: number; dphi: number } — The transient contact of {@link createMagicFormulaTire} as a pure right-hand side, for a caller that integrates the deflections itself (a multibody car's ODE): forces from the current deflections and the deflection rates `du/dt = −Vsx − |Vx|·u/σκ`, `dv/dt = Vsy − |Vx|·v/σα`, `dφ′/dt = |Vx|·(φ − φ′)/σα`. Right-tyre states live in the mirrored frame.
- `magicFormulaRelaxation` (function): function magicFormulaRelaxation(p: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients>, fz: number, kxk: number, kya: number, pressure?: number): { longitudinal: number; lateral: number; longitudinalStiffness: number; lateralStiffness: number } — Overall carcass stiffness and first-order relaxation lengths (MF 6.1, Pacejka 2012 §7.2): `σκ = Kxκ/Cx`, `σα = |Kyα|/Cy`, with `Cx`, `Cy` from `LONGITUDINAL_STIFFNESS`/`LATERAL_STIFFNESS` and their load and pressure terms.
- `magicFormulaRollingRadius` (function): function magicFormulaRollingRadius(p: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients>, fz: number, spin: number, pressure?: number): number — Effective rolling radius, m (MF 6.1, Besselink et al. 2010 Eqs. 1 and 7): the radius that turns wheel spin `Ω` into ground speed. Grows with spin by `Q_V1` and shrinks with load by the `BREFF`/`DREFF`/`FREFF` law on the pressure-corrected vertical stiffness.
- `magicFormulaSpinSlip` (function): function magicFormulaSpinSlip(p: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients>, input: { yawRate: number; spin: number; gamma: number; vx: number; vy?: number; fz: number }): { phi: number; phit: number } — Spin slip φ and turn slip φt (Pacejka 2012 §4.3.3, Eqs. 4.75–4.76 written for ISO yaw), 1/m, for {@link MagicFormulaInput}: `φt = ψ̇/Vc` and `φ = (ψ̇ + (1 − εγ)·Ω·sin γ)/Vc`, where εγ = `PECP1·(1 + PECP2·dfz)` is the share of camber that does not act as spin. A wheel leaning into a turn at its own rolling-cone curvature has φ ≈ 0. `Vc` is floored at `VXLOW`.
- `magicFormulaVerticalForce` (function): function magicFormulaVerticalForce(p: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients>, input: MagicFormulaVerticalInput): number — Tyre vertical force, N, from deflection (MF 6.1, Besselink et al. 2010 Eq. 4): `Fz = (1 + qV2·|Ω|R0/V0 − (qFcx·Fx/Fz0)² − (qFcy·Fy/Fz0)²)·(qFz1·ρ/R0 + qFz2·(ρ/R0)²)·(1 + pFz1·dpi)·Fz0`, with `qFz1` set so the stiffness at nominal load equals `VERTICAL_STIFFNESS`. Adds `VERTICAL_DAMPING` on the deflection rate and the MF-Swift bottoming spring once the rim is within `BOTTOM_OFFST`. Never pulls (≥ 0).
- `parseTirFile` (function): function parseTirFile(text: string, base: Readonly<MagicFormulaCoefficients> = TNO_205_60R15): MagicFormulaCoefficients — Read a TNO/ADAMS `.tir` property file into {@link MagicFormulaCoefficients}. Keys the file leaves out keep the value from `base` (default {@link TNO_205_60R15}), so a partial file still yields a complete set.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/marinePropeller

- `BSeriesPropeller` (interface): interface BSeriesPropeller — Geometry of a Wageningen B-series propeller.
- `OpenWaterPoint` (interface): interface OpenWaterPoint — Open-water thrust and torque coefficients at one advance ratio.
- `PropellerOperatingPoint` (interface): interface PropellerOperatingPoint extends OpenWaterPoint — Where a propeller runs to deliver a thrust at an inflow speed.
- `ScrewBladeSection` (interface): interface ScrewBladeSection — Blade chord and thickness at 0.75R, the section the ITTC-1978 correction scales.
- `Waterjet` (interface): interface Waterjet — A waterjet: an inlet in the hull bottom, a pump, and a nozzle.
- `WaterjetPoint` (interface): interface WaterjetPoint — A waterjet's thrust at one speed and power.
- `bSeriesBladeSection` (function): function bSeriesBladeSection(propeller: BSeriesPropeller): ScrewBladeSection — Holtrop and Mennen's (1982) estimate of the 0.75R chord and thickness ratio from diameter, blades and area ratio.
- `bSeriesOpenWater` (function): function bSeriesOpenWater(propeller: BSeriesPropeller, advance: number): OpenWaterPoint — Open-water `K_T` and `K_Q` of a Wageningen B-series propeller from the Oosterveld–van Oossanen regression polynomials (model scale, Re = 2·10⁶). Valid for positive thrust; past the zero-thrust advance the polynomials are extrapolations.
- `bSeriesShipOpenWater` (function): function bSeriesShipOpenWater(propeller: BSeriesPropeller, advance: number): OpenWaterPoint — Full-scale open water of a B-series propeller: the series polynomials with the ITTC-1978 correction `K_T −= ΔC_D·0.3·(P/D)·(c·Z/D)`, `K_Q += ΔC_D·0.25·(c·Z/D)`.
- `optimumPitchPropeller` (function): function optimumPitchPropeller(propeller: Omit<BSeriesPropeller, "pitchRatio">, thrust: number, advanceSpeed: number, density = 1025): { propeller: BSeriesPropeller; point: PropellerOperatingPoint } — The pitch ratio that delivers `thrust` at `advanceSpeed` with the best open-water efficiency, searched over `P/D` 0.5–1.4 (golden section on the efficiency of {@link propellerForThrust}).
- `propellerForThrust` (function): function propellerForThrust(propeller: BSeriesPropeller, thrust: number, advanceSpeed: number, density = 1025): PropellerOperatingPoint — The shaft speed at which a full-scale B-series propeller delivers `thrust` with inflow `advanceSpeed`: solves `K_T(J)/J² = T/(ρ·D²·V_A²)` for `J` by bisection on the falling branch.
- `propellerProfileDragIncrement` (function): function propellerProfileDragIncrement(section: ScrewBladeSection, roughness = 30e-6): number — ITTC-1978 profile drag change `ΔC_D` between the model-scale series and a full-scale propeller of the given roughness.
- `waterjetThrust` (function): function waterjetThrust(jet: Waterjet, power: number, speed: number, density = 1025): WaterjetPoint — Momentum theory of a waterjet: the pump lifts the swallowed flow from inlet to jet velocity, `η_p·P = ṁ·((1 + k_n)·V_j²/2 − (1 − k_i)·V_in²/2)`, and the thrust is the momentum it adds, `T = ṁ·(V_j − V_in)`, with `ṁ = ρ·A_n·V_j`. Solves the jet velocity for a shaft power by bisection.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/motorcycleManeuvers

- `BikeCourseSubject` (interface): interface BikeCourseSubject — The slice of a single-track sim the bike scenarios drive: a `VehicleDynamics` with a `lean` block or a {@link RiddenMotorcycle}.
- `BikeHandlingMetrics` (interface): interface BikeHandlingMetrics — Bike metrics comparable across any {@link BikeCourseSubject}.
- `BikeHandlingOptions` (interface): interface BikeHandlingOptions — Settings for {@link measureBikeHandling}.
- `BikeScenario` (type): type BikeScenario = "launch" | "brake" | "lean" | "laneChange" | "slalom" — One scenario of {@link measureBikeHandling}.
- `measureBikeHandling` (function): function measureBikeHandling(create: (speed: number) => BikeCourseSubject, options: BikeHandlingOptions): BikeHandlingMetrics — Drives fresh bikes from `create` through every bike scenario: a launch (0-100, 0-200 km/h), braking from 100 km/h, a full-steer lean test like `measureLean` (plus the lateral g the lean holds), an ISO 3888-1 double lane change with lanes sized for the bike, and a slalom. `create(speed)` may spawn rolling at `speed`; a subject that ignores it is launched from rest. Steering is a lean request (`steer · maxLean`) for every subject, so a game bike and the ridden reference motorcycle get the same inputs.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/motorcycleRider

- `MotorcycleRiderOptions` (interface): interface MotorcycleRiderOptions extends ReferenceMotorcycleOptions — Settings for {@link createRiddenMotorcycle}.
- `RiddenMotorcycle` (interface): interface RiddenMotorcycle — A reference motorcycle with a rider on it, driven like a game bike: `steer` asks for a lean (`steer · maxLean`, positive right), throttle and brake go to the bike's own launch, shift, wheelie and brake-limit logic.
- `RiddenMotorcycleState` (interface): interface RiddenMotorcycleState — Serializable state of a {@link RiddenMotorcycle}.
- `createRiddenMotorcycle` (function): function createRiddenMotorcycle(spec: ReferenceMotorcycleSpec, options: MotorcycleRiderOptions = {}): RiddenMotorcycle — Puts a steering-torque rider on a reference motorcycle; the bike only ever gets a bar torque, so countersteer, the lean response and its limits come from the multibody physics. The rider runs at 1 kHz: bar torque from lean error (proportional and integral) and lean rate, with the rate damping falling with speed as the bike's own lean damping rises (more of it at speed excites wobble). The structure is Sharp, Evangelou & Limebeer's (2004) steering controller; the gains are retuned for a quick, well-damped lean from 6 to 75 m/s. Steady turns, lane changes and slaloms are then scored through the same `AxisInput` a game bike takes.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/motorcycleTire

- `MotorcycleTireCoefficients` (interface): interface MotorcycleTireCoefficients — Coefficients of the motorcycle Magic Formula as identified by Sharp, Evangelou & Limebeer (2004), "Advances in the modelling of motorcycle dynamics", *Multibody System Dynamics* 12:251–283, §4 and Tables I–III, from the de Vries & Pacejka (1998) measurements. Camber enters the side force as its own arctangent term (the motorcycle form of Pacejka, *Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics*, ch. 11), so a leaned tyre carries camber thrust without sideslip. SI units, angles in rad.
- `MotorcycleTireInput` (interface): interface MotorcycleTireInput — Inputs to {@link motorcycleMagicFormula}, ISO-W axes (x forward, y left, z up).
- `MotorcycleTireOutput` (interface): interface MotorcycleTireOutput — Forces and moment from {@link motorcycleMagicFormula}, ISO-W axes, at the contact point.
- `SPORT_FRONT_120_70_ZR17` (const): const SPORT_FRONT_120_70_ZR17: Readonly<MotorcycleTireCoefficients> — Front 120/70 ZR17 sport tyre (Sharp, Evangelou & Limebeer 2004, Tables II–III middle rows; longitudinal shape from the 160/70 fit with pDx1 = 1.381, pDx2 = −0.04143, §4.5; relaxation §4.8).
- `SPORT_REAR_180_55_ZR17` (const): const SPORT_REAR_180_55_ZR17: Readonly<MotorcycleTireCoefficients> — Rear 180/55 ZR17 sport tyre (Sharp, Evangelou & Limebeer 2004, Tables II–III bottom rows; pDx1 = 1.355, pDx2 = −0.0603, §4.5; relaxation §4.8).
- `motorcycleMagicFormula` (function): function motorcycleMagicFormula(p: Readonly<MotorcycleTireCoefficients>, input: MotorcycleTireInput, v?: number): MotorcycleTireOutput — The steady-state motorcycle Magic Formula of Sharp, Evangelou & Limebeer (2004), Eqs. (1)–(31): pure and combined longitudinal and side slip with camber thrust as its own term, load-dependent stiffnesses, and an aligning moment from pneumatic trail on the zero-camber side force plus a camber twisting moment (residual torque Dr). The overturning moment is not here: it comes from the contact point moving across the tyre's round crown, which the vehicle's contact geometry carries. Sign convention: ISO-W, so the published formula (positive force for positive slip and camber) is mirrored. The published fit has one shift (rBy3) that would make left and right differ; it is applied to |β| so the tyre stays symmetric as the paper intends.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/oceanWaves

- `IrregularSeaOptions` (interface): interface IrregularSeaOptions — How to sample a spectrum into components.
- `OceanSea` (interface): interface OceanSea — A sea as a sum of regular components on deep water, plain data.
- `SeaSpectrum` (interface): interface SeaSpectrum — A sea spectrum by its significant height and peak period; `peakEnhancement` 1 is Pierson–Moskowitz, 3.3 the mean JONSWAP sea.
- `WaveComponent` (interface): interface WaveComponent — One regular wave component: `η = a·cos(k(x cos θ + y sin θ) − ωt + φ)`.
- `irregularSea` (function): function irregularSea(spectrum: SeaSpectrum, options: IrregularSeaOptions): OceanSea — Samples a spectrum into a deterministic irregular sea: frequencies in equal bands from 0.5ωp to 4ωp, each jittered within its band so the record does not repeat, amplitudes `√(2·S(ω)·Δω)`, random phases, and with `spreading` each component given a heading drawn from `cos^(2s)` about the mean.
- `regularSea` (function): function regularSea(amplitude: number, period: number, direction = 0, phase = 0, density = SEA_WATER_DENSITY, gravity = MARINE_GRAVITY): OceanSea — A single regular wave as an {@link OceanSea}: amplitude, m, period, s, travelling toward `direction`.
- `seaElevation` (function): function seaElevation(sea: OceanSea, x: number, y: number, time: number): number — Surface elevation, m, at a point and time.
- `seaWaterAt` (function): function seaWaterAt(sea: OceanSea, time: number): HullWater — The sea at one instant as {@link HullWater} for the hull integrator: submergence below the local surface and the incident-wave (Froude–Krylov) pressure, hydrostatic plus each component's dynamic pressure decaying as `e^(k·z')` with Wheeler stretching `z' = z − η`, so the pressure is zero on the moving surface. Integrating it over the wetted hull gives buoyancy and the nonlinear Froude–Krylov wave force together.
- `spectralMoment` (function): function spectralMoment(spectrum: SeaSpectrum, order: number, steps = 4000): number — Spectral moment `m_n = ∫ωⁿ·S(ω) dω`, by Simpson's rule from 0.2ωp to 6ωp.
- `waveSpectrum` (function): function waveSpectrum(spectrum: SeaSpectrum, omega: number): number — Spectral density `S(ω)`, m²·s, of a Pierson–Moskowitz (`γ = 1`) or JONSWAP sea in the DNV-RP-C205 form: `S_PM = (5/16)·Hs²·ωp⁴·ω⁻⁵·exp(−1.25(ωp/ω)⁴)`, times `(1 − 0.287 ln γ)·γ^exp(−(ω−ωp)²/(2σ²ωp²))` with `σ` 0.07 below the peak and 0.09 above it.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/planingHull

- `NACA_TN2876_MODEL` (const): const NACA_TN2876_MODEL: { readonly beam: number; readonly deadrise: number; readonly density: number; readonly viscosity: number; } — Model 276's beam, m, and its tank water.
- `NACA_TN2876_RUNS` (const): const NACA_TN2876_RUNS: readonly PrismaticPlaningRun[] — Langley tank model 276 (NACA TN 2876, Table I, public domain): a 20° deadrise prismatic surface, 4 in beam, in fresh water at 63.4 lb/ft³ and ν = 10.55·10⁻⁶ ft²/s. Rows with wetted chines, read from the table.
- `PlaningEquilibrium` (interface): interface PlaningEquilibrium extends PlaningState — Planing equilibrium and its stability margin.
- `PlaningFluid` (interface): interface PlaningFluid — Fluid for a planing calculation.
- `PlaningHull` (interface): interface PlaningHull — A prismatic planing hull for Savitsky's method, SI units.
- `PlaningState` (interface): interface PlaningState — A planing hull's running state at one speed and trim.
- `PrismaticPlaningRun` (interface): interface PrismaticPlaningRun — One run of a prismatic planing surface from NACA TN 2876 (Chambliss and Boyd, 1953), 20° deadrise, 4 in beam.
- `planingAtTrim` (function): function planingAtTrim(hull: PlaningHull, speed: number, trim: number, fluid: PlaningFluid = {}): PlaningState — Savitsky's planing equations at a given trim: wetted length from the lift fit, mean bottom velocity, Schoenherr friction, the centre of pressure `l_p/(λb) = 0.75 − 1/(5.21·C_V²/λ² + 2.39)`, and the force and moment balance with the thrust line.
- `planingEquilibrium` (function): function planingEquilibrium(hull: PlaningHull, speed: number, fluid: PlaningFluid = {}): PlaningEquilibrium — The trim at which a planing hull runs: the trim where the bottom pressure, friction and thrust leave no pitching moment about the centre of gravity (Savitsky's general equilibrium), with its resistance and porpoising margin.
- `savitskyLiftCoefficient` (function): function savitskyLiftCoefficient(trimDeg: number, meanWettedLengthRatio: number, speedCoefficient: number, deadriseDeg: number): number — Savitsky's lift coefficient of a prismatic planing surface, `C_Lβ = C_L0 − 0.0065·β·C_L0^0.6` with `C_L0 = τ^1.1·(0.012·λ^0.5 + 0.0055·λ^2.5/C_V²)` (τ and β in degrees, as the fit is written).
- `savitskyPorpoisingTrim` (function): function savitskyPorpoisingTrim(liftCoefficient: number, deadrise: number): number — Savitsky's (1964) porpoising stability limit: the trim above which a planing hull porpoises, against `√(C_Lβ/2)`, for deadrise 0°, 10° and 20° (Day and Haag's tests), interpolated quadratically in deadrise. The curves are the cubic fits of the chart published with OpenPlaning (Castro-Feliciano, MIT); valid for `0.13 ≤ √(C_Lβ/2) ≤ 0.3`, deadrise 0–20°.
- `savitskyWettedLength` (function): function savitskyWettedLength(trimDeg: number, liftCoefficient: number, speedCoefficient: number, deadriseDeg: number): number — The mean wetted length–beam ratio `λ` at which the surface carries `liftCoefficient` (bisection on Savitsky's lift).

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/referenceMotorcycle

- `MotorcycleControls` (interface): interface MotorcycleControls — Controls for one {@link ReferenceMotorcycle.step}.
- `MotorcycleModes` (interface): interface MotorcycleModes — Out-of-plane and in-plane straight-running eigenvalues of a reference motorcycle, 1/s.
- `MotorcyclePowertrain` (interface): interface MotorcyclePowertrain — Engine, primary drive, gearbox and chain.

Points and inertias are as tabulated (SAE side view, z down).

- `motorcycleStraightRunningModes` (function): function motorcycleStraightRunningModes(spec: ReferenceMotorcycleSpec, speed: number): MotorcycleModes — Straight-running stability of a {@link ReferenceMotorcycleSpec} at `speed` (Sharp, Evangelou & Limebeer 2004, section 6): settle the bike at speed under their speed controller, take the Jacobian of the full nonlinear plant by central differences, and split it into its out-of-plane and in-plane blocks. Rigid-body zero roots (position, heading, wheel angles) are dropped.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/rigidBodyTree

- `RigidBodyDefinition` (interface): interface RigidBodyDefinition — One rigid body of a {@link RigidBodyTree}. Every frame is parallel to the world in the reference pose (all joint coordinates zero, root unrotated), so a body is placed by world points in that pose.
- `RigidBodyTree` (interface): interface RigidBodyTree — The positions of a tree: root position (3, world) and unit quaternion `[w, x, y, z]` (body to world), then one coordinate per non-root joint. Velocities: root angular then linear velocity of the root origin, both in root axes (6), then one rate per non-root joint.
- `RigidBodyTreeState` (interface): interface RigidBodyTreeState — A {@link RigidBodyTree}'s state: coordinates from the last update and the forces applied since the last clear.
- `RigidJoint` (type): type RigidJoint = | { kind: "free" } /** Rotation about `axis` (unit, parent axes) through the body's origin. */ | { kind: "revolute"; axis: Vec3 } /** Translation along `axis` (unit, parent axes). */ | { kind: "prismatic"; axis: Vec3 } — How a body moves relative to its parent.
- `createRigidBodyTree` (function): function createRigidBodyTree(definitions: readonly RigidBodyDefinition[]): RigidBodyTree — Creates a {@link RigidBodyTree}: a tree of rigid bodies on free, revolute and prismatic joints with exact dynamics in spatial-vector form (Featherstone, *Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms*, 2008): the composite-rigid-body algorithm for the mass matrix and the recursive Newton–Euler algorithm for the velocity-product and applied forces. No small-angle or decoupling approximations; gyroscopic coupling of every spinning body is included.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/rungeKutta

- `RungeKutta4` (interface): interface RungeKutta4 — A reusable classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta stepper over a fixed-size state vector.
- `createRungeKutta4` (function): function createRungeKutta4(size: number): RungeKutta4 — Creates a {@link RungeKutta4} for states of `size` entries; its scratch buffers are allocated once, so a step allocates nothing.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/seakeepingHull

- `SeakeepingHull` (interface): interface SeakeepingHull — A rigid hull for time-domain seakeeping, in hull axes (x forward from the aft end, y to port, z up from the keel). Buoyancy and the Froude–Krylov wave force come from integrating the incident sea's pressure over the instantaneous wetted mesh; radiation is constant added mass and damping about G; each station adds a diffraction force by the strip-theory diffraction force (its section's diffraction integral at the reference frequency, applied to every wave component) and a momentum slamming force when it re-enters the water.
- `SeakeepingHullOptions` (interface): interface SeakeepingHullOptions — Options for {@link seakeepingHullFromStrip}.
- `SeakeepingState` (interface): interface SeakeepingState — Body state: G in earth axes (z up from still water), roll/pitch/yaw, and body velocities `[u, v, w, p, q, r]` at G.
- `SeakeepingStation` (interface): interface SeakeepingStation — One strip of the hull for the station forces.
- `SurgeForce` (type): type SurgeForce = (state: SeakeepingState) => number — External surge force along the body x axis, N, e.g. a propeller holding speed against resistance.
- `restingSeakeepingState` (function): function restingSeakeepingState(hull: SeakeepingHull): SeakeepingState — The hull floating at rest in still water: G above the origin at its equilibrium height, heel and trim.
- `seakeepingHullFromStrip` (function): function seakeepingHullFromStrip(hull: StripHull, options: SeakeepingHullOptions = {}): SeakeepingHull — Builds a {@link SeakeepingHull} from a strip-theory hull: mesh from its offsets, heave–pitch added mass and damping from strip theory at the reference frequency, surge added mass from Lamb's spheroid, sway and yaw from flat-plate strips (`ρπT²/2`), roll as shares of the dry inertia and of critical damping, and per-station diffraction and high-frequency slamming tables from the 2-D sections.
- `stepSeakeeping` (function): function stepSeakeeping(hull: SeakeepingHull, sea: OceanSea, state: SeakeepingState, dt: number, surge?: SurgeForce): SeakeepingState — Advances a hull in a sea by `dt` with fourth-order Runge–Kutta, in place. Forces: weight; buoyancy and Froude–Krylov from the sea pressure over the wetted mesh; constant added mass and damping; per-station diffraction `ρω²·Re(A·D·e^(iθ))` from each section's diffraction integral; momentum slamming `−(dm∞/dh)·ḣ²` on a station whose immersion `h` is rising; and an optional surge force.

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/sectionHydrodynamics

- `HalfSection` (type): type HalfSection = readonly (readonly [number, number])[] — Half a symmetric ship section below the waterline: points from the keel on the centreline to the waterline, as `[half-breadth, depth]` pairs with depth ≤ 0 (the waterline at 0).
- `SectionHeave` (interface): interface SectionHeave — Heave added mass, kg/m, and radiation damping, N·s/m², of a section at one frequency, with what the strip method needs.
- `lewisSection` (function): function lewisSection(halfBreadth: number, draft: number, areaCoefficient: number, points = 41): { section: HalfSection; a1: number; a3: number; scale: number } — A Lewis-form half-section `x = M((1 + a1) sin θ − a3 sin 3θ)`, `y = −M((1 − a1) cos θ + a3 cos 3θ)` from the keel (`θ = 0`) to the waterline (`θ = π/2`), fitted to a half-breadth, draft and section area coefficient.
- `sectionHeave` (function): function sectionHeave(section: HalfSection, frequency: number, density = 1025, gravity = 9.80665, panels = 24): SectionHeave — Heave added mass and damping of a symmetric section by Frank's close-fit source method: pulsating sources of constant strength on straight panels (mirrored to port) with the deep-water free-surface Green's function, the body condition met at panel midpoints. `frequency` `Infinity` uses the high-frequency limit (`φ = 0` on the surface).

## @jgengine/core/physics/reference/shipManoeuvring

Fresh tank water.
- `KVLCC2_L7_PUBLISHED` (const): const KVLCC2_L7_PUBLISHED: { readonly turning: readonly [{ readonly rudder: 35; readonly advance: { readonly calculated: 3.31; readonly measured: 3.25; }; readonly tacticalDiameter: { readonly calculated: 3.36; readonly measured: 3.34; }; }, { readonly rudder: -35; readonly advance: { readonly calcu… — Published turning and zig-zag results for the KVLCC2 L7 model: the MMG calculation and MARIN's free-running test (Yasukawa & Yoshimura 2015, Tables 4 and 5). Advance and tactical diameter are over `L`; overshoots in degrees.
- `KVLCC2_L7_SPEED` (const): const KVLCC2_L7_SPEED: number — The approach speed of the KVLCC2 simulations, m/s at L7 scale (15.5 kn full scale).

- `MmgHullDerivatives` (interface): interface MmgHullDerivatives — Hull force derivatives of the MMG standard method, non-dimensionalised by ½ρ·L·d·U² (forces) and ½ρ·L²·d·U² (moment).
- `MmgPropeller` (interface): interface MmgPropeller — Propeller of an MMG ship: open-water thrust `KT = k0 + k1·J + k2·J²` and its wake and thrust deduction.
- `MmgRudder` (interface): interface MmgRudder — Rudder of an MMG ship and its interaction with hull and propeller.
